geographic_coverage: West Bank including East Jerusalem; Area C/Jordan Valley emphasis
sources.methodology: UNICEF operational and partner monitoring
sources.limitations: Webpage publication metadata and stated reporting period are inconsistent; humanitarian estimates rather than climate-specific research. (UNICEF9)

sources.title: *Sudan's National Adaptation Plan*
sources.organization: Government of Sudan / HCENR, hosted by UNFCCC
geographic_coverage: National; state components for all 18 states
sources.methodology: State consultation, vulnerability assessment, station data, CMIP5 GCMs and BCSD downscaling
sources.limitations: Pre-war; CMIP5; six-station baseline; not an evaluation. (UNFCCC1)

sources.title: *Sudan Updated First NDC*
sources.methodology: Government synthesis of vulnerability, adaptation priorities and implementation needs
sources.limitations: Predates current war; some national trend statements are not readily reconcilable with the NAP station record; programme/self-report evidence. (UNFCCC2)

sources.title: *Sudan's NAP: Key adaptation priorities & financial needs*
sources.methodology: Policy presentation summarizing priorities, finance and support needs
sources.limitations: Not an independent implementation review; primarily restates national plans and financing needs. (UNFCCC6)

sources.title: *Climate-Fragility Risk Brief: Sudan*
sources.methodology: Literature and expert synthesis
sources.limitations: Pre-war political/security setting; secondary synthesis rather than causal evaluation. (Climate-Diplomacy7)

sources.title: *Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: Sudan*
sources.methodology: Research synthesis and policy analysis
sources.limitations: Predates April 2023 war; some institutional recommendations refer to arrangements that later changed. (NUPI8)

sources.title: *How does climate exacerbate root causes of conflict in Sudan? Climate Security Pathway Analysis*
geographic_coverage: Sudan; emphasis on Darfur, Kordofan, Blue Nile, Kassala
sources.methodology: Systematic literature interpretation plus stakeholder workshop
sources.limitations: Completed around onset of current war; mechanisms include workshop judgement and older studies; not causal impact evaluation. (CGSpace9)

sources.title: *Climate Change, Conflicts and Food Security in North Darfur State, Sudan: Risks and Implications*
sources.methodology: Al Fashir station data; RAI; crop-yield analysis; internet-based IDP household questionnaire
sources.limitations: Single-state study; only Al Fashir station used for drought analysis; internet survey during conflict/siege; no national inference warranted. (CMI - Chr. Michelsen Institute10)

sources.title: *Famine Review Committee: Sudan, October 2025 - Conclusions and Recommendations*
geographic_coverage: El Fasher, Kadugli, Dilling, Western Nuba Mountains and wider risk areas
sources.methodology: FRC review, multiple outcome datasets, extrapolation, key informants and expert judgement under access constraints
sources.limitations: Severe access/data constraints; FRC explicitly declined longer projection in some areas because conflict was too volatile. (IPCinfo5)

sources.title: *Three years on, war-weary Sudanese remain on the move*
sources.methodology: UNHCR operational displacement monitoring / briefing
sources.limitations: Fast-changing operational figures; not a climate-attribution source. (UNHCR3)

sources.title: *Terminal Evaluation Report: Climate Risk Finance for Sustainable and Climate Resilient Rainfed Farming and Pastoral Systems, Sudan*
geographic_coverage: Six states: River Nile, North Kordofan, Gedarif, South Darfur, Kassala, White Nile
sources.methodology: UNDP/GEF evaluation criteria; documents, interviews and limited field evidence
sources.limitations: Pre-war; commissioned within UNDP/GEF evaluation system; some respondents/financial records unavailable; COVID reduced field sample. (UNDP IEO Evaluation Resource Center11)

sources.title: *Environmental degradation and conflict in Darfur: implications for peace and recovery*
sources.organization: Humanitarian Practice Network / ODI; author Brendan Bromwich, UNEP
sources.methodology: Field-informed specialist synthesis
sources.limitations: Foundational but old; environmental scarcity is broader than anthropogenic climate change; Darfur-specific. (Humanitarian Practice Network12)

sources.title: *Sudan - Enhancing Community Resilience Project (P181490), Additional Financing 3 Project Paper*
geographic_coverage: Kassala, Northern, River Nile and other project locations
sources.methodology: Project monitoring, implementation ratings, risk analysis and results framework
sources.limitations: Administrative project evidence, not independent impact evaluation; targets are not achieved outcomes. (World Bank13)

sources.title: *New FAO-WFP report warns worsening hunger puts 13 hotspots at significant risk*
geographic_coverage: National with North/South Darfur and South Kordofan hotspots
sources.temporal_coverage: Jun-Nov 2026; some Sudan projections to Jan 2027
sources.methodology: GNAFC consensus early warning using field/technical teams and conflict, economic and natural-hazard analysts
sources.limitations: Forward-looking; not designed to isolate climate effects from conflict; report PDF access was blocked by the browser, but publication/release content was accessible. (World Food Programme14)

sources.title: *Risk of Famine persists as nearly 19.5 million people face acute food insecurity in Sudan*
sources.methodology: IPC and UN operational evidence
sources.limitations: Humanitarian operational source; rapidly changing; no climate attribution. (World Food Programme15)

sources.title: *Climate Risk Profile Somalia*
sources.organization: Weathering Risk / Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK)
sources.methodology: AGRICA methodology; multi-model RCP2.6/RCP6.0 projections plus sector synthesis
sources.limitations: Socioeconomic change not included in climate models; precipitation, river flooding, crop and ecosystem projections have substantial uncertainty; not a current humanitarian assessment.

sources.title: *Somalia's Third Generation Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0)*
sources.organization: Somalia; reproduced by FAO/FAOLEX through InforMEA
sources.methodology: Policy commitments and planned measures
sources.limitations: Policy intent, not evaluated implementation; accessible page is a UN/FAOLEX reproduction rather than the official UNFCCC PDF. (InforMEA)

sources.title: *Climate-related security risks and peacebuilding in Somalia*
sources.methodology: Single-case plausibility probe; qualitative process tracing; literature plus 27 interviews and expert consultations
sources.limitations: Older; UNSOM-focused; explicitly limited in generalizability and does not establish a national causal coefficient. (SIPRI)

sources.title: *Environmental Peacemaking in Somalia: Integrated Climate and Conflict Analysis of the Newly Liberated Areas of Hirshabelle and Galmudug*
geographic_coverage: Newly Liberated Areas, Hirshabelle and Galmudug
sources.methodology: Literature/regulatory review, expert consultations and Mogadishu stakeholder workshop
sources.limitations: Localized case; consultation/synthesis evidence rather than causal identification; must not be generalized nationally.

sources.title: *SWALIM Quarterly Newsletter: Jan-March 2026*
sources.organization: FAO Somalia Water and Land Information Management
sources.methodology: Combined Drought Index, hydrometeorological monitoring, satellite/DEM analysis, field observers and community feedback
sources.limitations: Operational quarterly monitoring, not climate attribution or long-term projection.

sources.title: *FAO GIEWS Country Brief: Somalia*
geographic_coverage: National with market and livelihood-zone examples
sources.methodology: Cereal balance, food-price monitoring, Earth observation and IPC evidence
sources.limitations: Snapshot; national totals coexist with geographically specific examples; does not independently identify causal conflict effects. (FAOHome)

sources.title: *Somalia IPC Acute Food Insecurity and Acute Malnutrition Analysis - Updated Projection April-June 2026*
sources.organization: Somalia IPC Technical Working Group / IPC partners
sources.methodology: IPC protocols; government, FAO/FSNAU, WFP, UNICEF, WHO, FEWS NET, REACH and cluster inputs
sources.limitations: Projection conditional on evolving rainfall, prices, assistance and conflict; some areas have scarce evidence due to limited/no humanitarian access.

sources.title: *UNHCR Somalia PSMN 2026 Q2 Report*
sources.methodology: Recorded displacement monitoring
sources.limitations: Web publication page gives high-level result but limited methodology detail; percentage refers to recorded displacement, not population-wide causal attribution. (UNHCR Data Portal)

sources.title: *Support for Strengthening Climate Change Adaptation Planning for the Federal Republic of Somalia*
sources.methodology: Programme diagnostics, institutional reviews and reported outputs
sources.limitations: Mostly programme theory/output reporting; page still says “Under Implementation” despite listed 2020-24 dates; effectiveness not independently evaluated here. (UNDP Climate Change Adaptation)

sources.title: *The World Bank Group in the Federal Republic of Somalia, Fiscal Years 2013-23: Country Program Evaluation*
sources.methodology: Project evidence, secondary datasets, literature review, 43 evaluative reports from 18 partners and interviews
sources.limitations: Evaluates World Bank Group engagement rather than the full Somali institutional/humanitarian system; some outcome evidence originates in project reporting.

sources.title: *Evaluation of Somalia WFP Country Strategic Plan 2022-2025*
sources.methodology: Independent evaluation conducted Jun 2024-Mar 2025
sources.limitations: WFP-specific; effectiveness attribution occurs in a highly dynamic multi-actor crisis; resilience and capacity-strengthening results constrained by funding/logistics. (World Food Programme)

sources.title: *Joint Communiqué - Activation of the National Preparedness Plan for Food and Nutrition Security Crises*
sources.organization: Federal Government of Somalia and partners / World Bank host
sources.methodology: Administrative record and response framework
sources.limitations: Evidence of activation, coordination and intended mechanisms - not evidence that the plan subsequently reduced losses. (World Bank)

sources.title: *UNDP Somalia Annual Report 2025*
sources.methodology: UNDP programme monitoring/reporting
sources.limitations: Self-reported outputs/results; no counterfactual; reported peacebuilding and resilience achievements should not be interpreted as independently demonstrated causal effects. (UNDP)

sources.title: Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: South Sudan (2025)
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate, peace, and security conditions synthesized for the 2025 fact sheet.
sources.methodology: SIPRI and partner authors synthesize climate trends, conflict dynamics, institutional context, and policy implications into a country fact sheet with recommended actions.
sources.limitations: The official catalogue states April 2025 without a day, so publication_date preserves month precision; the concise synthesis does not replace review of its underlying sources.

sources.title: Climate Security Risks in South Sudan: An Information Brief (2025)
sources.temporal_coverage: Current climate-security risks and response priorities as assessed in 2025.
sources.methodology: The information brief was jointly developed by UNDP, UNMISS, and the UN Resident Coordinator's Office to synthesize climate-related security risks and strategic interventions for South Sudan.
sources.limitations: This is a short strategic brief rather than a reproducible dataset; its country-level framing can obscure variation among states, livelihood systems, and conflict settings.

sources.title: Joining Forces for a Conflict-Sensitive Flood Response in South Sudan (2025)
geographic_coverage: South Sudan (national and selected flood-affected subnational locations)
sources.temporal_coverage: Lessons from the 2024 flood response and preparedness priorities for the 2025 flood season.
sources.methodology: The article distils a UN Community of Practice discussion and operational examples from UNMISS, OCHA, the UN Country Team, national authorities, and subnational flood taskforces.
sources.limitations: The source is a practice-oriented UN news account, not an independent evaluation; selected operational examples cannot establish how consistently conflict sensitivity was applied nationwide.

sources.title: South Sudan Country Climate and Development Report (2026)
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate and development baselines with forward-looking climate and development analysis published in 2026.
sources.methodology: The World Bank country diagnostic integrates climate information with macroeconomic, sectoral, institutional, and development analysis to identify climate-resilient development priorities.
sources.limitations: A national diagnostic may mask subnational differences and depends on model assumptions and uneven underlying data availability; this record does not independently reproduce or verify those inputs.

sources.title: First National Adaptation Plan for Climate Change Republic of South Sudan
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of South Sudan and United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
sources.methodology: The national planning document organizes adaptation around three resilience pillars and nine priority sectors to guide policy and implementation from national to community level.
sources.limitations: The plan records government priorities and intended actions rather than evaluated adaptation outcomes; implementation progress after its 2021-2025 planning horizon requires separate evidence.

sources.title: South Sudan Second Nationally Determined Contribution
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of South Sudan and United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate commitments and priorities submitted in 2021, principally oriented to 2030.
sources.methodology: The government submission updates the national greenhouse-gas inventory and sets sectoral mitigation, adaptation, and implementation commitments under the Paris Agreement.
sources.limitations: The date recorded is the UNFCCC submission date, 2021-09-21, not the portal file-publication timestamp; an NDC states commitments and assumptions rather than demonstrating achieved results.

sources.title: South Sudan Flood Damage and Needs Assessment Study (2021)
sources.organization: International Organization for Migration (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM)
geographic_coverage: Three flood-affected payams in South Sudan
sources.temporal_coverage: Impacts of the June-December 2020 floods, with fieldwork from 2021-08-31 to 2021-10-14.
sources.methodology: IOM field-validated the 2020 flood assessment using two quantitative tools, focus-group discussions, and key-informant interviews, consulting more than 1,131 people across three payams.
sources.limitations: The official page states publication year 2021 without an exact month or day, so publication_date preserves year precision; purposive coverage of three payams is not nationally representative.

sources.title: South Sudan UN Common Country Analysis (CCA)
sources.organization: United Nations Resident Coordinator's Office in South Sudan
sources.temporal_coverage: Multisector country context through late 2021, published on the UN portal in 2022.
sources.methodology: The UN country analysis synthesizes political, conflict, humanitarian, socioeconomic, environmental, and institutional evidence to identify constraints to sustainable development.
sources.limitations: The portal publication date, 2022-06-27, is used consistently, while the downloadable document is versioned 2021-12-24; underlying indicators have different reference periods and may have since changed.

sources.title: INFORM South Sudan Country Risk Profile (2021)
sources.temporal_coverage: INFORM 2021 risk profile, including trend displays for 2017-2021.
sources.methodology: INFORM combines standardized indicators of hazard and exposure, vulnerability, and lack of coping capacity into a composite country risk index with peer and trend comparisons.
sources.limitations: The profile identifies version 2021 rather than a dated publication, so publication_date records the stated version year; composite national scores compress indicator uncertainty and subnational disparities.

sources.title: Climate change deepens gender inequality and violence in South Sudan: UNFPA study highlights urgent need for action
sources.organization: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), Sudd Institute, and South Sudan National Bureau of Statistics
sources.temporal_coverage: Study findings released in 2025 on current climate-related gender and violence risks.
sources.methodology: The UN story summarizes a vulnerability study conducted by UNFPA with the Sudd Institute and National Bureau of Statistics in three high-exposure locations, with findings validated in a stakeholder workshop.
sources.limitations: This is a summary rather than the full study methodology; purposive selection of three highly exposed locations and condensed reporting limit national generalization.

sources.title: South Sudan Event Tracking Report 73: Flood Displacements (1-31 December 2024)
sources.organization: International Organization for Migration (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM)
sources.temporal_coverage: Flood-related displacement events recorded from 2024-12-01 to 2024-12-31.
sources.methodology: IOM DTM enumerators used event tracking to document disaster-related displacement during December 2024 and record affected people's reported priority needs.
sources.limitations: Event tracking is a rapid, period-specific account rather than a complete displacement stock; the 2025-02-10 publication date follows the December 2024 observation period.

sources.title: South Sudan Climatology (ERA5)
sources.organization: World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal
sources.temporal_coverage: ERA5 climatology for 1991-2020 and historical daily data for 1950-2023.
sources.methodology: The World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal presents ERA5 reanalysis-derived South Sudan climatology for 1991-2020 and historical daily data for 1950-2023 at 0.25-degree resolution.
sources.limitations: ERA5 is model-based reanalysis rather than direct station observation, and national summaries can mask subnational variation. This living page can change and has no fixed publication date; publication_date remains null with basis not-stated.

sources.title: South Sudan - Trends & Variability (CMIP6)
sources.organization: World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal
geographic_coverage: South Sudan (national aggregation with mapped subnational detail)
sources.temporal_coverage: CMIP6 reference period 1995-2014 and scenario projections through 2100.
sources.methodology: CMIP6 multi-model ensemble trends, variability, and emergence from historical variability at 0.25-degree resolution across SSPs.
sources.limitations: The accessible page exposed direction, scenario, horizon, and uncertainty but not stable numeric p10, p50, and p90 exports; national aggregation masks local variation.

sources.title: Uplifting Vulnerable South Sudanese Households through Safety Net Assistance
geographic_coverage: Ten project counties in South Sudan
sources.temporal_coverage: South Sudan Safety Net Project implementation and reported results from 2020 to 2023.
sources.methodology: Official results brief using delivery records, monitoring indicators, and selected beneficiary outcome measures.
sources.limitations: Not an independent impact evaluation; selected beneficiaries in ten counties do not establish national or climate-attributable effects.

sources.title: Building community resilience from the ground up in South Sudan
geographic_coverage: Twenty selected counties in South Sudan
sources.temporal_coverage: ECRP implementation from 2020 to 2024 and functionality reporting as of 2024.
sources.methodology: Official feature summarizing project monitoring, infrastructure functionality, flood-protection reach, and community-institution outputs.
sources.limitations: Not an independent evaluation; selected counties, third-party implementation, and output indicators limit generalization and causal interpretation.

sources.title: Narrow Path to Recovery: Finding a Climate-Smart Pathway and Stabilizing South Sudan's Economy
sources.temporal_coverage: Current flood and development conditions summarized from the 2026 CCDR and Public Finance Review.
sources.methodology: Official press release summarizing selected CCDR and Public Finance Review findings.
sources.limitations: Does not expose underlying spatial analysis, model ranges, or source tables and supports only the stated national headline finding.

sources.title: *Background analysis of climate risks to Syria's electricity and urban water sectors* (ODI: Think change1)
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical trends to reconstruction scenarios through 2045+
sources.methodology: New climate-trend analysis, population scenarios, water systems and electricity-demand analysis
sources.limitations: Reconstruction-oriented; population scenarios are planning tools rather than forecasts; substantial data gaps acknowledged.

sources.title: *Human-induced climate change compounded by socio-economic water stressors increased severity of drought in Syria, Iraq and Iran* (World Weather Attribution7)
geographic_coverage: Euphrates-Tigris basin including large parts of Syria and Iraq; Iran separately
sources.methodology: 36-month SPEI; observations and climate models using published peer-reviewed attribution methods
sources.limitations: Regional basin result cannot be generalized to every Syrian locality; rapid attribution study, not a conflict-causality study.

sources.title: *Syrian Arab Republic Nationally Determined Contribution. NDC1* (Climate Laws8)
sources.organization: Syrian Arab Republic / UNFCCC; mirror by Climate Change Laws of the World
sources.methodology: Government NDC; repository metadata and topic extraction
sources.limitations: Official UNFCCC primary PDF could not be fetched because of a redirect loop; repository topic extraction is explicitly beta. Detailed primary-text locator LOCATOR NOT VERIFIED.

sources.title: *FAO GIEWS Country Brief - Syrian Arab Republic* (FAOHome2)
sources.methodology: Crop, rainfall, input, import and food-security monitoring
sources.limitations: Current operational synthesis rather than causal impact evaluation; subnational detail uneven.

sources.title: *UNHCR Syria Operational Update - March 2026* (UNHCR Data Portal3)
sources.methodology: Operational displacement, return and assistance data
sources.limitations: Rapidly changing population movements; estimates depend on operational data systems.

sources.title: *Syria at a turning point: A new chapter for children - Annual Report 2025* (UNICEF9)
geographic_coverage: All 14 governorates, with selected subnational examples
sources.methodology: Programme monitoring and sectoral operational statistics
sources.limitations: UNICEF self-report; beneficiary/reach numbers are outputs unless an evaluation establishes outcomes.

sources.title: *The Syrian Conflict: Physical Damage and Reconstruction Assessment (2011-2024)* (World Bank4)
sources.methodology: Predominantly remote data and asset/exposure modelling
sources.limitations: Does not measure full human/economic impacts or service-restoration needs; remote-data uncertainty; sectoral disaggregation limited.

sources.title: *Syria Common Country Analysis: 2024 Update* (UN Syria10)
sources.methodology: Synthesis of UN, government and external evidence
sources.limitations: Some environmental material derives from older sources; broad synthesis claims need source-level checking before causal use.

sources.title: Kelley et al., *Climate change in the Fertile Crescent and implications of the recent Syrian drought* (Columbia OCP5)
sources.temporal_coverage: Pre-2011 drought and longer climatic record
sources.methodology: Observations, CMIP5 simulations and secondary social evidence
sources.limitations: Historical and heavily contested causal interpretation; migration/conflict evidence relies partly on secondary sources.

sources.title: Selby et al., *Climate change and the Syrian civil war revisited* (Cambridge Repository11)
sources.methodology: Systematic interrogation of climate, migration and conflict evidence
sources.limitations: Historical critique rather than evidence about current Climate-FCV mechanisms; cannot prove a zero climate effect.

sources.title: Eklund et al., *Societal drought vulnerability and the Syrian climate-conflict nexus are better explained by agriculture than meteorology* (Nature12)
sources.methodology: Satellite-derived cropland and climate data
sources.limitations: Cropland is not equivalent to household livelihood, migration or political behaviour; historical focus.

sources.title: *Making Adaptation Work: Addressing the compounding impacts of climate change, environmental degradation and conflict in the Near and Middle East* (ICRC6)
geographic_coverage: Near/Middle East; examples from Syria, Iraq, Yemen
sources.methodology: Desk review and country examples
sources.limitations: Many findings are regional rather than Syria-specific; not an impact evaluation.

sources.title: *Syrian Arab Republic Interim Country Strategic Plan Evaluation 2018-25* (World Food Programme13)
sources.methodology: Theory-based mixed-methods evaluation
sources.limitations: Page publication date conflicts with stated evaluation period; downloaded evaluation PDF was not fetchable in this session; findings on publication page were verified. Not a climate-specific impact evaluation.

sources.title: *JP Syria 2.0 Annual Programme Narrative Progress Report 2025* (MPTF Gateway14)
sources.organization: UN Joint Programme: FAO, UNDP, UNFPA, UN-Habitat, UNICEF, WFP
sources.methodology: Implementing-agency monitoring, lessons and reported outputs
sources.limitations: Self-reported programme evidence, geographically narrow; lessons should not be treated as independently demonstrated outcomes.

sources.title: *Increasing the climate change resilience of communities in Eastern Ghouta...* (Adaptation Fund15)
sources.methodology: Project design, administrative and performance documentation
sources.limitations: Project objectives and budgets are intended mechanisms, not proof of resilience outcomes; local evidence only.

sources.title: *Approval of request for no-cost extension of project completion date: UN-Habitat (Syria)* (Adaptation Fund16)
sources.methodology: Secretariat review of documented implementation delays
sources.limitations: Establishes implementation delay and reported causes, not the magnitude of resulting resilience loss.

sources.title: *Syria - Country Overview* (World Bank17)
sources.methodology: World Bank synthesis and high-frequency indicators
sources.limitations: Page explicitly notes limited and unevenly reliable official data; current estimates remain uncertain.

sources.title: Ukraine: Building Climate Resilience in Agriculture and Forestry
sources.temporal_coverage: Observations mainly from the 1980s onward and RCP projections through 2100.
sources.methodology: Climate-model ensemble across approximately 7,400 grid points with sector and distributional modelling.
sources.limitations: Prepared before the full-scale invasion, uses older RCPs, and has no war-adjusted exposure baseline.

sources.title: Ukraine's Climate Change Adaptation Communication to UNFCCC
sources.organization: Government of Ukraine and United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, national and sectoral with some subnational references
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical evidence and policy status mainly through 2023-2024, with projections to 2100.
sources.methodology: Official synthesis of climate risks, policy arrangements, barriers, needs, and sector priorities.
sources.limitations: Mostly repackages pre-invasion assessments and has limited post-2022 quantitative risk updating.

sources.title: Ukraine Fifth Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment: February 2022-December 2025
sources.organization: Government of Ukraine, World Bank Group, European Commission and United Nations
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, with sector, oblast and hromada detail where available
sources.temporal_coverage: Damage through 31 December 2025, losses with an 18-month projection, and needs for 2026-2035.
sources.methodology: Joint administrative, engineering, remote-sensing, partner, and modelling assessment using sector damage, loss, and needs methods.
sources.limitations: Occupied and frontline data are incomplete, methods evolve, and needs are not outcomes or firm finance commitments.

sources.title: Status of Environment and Climate in Ukraine: Assessing the Impact of War and Implications for Reconstruction
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, with mapped subnational and ecosystem evidence
sources.methodology: Multi-source environmental synthesis using remote sensing, administrative data, mapped analysis, and policy review.
sources.limitations: Coverage is weakest in occupied and combat areas and attribution among climate, warfare, and land management is often limited.

sources.title: Attacks against Ukraine's Energy Infrastructure and Update on the Human Rights Situation in Ukraine, 1 December 2025-31 May 2026
sources.organization: Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
geographic_coverage: Government-controlled Ukraine and selected affected cities and facilities
sources.methodology: Field monitoring, 180 visits, 1,926 interviews overall, and specialized energy-impact visits and interviews.
sources.limitations: No direct occupied-territory access; seasonal cold and heat are not attributed to climate change.

sources.title: Rapid Environmental Assessment of Kakhovka Dam Breach, Ukraine, 2023
sources.organization: United Nations Environment Programme and UNEP-DHI
geographic_coverage: Lower Dnipro, Kakhovka reservoir, downstream and irrigation-dependent areas
sources.methodology: Remote sensing, hydrological analysis, partner data, desk evidence, and expert assessment under access constraints.
sources.limitations: Many impacts were modelled or preliminary; the breach is a conflict-related infrastructure disaster, not a climate event.

sources.title: Impact of the Russia-Ukraine Armed Conflict on Water Resources and Water Infrastructure
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, concentrated in eastern and southern incident evidence
sources.temporal_coverage: Mainly the first three months after 24 February 2022.
sources.methodology: Systematic compilation of realized and potential impacts from verified public reports and supplementary evidence.
sources.limitations: Early-war and undercounted snapshot with reporting bias and no climate attribution.

sources.title: Rebuilding Ukraine by Reinforcing Regional and Municipal Governance
sources.organization: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
sources.temporal_coverage: Primarily pre-February 2022 capacity evidence interpreted for recovery.
sources.methodology: Surveys of 741 municipalities, 119 rayons and 24 oblasts plus Kyiv, with administrative and efficiency analysis.
sources.limitations: Pre-full-scale-war, partly self-reported baseline; current municipal capacity can differ substantially.

sources.title: Final Evaluation of Mykolaiv Recovered
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme Evaluation Resource Centre / external evaluation team
geographic_coverage: Mykolaiv Oblast and participating municipalities and institutions
sources.temporal_coverage: Project from July 2023 through December 2025; evaluation October 2025-February 2026.
sources.methodology: External mixed-method final evaluation using interviews, document review, site evidence, and participant surveys.
sources.limitations: Limited counterfactual and causal attribution, low response rates for some surveys, and no national generalizability.

sources.title: Ukraine: Reframing the Narrative of Climate, Environmental Degradation and Conflict
sources.organization: adelphi / Weathering Risk / International Rescue Committee
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, with southern, eastern and community examples
sources.methodology: Desk review, expert consultations, and qualitative pathway synthesis.
sources.limitations: Expert synthesis rather than causal evaluation; some chains rely on secondary evidence and remain inferential.

sources.title: Priorities for Agricultural Support in Ukraine
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, national and agroecological with east-central hotspots
sources.temporal_coverage: War context through 2024 with climate scenarios at 1.5 and 3 degrees Celsius warming.
sources.methodology: Agricultural-sector review, policy analysis, and model-derived green-water-scarcity estimates.
sources.limitations: Some modelling was forthcoming, scenario results are not observed impacts, and exposure is not fully war-adjusted.

sources.title: Policy Brief: State Strategy on Internal Displacement
sources.organization: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees Ukraine
geographic_coverage: Ukraine, national, regional and community implementation
sources.methodology: Review of the adopted strategy, legal framework, targets, responsibilities, and implementation arrangements.
sources.limitations: Newly adopted policy; first formal assessment is due in 2027 and financing and local delivery remain uncertain.

sources.title: Yemen Country Climate and Development Report: Policy Note
geographic_coverage: Yemen, national with spatial exposure and sector modelling
sources.temporal_coverage: Recent baseline with projections mainly to 2050 and economic scenarios to 2040.
sources.methodology: Climate and macroeconomic modelling, spatial exposure analysis, and sector policy synthesis.
sources.limitations: Scenario results are not forecasts; the PDF contains erroneous West Bank and Gaza running headers and substantial data gaps.

sources.title: Charting the Course: A Water Security Diagnostic for Yemen
geographic_coverage: Yemen, national with basin and city cases including Taiz
sources.temporal_coverage: Structural history and conflict-era evidence through 2024.
sources.methodology: Administrative and remote-sensing evidence, mobile survey, literature synthesis, modelling, and consultations with nearly 1,700 participants.
sources.limitations: Hydrological monitoring is degraded, groundwater information is incomplete, and consultation evidence is not a causal estimate.

sources.title: Yemen's NDC 3.0 Vision
sources.organization: Republic of Yemen and United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate 1971-2020, mid-century projections, and policy roadmap through 2035.
sources.methodology: Official climate-risk and policy synthesis with sector goals and institutional roadmap.
sources.limitations: The registered document calls itself a Vision and says final NDC preparation and submission would occur in 2026; operational status is unclear.

sources.title: Water-related Conflict Assessment Report
geographic_coverage: Selected districts in Abyan, Hadramawt, and Dhamar
sources.temporal_coverage: Field and project evidence mainly from 2022-2023.
sources.methodology: Local conflict assessment, interviews, community consultation, institutional analysis, and project-linked field evidence.
sources.limitations: Narrow local coverage, inconsistent document dating, and project-linked evidence without independent measurement of durable conflict reduction.

sources.title: Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: Yemen 2023
sources.organization: Stockholm International Peace Research Institute and Norwegian Institute of International Affairs
geographic_coverage: Yemen, national with selected local examples
sources.methodology: Four-page secondary synthesis of climate, livelihood, mobility, and conflict pathways.
sources.limitations: Secondary and concise; it identifies conditional mechanisms rather than demonstrating causal climate-conflict effects.

sources.title: Climate and Health Vulnerability Assessment: Republic of Yemen
sources.temporal_coverage: Recent baseline with CMIP6 projections to mid-century.
sources.methodology: Desktop health-vulnerability assessment using CCKP and CMIP6 climate indicators, facility data, and adaptive-capacity indicators.
sources.limitations: Facility exposure does not establish structural vulnerability or service failure; some labels and units appear inconsistent.

sources.title: Yemen, Government-Controlled Areas: Acute Food Insecurity Analysis, March-December 2026
geographic_coverage: 118 districts in 12 Government of Yemen-controlled governorates
sources.methodology: IPC convergence-of-evidence classification using food security, livelihoods, prices, assistance, conflict, and hazard evidence.
sources.limitations: Medium evidence level and partial territorial coverage; results are multi-causal and not attributable to climate alone.

sources.title: Independent Country Programme Evaluation: Yemen
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme Independent Evaluation Office
geographic_coverage: Yemen with fieldwork in seven governorates
sources.methodology: Independent evaluation using document review, 169 interviews, more than 25 visits, and 13 focus groups.
sources.limitations: No focus groups in de facto authority areas and limited causal attribution of welfare, resilience, or peace outcomes.

sources.title: Inter-Agency Humanitarian Evaluation of the Yemen Crisis
geographic_coverage: Yemen with six-governorate survey and field evidence
sources.methodology: Independent theory-based evaluation with 144 interviews, 64 focus groups, project visits, aid-worker survey, SMS survey, and secondary analysis.
sources.limitations: Low SMS response, restricted Marib and de facto authority access, agency data-sharing constraints, and no climate-specific evaluation design.

sources.title: Yemen Emergency Crisis Response Project P159053: Implementation Completion Report Review
geographic_coverage: Yemen, project areas and participating local institutions
sources.temporal_coverage: Emergency project implementation and completion through 2022.
sources.methodology: Independent desk review of completion evidence, monitoring, third-party verification, outputs, and stated outcomes.
sources.limitations: Welfare effects and causal mechanisms were inadequately specified, and output delivery is stronger evidence than sustained resilience.

sources.title: Final Evaluation: Strengthening Institutional and Economic Resilience in Yemen
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme and European Union external evaluation team
sources.methodology: External mixed-method evaluation with document review, 105 stakeholders, site evidence, and qualitative assessment.
sources.limitations: No structured impact assessment or counterfactual; maintenance, inclusion, and peace effects remain incompletely measured.

sources.title: Conflict Resilience of Water and Energy Supply Infrastructure: Insights from Yemen
geographic_coverage: Urban Yemen, including Sana'a and Taiz
sources.methodology: Qualitative resilience framework using interviews, narratives, utility information, and secondary data.
sources.limitations: Limited representativeness and incomplete quantitative data; continuity is not consistent system performance.

sources.title: Livelihood Resilience and Adaptation Practices Among Agricultural Communities in Yemen
geographic_coverage: Six rural communities in Abyan, Hadramawt, Marib, and Taiz
sources.methodology: Purposive survey of 164 people, 20 interviews, six focus groups, ethnographic observation, and grounded-theory analysis.
sources.limitations: Non-representative local sample, only 13 survey respondents in Marib, and causal claims rely heavily on perceptions and qualitative evidence.

evidence_records.statement: Afghanistan’s mean annual temperature increased by about 1.8°C between the 1951-1980 and 1981-2010 climatic periods, with larger reported warming in the South than nationally.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Strong observed warming.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Reanalysis-based historical result; does not alone establish impacts.

evidence_records.statement: The SNC’s analysis of 95th-percentile precipitation found no noticeable increase in heavy precipitation during 1950-2010, despite reports of increasing flood impacts.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Flood impacts ≠ proven rainfall trend.

source_refs.locator: viewer P49, Fig. 13 and accompanying text. (UNFCCC1)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Flood risk also depends on snowmelt, drought-hardened soils, land/exposure and infrastructure; later trends may differ.

evidence_records.statement: Seven CORDEX regional models projected roughly +1.5°C warming by 2050 under RCP4.5 and about +3°C under RCP8.5 relative to a 1976-2005 baseline; near-term Central Highlands/Hindu Kush warming was 1.5-1.7°C versus 1.1-1.4°C in lowlands.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Mid-century warming across scenarios.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Older-generation scenarios/models; stated projection uncertainty about ±2°C.

evidence_records.statement: The SNC projected a 5-10% spring precipitation decline through 2050 in the North, Central Highlands and East, while projecting about a 10% winter increase in the Hindu Kush and no significant precipitation trend in the arid South.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Precipitation change is region/season specific.
evidence_records.ecological_level: North; Central Highlands; East; Hindu Kush; South
evidence_records.uncertainty: Source explicitly says precipitation-model uncertainty is higher.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI/NUPI reports mean annual temperature rising from 12.23°C in 1960 to 14.24°C in 2024 and summarizes current models as projecting a further 1.5-3°C increase by 2050 depending on emissions.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Recent synthesis confirms warming direction.

source_refs.locator: PDF P1, “Climate exposure: trends and projections”. (NUPI3)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Secondary synthesis rather than primary climate dataset; scenario details abbreviated.

evidence_records.statement: Afghanistan’s 2015 NDC identified funding gaps, lack of expertise, inadequate historical climate data, weak public awareness and security as major adaptation barriers and estimated $10.785 billion for its listed adaptation actions over ten years.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Adaptation constrained by finance, data, expertise and security.

source_refs.locator: PDF P4, “Adaptation Needs and Means of Implementation,” lines 188-240. (UNFCCC5)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Government self-assessment from 2015; institutional arrangements subsequently changed substantially.

evidence_records.statement: In September-October 2025, IPC classified an estimated 13.8 million people, 28% of the analysed population, in IPC Phase 3 or worse, including about 2.9 million in Phase 4.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Acute food insecurity remained widespread.
evidence_records.uncertainty: IPC explicitly identifies several simultaneous drivers; not climate-attributable as a whole.

evidence_records.statement: IPC reported the 2025 drought as the most extensive since 2018 and 2021 and estimated 3.4 million people in 65 districts were severely affected through food, water and livelihood impacts.
evidence_records.compact_statement: 2025 drought had broad livelihood exposure.
evidence_records.ecological_level: 65 districts; especially cited Daikundi, Helmand, Kandahar
evidence_records.uncertainty: IPC is synthesizing FAO/OCHA estimates; the statistic does not establish anthropogenic attribution.

evidence_records.statement: IPC projected 13.8 million people in Phase 3 or worse for April-September 2026, including about 2.889 million in Phase 4.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Food insecurity projected to remain high in 2026.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Projection contingent on assumptions about weather, production, assistance, markets and borders.

evidence_records.statement: In WoAA 2025, 64% of households reported drought impacts, up from 34% in 2024; 92% did so in the Central Highlands. Flood exposure was 10%, while earthquake exposure was recorded separately at below 1% because fieldwork preceded later earthquakes.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Drought dominated 2025 reported environmental exposure.

source_refs.locator: viewer P40-P41, Fig. 45 and drought discussion. (UNDP2)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Household self-report; earthquake timing demonstrates why geological hazards must be kept distinct.

evidence_records.statement: The share of households reporting full drinking-water sufficiency fell from 59% in 2024 to 44% in 2025; Central Highlands and Eastern regions experienced the largest declines.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Drinking-water sufficiency worsened.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Report interprets drought, population pressure and infrastructure jointly; shares are survey responses.

evidence_records.statement: In UNDP’s 2025 12-province comparison, recent returnees had a 92% subsistence-insecurity headcount, versus 85% among non-recent returnees and 74% among local communities.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Recent returnees showed higher multidimensional deprivation.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Subsample finding, not automatically national for all returnees.

evidence_records.statement: Female-headed households in the common 2025 survey sample increasingly relied on home-based production; 68% of adults were working versus 54% in male-headed households, but child labour was 10% versus 7%, making this coping strategy potentially costly.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Home-based coping can carry human-capital costs.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Observational comparison; UNDP’s interpretation of adaptation mechanism is not causal proof.

evidence_records.statement: About 17% of surveyed women returnees in Herat, Nangarhar and Kabul were employed after return; 77% lacked tools for income generation and only 9% reported having needed equipment.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Women returnees face strong livelihood-capacity constraints.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Telephone/cross-sectional sample excludes some women without phone access; no causal inference.

evidence_records.statement: More than 75% of 292 surveyed returnee households in Herat and Kandahar said clean-water access was difficult or very difficult, and over 70% said it had worsened during the previous six months as returns increased.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Returns overlap with severe local water stress.

source_refs.locator: PDF P2/P7, methodology and Water Impacts. (Mercy Corps4)

evidence_records.uncertainty: “Due to returns” is respondent/report attribution; cannot quantify causal share versus drought, extraction and infrastructure.

evidence_records.statement: Mercy Corps respondents reported water-related community tensions roughly three times more often in urban than rural surveyed communities, and about 80% of reported cases were described as unresolved by community mediation.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Local water stress can become a social-tension mediator.
evidence_records.ecological_level: Surveyed urban/rural sites in Herat and Kandahar
geographies: Surveyed urban/rural sites in Herat and Kandahar

source_refs.locator: PDF P9, “Financial, Social and Protection Costs”. (Mercy Corps4)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Local perceptions; water stress itself reflects non-climate drivers. No evidence that these tensions caused organized violence.

evidence_records.statement: In three Balkh districts, participants described drought-related displacement as a gradual process in which depleted livelihoods, higher costs and reduced access to basic services accumulated until households could no longer cope.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Drought -> livelihood erosion -> displacement, locally documented.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Purposive qualitative study; process evidence is stronger than prevalence evidence and remains local.

evidence_records.statement: Balkh participants made 17 references to intracommunity tensions associated with varying combinations of local conflict dynamics, personal grievances and competition for scarce resources, but ten references indicated insecurity was not an issue.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Conflict evidence in Balkh is mixed, not deterministic.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Small purposive qualitative sample; divergent reports; no causal attribution to climate.

evidence_records.statement: Ten participants in the Balkh study said displaced households mainly relied on family, friends or the wider host community to meet basic needs or find work.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Informal solidarity is a resilience resource.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Very small qualitative evidence; availability and durability of support are not quantified.

evidence_records.statement: Balkh climate-affected IDPs reported coping measures including debt, asset sales, drinking unsafe water, family separation and reduced meals.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Coping often depletes future resilience.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Qualitative local findings; prevalence unknown.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI/NUPI concludes that climate change is rarely the main driver of conflict in Afghanistan and organizes relevant mechanisms around livelihood impacts, migration/mobility, armed actors/security and political-economic grievances.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate-FCV effects are mediated.

source_refs.locator: PDF P1, “Climate-related peace and security risks”. (NUPI3)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Expert synthesis; does not estimate causal effects.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI/NUPI finds that restrictions on women’s and girls’ rights and sociocultural norms increase dependence and constrain participation and disaster-assistance access, thereby reducing adaptive capacity.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Gender restrictions amplify climate vulnerability.
evidence_records.uncertainty: General synthesis; extent varies locally and by household.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI/NUPI identifies governance challenges, political context and donor hesitancy as impediments to effective climate-adaptation strategies.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Political/institutional conditions constrain adaptation.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Expert synthesis; separate effects of sanctions, governance and donor choices are not quantified.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI/NUPI describes shared-water tensions with Iran as arising from a combination of water stress, water-management decisions, dam/irrigation plans and political instability, while also identifying transboundary water cooperation as a possible entry point for dialogue.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Shared water can generate both tension and cooperation.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Climate contribution cannot be separated from allocation, infrastructure and political decisions; peace benefit is potential rather than evaluated outcome.

evidence_records.statement: UNDP reports humanitarian funding declining from $1.62 billion in 2024 to $0.91 billion in 2025, while more than 440 health facilities were closed or suspended because of funding shortages.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Aid contraction weakened service-delivery capacity.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Funding and service decline are not climate impacts; they can increase vulnerability to multiple shocks.

evidence_records.statement: Current World Bank/ARTF support keeps funds outside de facto-authority systems and control and uses independent third-party monitoring to verify project compliance.
evidence_records.compact_statement: External delivery architecture substitutes for normal state channels.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Demonstrates delivery arrangements, not effectiveness or adaptation outcomes.

evidence_records.statement: The 2023 CDRRP terminal evaluation rated overall project outcomes 5.25/6, but activities had been suspended in August 2021 and never resumed, and the evaluator lacked some information needed for cost-effectiveness assessment.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Positive project rating with major evaluation/context constraints.

source_refs.locator: PDF P1, P21 and P73, Exhibit 9-5. (Evaluation Resource Center6)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Terminal evaluation without counterfactual; almost two-year post-suspension gap; remote methodology.

evidence_records.statement: The 2019 CCAP terminal evaluation rated overall project results “Satisfactory” and judged that target rural livelihoods and exposure to climate-induced disaster risk had improved within the project areas.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Earlier adaptation project rated satisfactory.

source_refs.locator: PDF P10, evaluation rating table/conclusion. (Evaluation Resource Center11)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Evaluator judgement, not counterfactual impact estimate; cannot be generalized beyond project areas or to present institutions.

evidence_records.statement: The same 2019 evaluation rated M&E at entry and implementation only moderately satisfactory, found many indicators insufficiently SMART/outcome-focused, and noted the lack of an adequate exit strategy for some infrastructure.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Evaluation design and sustainability weaknesses limited confidence.

source_refs.locator: PDF P41-P43 §3.2.5 and P53 sustainability/exit discussion. (Evaluation Resource Center11)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Clear evaluation finding; actual long-term failure/success was not measured.

evidence_records.statement: The World Bank estimated nearly 3.7 million returns from Iran and Pakistan during Afghanistan’s FY2025, population growth of about 11% and a 5.6% fall in GDP per capita, with return concentrations adding pressure to health, nutrition and WASH services.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Mass returns are an independent vulnerability and service-pressure driver.
evidence_records.ecological_level: National; notably Herat in service discussion

source_refs.locator: viewer P7/P14 and P26. (The World Bank9)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Macro estimates; return effects interact with aid, markets, borders and drought but should not be labelled climate effects.

evidence_records.statement: WFP's country synthesis identifies droughts and heatwaves as compounding desertification and water scarcity and threatening agricultural productivity in Burkina Faso.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Drought and heat pressures compound water scarcity and agricultural risk.

source_refs.locator: country overview sections 'Burkina Faso' and 'Resilience building'

evidence_records.uncertainty: The operational overview provides no reproducible national trend analysis and does not isolate anthropogenic climate attribution.

evidence_records.statement: WFP reports that agriculture employs about 80 percent of the population, most production is rainfed and climate-sensitive, and smallholders often lack markets, quality inputs, and modern techniques.
evidence_records.compact_statement: High dependence on rainfed agriculture creates broad livelihood exposure.

source_refs.locator: country overview paragraphs on climate change and agriculture

evidence_records.uncertainty: The employment share is a national aggregate and does not describe subnational or livelihood-specific exposure.

evidence_records.statement: Burkina Faso's updated National Adaptation Plan provides a national framework for prioritizing climate risks, sector actions, institutions, and adaptation implementation.
evidence_records.compact_statement: An updated national plan establishes adaptation priorities and institutional responsibilities.

source_refs.locator: UNFCCC document record and updated NAP sector and institutional framework

evidence_records.uncertainty: Plan adoption does not demonstrate financed implementation, local reach, or effectiveness.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI's systematic review finds that West African climate-conflict research supports mediated pathways through livelihoods, migration and pastoral mobility, armed-group tactics, and elite exploitation, while emphasizing that the underlying academic evidence remains limited.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Regional evidence supports mediated, not deterministic, climate-insecurity pathways.

source_refs.locator: webpage summary and report sections II-III on pathways and evidence limits

evidence_records.uncertainty: This regional synthesis cannot establish that any pathway operates uniformly or causally across Burkina Faso.

evidence_records.statement: CGIAR reports that Burkina Faso's climate-security strategy process drew on research and a three-phase consultation led by the environment ministry with UNDP and the Liptako-Gourma authority.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate-security analysis entered a multi-actor national strategy process.
institutions: Ministry of Environment, Water and Sanitation

source_refs.locator: sections on Burkina Faso consultation and national climate-security strategy

evidence_records.uncertainty: The page documents process and draft uptake, not adoption, implementation, or peace outcomes.

evidence_records.statement: UNHCR documented displaced families in Kongoussi and Kaya whose temporary shelters and belongings were damaged by heavy 2020 rains, including families located on flood-prone land because safer urban land was scarce.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Conflict-displaced households faced concentrated flood exposure in unsafe urban sites.

source_refs.locator: paragraphs on Kongoussi and Kaya flood impacts and floodplain settlement

evidence_records.uncertainty: The documented sites illustrate a pathway but are not representative of all displaced households or towns.

evidence_records.statement: UNHCR reports cautious expert assessment that violence and displacement have overlapped with poor drought-affected areas where armed groups exploited tensions over water and arable land; the source explicitly rejects a simple direct climate-conflict link.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Resource stress can be exploited within wider armed-conflict dynamics, but attribution is limited.

source_refs.locator: paragraphs cautioning against direct attribution and describing resource-tension exploitation

evidence_records.uncertainty: Conflict, exclusion, political violence, and land governance remain independent drivers; the source offers no causal estimate.

evidence_records.statement: WFP describes acute hunger as driven by interacting violence, displacement, poverty, market disruption, service constraints, and climate shocks, with women and girls facing heightened food-security and protection risks.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Multiple shocks create differentiated food and protection sensitivity.

source_refs.locator: country overview paragraphs on crisis drivers, hunger, and differentiated vulnerability

evidence_records.uncertainty: The synthesis combines indicators with different dates and cannot allocate observed hunger among interacting drivers.

evidence_records.statement: WFP reports that insecurity restricts farming, destabilizes markets, limits essential services, and constrains humanitarian access, leaving some communities reliant on costly road or helicopter deliveries.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Conflict and access constraints erode household and institutional coping options.

source_refs.locator: country overview paragraphs on insecurity, services, markets, and humanitarian access

evidence_records.uncertainty: The national overview does not quantify access constraints by location or isolate their climate-adaptation effect.

evidence_records.statement: WFP reports resilience activities that restore degraded land, develop lowlands, construct water assets, support smallholders, and aim to reduce resource tensions and foster social cohesion.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Land, water, and livelihood assets provide potential adaptive and cohesion capacity.
geographies: WFP target areas in Burkina Faso
evidence_records.uncertainty: These are program activities and intended mechanisms, not independently measured adaptation or cohesion impacts.

evidence_records.statement: WFP's independent portfolio evaluation found an adaptive emergency-response vehicle and humanitarian-access strengths, but also an initially reactive approach, rising food insecurity despite response scale, uncertain resilience achievements, and inclusion investments whose potential remained unproven.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Independent evaluation found response strengths alongside major effectiveness and sustainability limits.

source_refs.locator: evaluation webpage conclusions on relevance, emergency response, food insecurity, resilience, inclusion, and staffing

evidence_records.uncertainty: The evaluation covers activities only through July 2022 and does not isolate climate-specific program effects.

evidence_records.statement: A World Bank results brief reports that the local-government program worked across all 13 regions and supported regulatory reform, fiscal transfers, municipal monitoring, citizen accountability, and displaced-person assistance through all 349 municipalities.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Nationwide municipal systems provide an institutional platform for crisis-sensitive delivery.
evidence_records.uncertainty: The implementing institution's results brief does not independently verify service quality or climate-specific capacity.

evidence_records.statement: The local-government program reported assistance to 423,521 displaced people, training for municipal and social-service staff, and displaced-person support integrated into 349 municipal plans, while fiscal and market revenue shocks exposed municipal financing constraints.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Municipal crisis delivery reached displaced households but remained exposed to fiscal shocks.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Reported outputs do not establish longer-term welfare, cohesion, or climate-resilience effects.

evidence_records.statement: FAO's Liptako-Gourma lessons report that a 2020-2024 FAO-IOM initiative engaged farmer organizations and authorities to strengthen transhumance governance, social cohesion, and resilience amid land, water, pasture, climate, and security pressures.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Conflict-sensitive transhumance governance is a documented regional resilience practice.

source_refs.locator: project summary and lessons on 2020-2024 peaceful transhumance initiative

evidence_records.uncertainty: The regional good-practice summary does not isolate Burkina Faso results or provide an independent counterfactual evaluation.

evidence_records.statement: Since 2023 the Hydromet project has distributed 9,700 farmer rain gauges, trained recipients and local liaisons, and linked observations to meteorological, water-resource, and agricultural early-warning institutions across multiple provinces.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Farmer rain gauges and institutional links expand localized climate-information capacity.
institutions: Ministry of Agriculture Early Warning System

source_refs.locator: story highlights and sections on training, institutional links, and 9,700 rain gauges

evidence_records.uncertainty: Output monitoring and testimonials do not establish uptake equity, forecast accuracy, yield effects, or performance in insecure areas.

evidence_records.statement: Mean temperature in CAR has increased by about 0.35°C per decade since the 1970s.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Rapid observed warming since 1970s.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Directly reported in reviewed synthesis; underlying datasets not independently reanalysed here.

evidence_records.statement: Regional projections used for CAR indicate mid-century warming of about 2-2.5°C under SSP2-4.5 and 2.5-3°C under SSP5-8.5.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Substantial further warming by ~2050.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Projection is presented for the wider region relevant to CAR, not a high-resolution CAR-only ensemble.

evidence_records.statement: Frequency and intensity of heavy precipitation are projected to increase, with potential increases in flooding and soil erosion.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Heavier rainfall likely raises flood risk.
evidence_records.scenario: Future; source does not give one single national horizon
evidence_records.uncertainty: Magnitude and local distribution remain uncertain.

evidence_records.statement: Drought remains a recurrent hazard, particularly in northern CAR, but the climate synthesis notes that future drought could decrease under wetter rainfall projections.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Current drought hazard; future trend uncertain.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Important counter-evidence to simple “ever-worsening drought” narratives.

evidence_records.statement: CAR's NAP treats agriculture/livestock, energy, forests, water, health, land-use planning, infrastructure and habitat as adaptation sectors.
evidence_records.compact_statement: NAP is multi-sectoral.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Establishes policy scope, not delivery.

evidence_records.statement: CAR's BTR states that climate-risk/vulnerability work is insufficient and that much existing assessment is qualitative and subjective.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate-risk evidence base remains weak.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Government self-diagnosis; it does not quantify how much insecurity versus other constraints causes the deficit.

evidence_records.statement: The BTR reports weak integration of adaptation into planning/budget systems, lack of a specific adaptation budget, limited sector adaptation plans, and shortages of climate data, equipment and human resources.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Core adaptation institutions face implementation constraints.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Constraints are clear; their causal attribution to FCV specifically is not isolated.

evidence_records.statement: NDC 3.0 records a 2025 baseline in which several strategic water-planning instruments and the intended national water-information/monitoring system were not yet operational, with 2030 targets for establishment.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Water planning/monitoring starts from major gaps.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Baseline is government-reported; future targets are commitments rather than outcomes.

evidence_records.statement: NDC 3.0 identifies women, youth, persons with disabilities, displaced people and Indigenous peoples among groups to be included in climate indicators and implementation.
evidence_records.compact_statement: National policy recognizes differentiated vulnerability.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Policy recognition does not establish measured differences in climate impacts or outcomes.

evidence_records.statement: IPC analysis estimates more than 2 million people in IPC Phase 3+ during April-August 2026, including about 262,000 in Phase 4.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Nearly one-third faces acute food insecurity.

source_refs.locator: current CAR IPC analysis, opening results section (IPCinfo)

evidence_records.uncertainty: IPC is a standardized analytical classification; the period is a projection/current analytical estimate, not a census.

evidence_records.statement: The IPC analysis attributes improved conditions relative to an earlier projection partly to better rainfall, stronger agricultural production and humanitarian food assistance.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Rainfall and production can improve food outcomes.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Does not isolate rainfall's causal effect from assistance, conflict or market changes.

evidence_records.statement: The same IPC assessment identifies persistent conflict, displacement, high food/fuel prices, weak purchasing power and degraded roads as continuing constraints on food access.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Food insecurity has major non-climate drivers.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Strong evidence of co-drivers, but not a decomposition of their relative causal weight.

evidence_records.statement: UNHCR recorded roughly 442,000 IDPs in CAR in September 2025, alongside refugee and asylum-seeker populations including people displaced by the Sudan war.
evidence_records.compact_statement: CAR combines internal and cross-border displacement.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Primarily FCV exposure evidence; it does not establish climate causation.

evidence_records.statement: By April 2026 roughly 22,000 Sudanese refugees were in the Birao/Korsi area, approximately doubling Birao's local population, while substantial basic-service gaps persisted.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Refugee inflow sharply increased Birao service demand.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Highly localized; must not be generalized to CAR nationally.

evidence_records.statement: NUPI concludes that limited weather monitoring and security-risk analysis leave insufficient CAR-specific evidence on climate-peace-security relationships.
evidence_records.compact_statement: CAR-specific climate-security evidence is thin.
evidence_records.uncertainty: This is a finding about the evidence base, not about the magnitude of a climate-conflict effect.

evidence_records.statement: NUPI reports that climatic pressures and insecurity in the wider region can alter transhumant movement into CAR, while weak regulation and competition can contribute to tensions.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate and insecurity can reshape pastoral mobility.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Part of the climate link is regional; source itself says CAR-specific causal evidence is limited.

evidence_records.statement: NUPI reports that armed actors' control/taxation of transhumance corridors and natural resources can intensify farmer-herder tensions and weaken local dispute-resolution systems.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Armed control can turn mobility into a conflict risk.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Specialist synthesis; local incidence and prevalence are not quantified nationally.

evidence_records.statement: ICRC practitioner evidence describes pre-crisis livestock-route regulation and negotiated compensation as mechanisms that reduced disputes, while violence and state withdrawal after 2013 disrupted these arrangements.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Governance institutions can reduce or amplify farmer-herder risk.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Qualitative practitioner source; locations and effect sizes are not systematically sampled.

evidence_records.statement: The May 2025 World Bank ISR reported 583,389 farmers reached by the emergency food project, including 168,336 women, against a 700,000 target.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Large programme reach was reported.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Self-reported/project-supervision indicator; reach is not evidence of resilience outcome.

evidence_records.statement: At the same reporting point, recorded food-crop production was 112,912 tonnes against a 200,000-tonne intermediate target, while hydrometeorological equipment procurement was still under way.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Some output targets remained incomplete.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Project monitoring, not independent evaluation; future completion possible.

evidence_records.statement: IEG's independent assessment of the 2014-2016 emergency food/agriculture operation rated its outcome unsatisfactory and identified weak monitoring, seed-procurement problems and incomplete infrastructure.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Earlier emergency agriculture response performed poorly.

source_refs.locator: Principal Ratings and Summary, pp. viii-xi

evidence_records.uncertainty: Independent but historical; cannot be assumed to describe present project performance.

evidence_records.statement: IEG found that reliance on cooperative membership for targeting could miss particularly vulnerable non-members, illustrating an unintended inclusion/exclusion risk in fragile settings.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Delivery design can exclude vulnerable households.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Evaluated finding from one older operation; not evidence that all current programmes reproduce the problem.

evidence_records.statement: NDC 3.0 reports earlier projections in which Sudano-Sahelian temperatures rise from +0.7°C in 2025 to +4.8°C in 2100.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Strong long-run northern warming projected.
evidence_records.scenario: 2025-2100; scenario/model not stated in cited passage
evidence_records.uncertainty: Exact values verified, but inherited from NDC 2.0 and model/scenario absent at locator.

evidence_records.statement: NDC 3.0 reports 2040 precipitation reductions of about 1-5% in High Savannas/High Plateaus and 2-0% in the bimodal forest zone, with 0-2% increase possible on the coast.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Rainfall change is spatially heterogeneous.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Underlying projection methodology not shown at locator.

evidence_records.statement: NDC 3.0 anticipates lower crop yields, livestock productivity and water availability in some regions under warming.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Agriculture/livestock/water are climate-sensitive.
evidence_records.uncertainty: National policy synthesis rather than new impact modelling.

evidence_records.statement: IMF identifies recurrent drought, flood, landslide and coastal erosion as major climate-related risks in Cameroon.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Multiple climate hazards affect Cameroon.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Expert diagnostic; landslide occurrence also depends on geological/land-use/infrastructure factors.

evidence_records.statement: UNHCR portal reports an estimated 510,855 IDPs in the Far North as of 31 July 2026.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Far North has >510k estimated IDPs.

source_refs.locator: indicator “IDPs in the Far North region,” lines 37-43. (UNHCR Data Portal)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Estimate produced by IOM; not a climate-displacement count.

evidence_records.statement: OCHA/UNHCR portal reports an estimated 493,402 IDPs in the North-West/South-West as of 31 July 2026.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Nearly 493k NW/SW IDPs.

source_refs.locator: indicator “IDPs in North-West/South-West,” lines 30-36. (UNHCR Data Portal)

evidence_records.uncertainty: OCHA estimate; separate methodology from Far North figure.

evidence_records.statement: WFP estimated 2.9 million people faced acute food insecurity in June-August 2026, including 249,000 at emergency levels; >82% were in six crisis regions.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Acute hunger concentrated in crisis regions.
evidence_records.ecological_level: Far North, East, Adamawa, North, NW, SW

source_refs.locator: webpage para. beginning “Cameroon continues…”, lines 251-253. (World Food Programme)

evidence_records.uncertainty: WFP explicitly identifies multiple drivers; not climate-attributable as a whole.

evidence_records.statement: WFP reported displaced families exhausting coping mechanisms amid conflict, food insecurity and intensifying climate shocks.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Coping capacity is strained in crisis settings.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Operational assessment, not representative coping-capacity survey.

evidence_records.statement: Funding shortfalls forced WFP to reduce its 2026 targeted assistance population by more than 35%.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Humanitarian delivery capacity fell materially.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Establishes reduced target coverage, not downstream effects on conflict or resilience.

evidence_records.statement: UNDP reports local authorities lack sufficient autonomy, technical capacity and human resources, while slow fiscal/competency transfers restrict service delivery.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Decentralized delivery capacity is constrained.
evidence_records.uncertainty: UN synthesis rather than a municipality-level performance census.

evidence_records.statement: UNDP states that protracted crises and large displaced/refugee populations place sustained pressure on national/local authorities and resources.
evidence_records.compact_statement: FCV and displacement strain service systems.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Direction to specific climate-adaptation outcomes is inferred, not measured.

evidence_records.statement: NDC 3.0 assigns climate coordination to MINEPDED and specifies national/local coordination and working groups for adaptation, finance, research/MRV and gender.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Formal multi-level climate governance exists.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Institutional design is verified; actual effectiveness cannot be inferred.

evidence_records.statement: NDC 3.0 identifies inadequate intersectoral consultation, weak private/CSO ownership, regulatory gaps, climate-finance access problems and fragmented data as governance challenges.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Implementation constraints remain substantial.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Government self-assessment; magnitude not quantified.

evidence_records.statement: The immediate documented triggers of 2021 Logone Birni clashes included cattle drowning in a fishing channel and later cattle destroying crops.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Immediate clash triggers involved resource-use incidents.

source_refs.locator: “Clashes in Cameroon’s Logone Birni,” lines 90-94. (Refugees International)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Source is secondary/field-report evidence, not incident-level causal adjudication.

evidence_records.statement: Interviewed displaced people linked Logone Birni tensions to erratic rainfall/flooding affecting food, pasture, water and crops.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate stress was reported as an aggravating mediator.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Respondent attribution; governance and armed-political factors also reported; no causal identification.

evidence_records.statement: Refugees International notes that Lake Chad shrank severely after 1970s-80s droughts but subsequently recovered/stabilized substantially, while population growth and conflict-related restrictions continued to affect access.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Simple “ever-shrinking lake causes conflict” narrative is inadequate.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Regional rather than Cameroon-only evidence; hydrological figures are secondary within report.

evidence_records.statement: Kilum-Ijim field surveys found sporadic/unreliable rainfall and more dry spells associated with reduced pasture and longer-distance livestock movement.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Rainfall variability pressures pastoral mobility locally.

source_refs.locator: “Pasture Degradation and Shrinking Water Courses,” lines 467-475. (Frontiers)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Local observational/perception evidence; does not isolate climate change from variability.
