evidence_records.statement: In the same study, increasing cattle numbers and grazing pressure exceeded carrying capacity in some zones and were associated with pasture degradation and farmer-pastoralist conflict pressure.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Herd pressure is an independent co-driver.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Association and local interpretation; not national.

evidence_records.statement: Fundong council and traditional authorities were reported to demarcate grazing land and provide livestock water, while households diversified activities.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Local institutions provide some risk-reducing capacity.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Measures documented; effectiveness on conflict incidence not independently evaluated.

evidence_records.statement: AEP-Youth had no statistically significant impact on participants’ measured ability to recover from overall, climate or non-climate shocks.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Programme did not measurably improve shock recovery.

source_refs.locator: PDF p.23, Table 9 and text, lines 834-850. (IFAD)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Stronger attribution than most sources but non-randomized matching design and programme-specific sample.

evidence_records.statement: AEP-Youth participants’ FIES score was 13.2% lower than comparison households, while dietary-diversity measures showed no discernible effect.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Food-security gain did not translate into measured diet gains.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Programme-specific; outcome metric not direct climate resilience.

evidence_records.statement: PADFA had no dedicated climate-adaptation measures in its design and implemented only 46% of planned irrigation schemes, reducing the evaluation’s assessed likelihood of greater producer resilience.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Partial irrigation weakened intended adaptation.

source_refs.locator: PDF p.10, “Adaptation to climate change,” lines 567-580. (IOE)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Evaluation is independent, but resilience outcome itself was not directly causally measured.

evidence_records.statement: The Lake Chad CSO monitoring mission recorded beneficiary reports of reduced farmer-herder and IDP-host disputes after peacebuilding interventions.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Beneficiaries reported peacebuilding benefits.

source_refs.locator: PDF p.9, “Feedback from beneficiaries,” lines 298-315. (MPTF Gateway)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Self-reported during joint programme monitoring; no control group or independent outcome verification.

evidence_records.statement: World Bank reports security problems in NW/SW and Far North impeded implementation and led to reduced scope in conflict-affected cities.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Conflict directly constrained resilience investment delivery.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Clear project-level evidence; cannot infer all national adaptation delivery is similarly constrained.

evidence_records.statement: The urban project reported 364.12 ha protected from a 1-in-10-year flood, versus a 280-ha target.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Completed drainage produced measurable flood-protection output.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp.14-16, Table 2 and paras.28-31. (World Bank)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Output/modelled protection, not observed avoided losses across future floods.

evidence_records.statement: The same ICR records that planned nature-based drainage restoration was not completed and a formal beneficiary satisfaction survey was not conducted.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Important outcome/evaluation components remained incomplete.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Directly documented programme limitation.

evidence_records.statement: Under RCP4.5, the NAP reports median annual-mean warming of 1.4°C for 2041-2070 and 1.7°C for 2071-2100 relative to 1981-2010.
evidence_records.compact_statement: RCP4.5 produces a clear long-run warming signal.

source_refs.locator: printed p.37, Fig.14, “Key message for temperature.”

evidence_records.uncertainty: National ensemble; masks local variation.

evidence_records.statement: Under RCP8.5, median annual-mean warming is 2.1°C in 2041-2070 and 3.7°C in 2071-2100 relative to 1981-2010; IQRs are 1.8-2.4°C and 2.9-4.2°C.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Higher-emissions scenario implies substantially greater warming.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Ensemble/model uncertainty remains.

evidence_records.statement: National annual-mean precipitation projections have broad uncertainty: under RCP8.5 for 2071-2100 the NAP gives a median −2.3% change but an IQR from −8.8% to +14%.
evidence_records.compact_statement: National precipitation direction is uncertain.

source_refs.locator: printed p.39, Fig.19 / precipitation key message.

evidence_records.uncertainty: Range spans drying and wetting; national mean conceals regional contrasts.

evidence_records.statement: IMF staff found disagreement between CRU and ERA5 historical precipitation signals and noted only about six weather stations per million km².
evidence_records.compact_statement: Sparse observations limit confidence in national climate baselines.
evidence_records.uncertainty: IMF synthesis; station figure is an indicator of monitoring density, not full forecast capability.

evidence_records.statement: The World Bank reported that floods from Nov. 2023-Jan. 2024 affected more than 2.2 million people across 18 of 26 provinces and damaged homes, roads, electricity, water infrastructure and agricultural land.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Recent floods caused multi-sector, multi-province losses.

source_refs.locator: PDF p.3/report p.2, Country Context ¶2. (World Bank5)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Source calls floods climate-exacerbated; individual losses should not be attributed solely to climate change.

evidence_records.statement: The NAP identifies agriculture, water resources, health, coastal zones and energy among the country's most climate-vulnerable sectors.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate vulnerability spans major livelihood and service sectors.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Relies partly on older national vulnerability assessments.

evidence_records.statement: The NAP identifies restricted mobility and lower access to education, credit/banking and land tenure among factors limiting women's adaptive capacity.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Gendered institutions constrain adaptation options.
evidence_records.uncertainty: National framing may hide substantial local variation; some underlying statistics are older.

evidence_records.statement: In May 2026, FAO/WFP reported more than 26.5 million people struggling to meet basic food needs, including more than 3.6 million in IPC Emergency conditions.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Acute food insecurity remains extremely large.

source_refs.locator: heading and first two paragraphs, 13 May 2026. (World Food Programme1)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Multi-causal humanitarian outcome; not evidence of climate attribution.

evidence_records.statement: The same May 2026 FAO/WFP update reported more than 7.8 million IDPs and identified conflict-driven livelihood destruction, market disruption and restricted farmland access in North/South Kivu, Ituri and Tanganyika.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Conflict displacement directly reduces livelihood and market access.

source_refs.locator: paragraphs following headline, especially paras 3-5. (World Food Programme1)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Does not establish how much food insecurity is climate-driven.

evidence_records.statement: As of June 2026, IMF reporting continued to describe the security situation in eastern DRC as volatile, with severe displacement and food insecurity.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Eastern FCV conditions remained an active delivery constraint in mid-2026.

source_refs.locator: bullet list and opening programme-review paragraphs. (IMF8)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Macro/programme source; not granular enough for territorial access conditions.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI finds that climate-security risks in North and South Kivu are conditioned by governance and access to land and water, especially where resource access is already disputed.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Resource governance mediates climate-related conflict risk.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Qualitative synthesis; does not establish a national average causal effect.

evidence_records.statement: In the Ruzizi Plain, FBA/SIPRI sources report that drought/pasture and water pressures alter livestock movement and interact with existing farmer-pastoralist and identity disputes.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate stress may intensify existing Ruzizi resource conflicts through mobility.

source_refs.locator: report p.10, “Security risks related to natural resource scarcity”

evidence_records.uncertainty: Local qualitative evidence; alternative explanations include land tenure, ethnicity, political mobilization and historical conflict.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI documents that insecurity, armed-group control and blocked routes can restrict farmland access and food supply chains, weakening livelihoods and increasing vulnerability to later climate shocks.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Conflict can erode adaptive capacity by blocking land, markets and services.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Qualitative; magnitude is not quantified.

evidence_records.statement: Specialist evidence links armed-group and elite exploitation of forests and minerals in eastern DRC to environmental degradation and weakened resource governance.
evidence_records.compact_statement: FCV-related extraction can undermine environmental governance and resilience.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Extraction/degradation is an independent environmental/FCV driver, not automatically a climate impact.

evidence_records.statement: The revised NDC sets a 2030 GHG reduction target of 21% below BAU, comprising 19% conditional and 2% unconditional action.
evidence_records.compact_statement: DRC's revised 2030 mitigation target is mostly conditional.

source_refs.locator: PDF/printed p.9, “Processus de révision de la CDN.”

evidence_records.uncertainty: Commitment/target, not an achieved reduction.

evidence_records.statement: The revised NDC estimates USD 23.08 billion for priority adaptation measures within its overall USD 48.68 billion budget.
evidence_records.compact_statement: NDC adaptation ambition carries very large financing requirements.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Financing requirement is not secured finance or delivered adaptation.

evidence_records.statement: IMF staff reported that authorities expected only around 2% of NDC investment requirements to be covered by budget resources and stated that, as of 2024, no significant NDC implementation progress had yet been made.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Financing and implementation gaps constrain national climate ambition.
evidence_records.uncertainty: “No significant progress” is reported by authorities through IMF staff, not an independent outcome evaluation.

evidence_records.statement: UNDP's independent evaluation found that national and institutional frameworks for climate mitigation/adaptation and natural-resource management had been strengthened, including forest monitoring and support to NDC/REDD+ processes.
evidence_records.compact_statement: National climate-policy enabling systems improved.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Evaluates UNDP contribution, not the effectiveness of the entire national climate system.

evidence_records.statement: The same evaluation found mixed decentralized natural-resource-governance performance, with delays and insufficient local engagement/ownership threatening some land-use and community-forestry processes.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Stronger national frameworks have not consistently translated into local implementation.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Applies to evaluated interventions, not every province or institution.

evidence_records.statement: UNDP's independent evaluation found that several climate-resilience project achievements were not sustained; it recorded problems including an early-warning system that remained non-functional and deterioration/technical shortcomings in coastal-protection infrastructure.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Evaluated adaptation assets showed sustainability and operationalization failures.

source_refs.locator: Finding 15, PDF p.52/report p.42 and continuation.

evidence_records.uncertainty: Limited programme sample; cannot characterize all DRC adaptation programmes.

evidence_records.statement: In the first World Bank ISR, the Urban Flood Resilience Project had 0 current beneficiaries from climate-resilient infrastructure, 0 beneficiaries from early-warning services and 0 completed key DRM instruments as of 15 Aug. 2025, while 26 people had been trained by September.
evidence_records.compact_statement: New urban flood programme was still at an early output stage in 2025.

source_refs.locator: PDF p.3 §6.1 and p.4 intermediate indicators. (World Bank6)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Zero early indicators do not imply project failure; project only became effective in July 2025.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI documents women- and youth-led initiatives in eastern DRC involving peace committees, social cohesion, forest restoration, climate justice, sustainable agriculture and conservation.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Local women and youth provide climate/peace resilience capacity.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Examples are illustrative rather than a representative inventory or impact evaluation.

evidence_records.statement: FBA's eastern DRC workshop identified customary/traditional authorities and local governance systems as potentially important for managing climate stresses and planning adaptation, while noting institutional weakness.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Customary/local institutions can be resilience assets but are uneven.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Workshop evidence; customary authority roles can also be contested and should not be assumed uniformly positive.

evidence_records.statement: FAO/WFP stated in May 2026 that humanitarian assistance remained critically below needs and emphasized safe, sustained access alongside longer-term livelihood support.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Delivery shortfalls constrain both emergency coping and recovery.

source_refs.locator: paragraphs on humanitarian shortfall and dual response. (World Food Programme1)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Agency operational statement; not a comparative effectiveness evaluation.

evidence_records.statement: Ethiopia’s national mean temperature increased by about 1°C since the 1960s.
evidence_records.compact_statement: ~1°C observed warming since 1960s.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Government synthesis; national average masks spatial differences.

evidence_records.statement: Annual rainfall is highly variable; the NDC gives annual variation around mean rainfall of about 25%, reaching 50% in some areas.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Rainfall variability is large and spatially uneven.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Metric is NDC synthesis; local trends differ.

evidence_records.statement: Under CMIP6 projections used by the CCDR, extreme heat rises most in hotter northern/eastern Ethiopia, with about 40 additional extreme-heat days projected in Afar.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Afar faces large projected heat-day increase.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Magnitude depends on model/scenario/horizon definitions.

evidence_records.statement: Heavy-rainfall intensity is projected to rise, increasing flood risk, while consecutive dry days may rise slightly mainly in drier zones.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Flood intensity risk rises; dry-day change is spatially uneven.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Mean precipitation direction remains uncertain.

evidence_records.statement: Average annual exposure is estimated at about 5 million people for drought and 0.25 million for flooding.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Large recurring drought/flood exposure.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Estimates derive from referenced hazard datasets, not contemporaneous census exposure.

evidence_records.statement: Pastoralists’ communal land-use rights in lowlands remain weakly recognized and largely unregistered, which can jeopardize access to dry-season grazing and water and increase climate vulnerability.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Tenure insecurity can amplify pastoral climate vulnerability.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Mechanism is analytically plausible and explicitly stated by CCDR; extent varies locally.

evidence_records.statement: Informal settlements are estimated to cover 74% of urban areas, and vulnerable residents in flood-runoff/wetland/hazard locations face elevated climate-event and service-access risks.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Informality concentrates urban hazard/service vulnerability.
evidence_records.uncertainty: 74% estimate comes from cited secondary source; not uniform across cities.

evidence_records.statement: WFP’s 2026 emergency page describes food insecurity as simultaneously driven by displacement, insecurity, drought risk and high food prices.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Current food crisis is explicitly multi-causal.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Humanitarian operational assessment, not causal decomposition.

evidence_records.statement: Insecurity in Amhara creates direct risks for WFP/partners and raises operating costs.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Conflict constrains humanitarian delivery.

source_refs.locator: webpage “Ethiopia,” paragraph following headline indicators. (World Food Programme8)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Supports delivery constraint, not a quantified adaptation-effect size.

evidence_records.statement: A World Bank survey in pastoral/agropastoral communities found each day with a violent conflict event associated with >12% higher food poverty.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Conflict exposure is associated with sharply higher food poverty.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Observational association; underlying study cited as a World Bank assessment/project concept.

evidence_records.statement: Climate-risk research reproduced by the CCDR finds an association between extreme-heat exposure, food insecurity and subsequent conflict risk at woreda level.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Heat-food insecurity-conflict link is correlational.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Original detailed study file not fully fetched; association does not establish causality.

evidence_records.statement: In Somali Region case-study sites, drought coping through changing pastoral mobility has produced competition over water/pasture and intercommunal conflict in some instances.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Drought-related mobility can mediate local resource conflict.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Local qualitative finding; not nationally generalizable and drought is not sole conflict driver.

evidence_records.statement: The NDC prioritized 40 adaptation interventions with a 2018 baseline and 2030 targets/indicators.
evidence_records.compact_statement: National adaptation architecture has 40 targeted interventions.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Policy commitments are not evidence of realized outcomes.

evidence_records.statement: The 2025 government stocktake found that 31 of 41 NDC adaptation indicators - nearly 66% - had not been tracked.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Most sampled adaptation indicators lacked tracking.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Government stocktake; absence of tracking does not mean absence of implementation.

evidence_records.statement: Regional and woreda strategic capacity for climate action is assessed as very low, with limited finance and insufficiently assigned subnational roles.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Local climate implementation capacity is weak.
evidence_records.uncertainty: National-level synthesis; capability varies between jurisdictions.

evidence_records.statement: Ethiopia has functional climate-related early-warning systems managed from woreda upward.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Early-warning capacity exists across government levels.
evidence_records.uncertainty: “Functional” does not establish universal coverage, forecast skill or effective last-mile response.

evidence_records.statement: The 2025 stocktake found implementation and tracking varied substantially between ministries, with few interventions progressing as planned and the status of most interventions unknown.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Adaptation implementation evidence is incomplete and uneven.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Government self-stocktake rather than independent evaluation.

evidence_records.statement: IEG found statistically significant land-restoration effects from Ethiopian SLM interventions compared with controls in high-pressure highland watersheds.
evidence_records.compact_statement: SLM produced measured land-restoration gains.

source_refs.locator: underlying IEG analysis, Chapter 4, Table 4.2. (Independent Evaluation Group13)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Evaluated watersheds are not representative of all Ethiopia.

evidence_records.statement: IEG found that area closures can increase vulnerability where restrictions on grazing mobility are not compensated by adequate fodder or alternative access.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Restoration can create livelihood trade-offs.

source_refs.locator: underlying IEG analysis, Chapter 4, “Land Area Closures and Fencing.” (Independent Evaluation Group13)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Effect depends on design and local socioecological system.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI found mixed evidence that SIIPE drought insurance could reduce drought-driven mobility and thereby lower intercommunal conflict risk.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Insurance may support peace through reduced distress mobility, but evidence is mixed.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Theory of change not consistently realized; severe drought still drove movement.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI found that programme targeting/exclusion could generate resentment and recommended clearer criteria, feedback channels and conflict analysis.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Poor targeting transparency can create programme-related tension.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Respondents also reported settings without beneficiary/non-beneficiary tension; effect is conditional.

evidence_records.statement: WFP reports that IFTIIN supports 17,000 pastoral/agropastoral families across multiple Somali Region woredas through solar irrigation and related resilience measures.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Recent lowland programme has substantial stated reach.

source_refs.locator: webpage paragraphs under headline. (World Food Programme12)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Beneficiary reach and outputs are programme reporting, not independent impact estimates.

evidence_records.statement: An older World Bank-GFDRR profile reports observed warming since 1960 and projects further warming, more hot days and nights, uncertain rainfall outside a drier June-August signal, and sea-level rise exposure for Haiti.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Haiti faces rising heat, uncertain seasonal rainfall, and sea-level pressures.
evidence_records.scenario: Older AR4-era national and Caribbean projections to 2060 and 2090

source_refs.locator: p. 4, sections 'Climate baseline summary for Haiti' and 'Climate future'

evidence_records.uncertainty: The direction of warming is robust, but the profile uses older models and partly regional precipitation and sea-level evidence.

evidence_records.statement: The World Bank climate-health assessment identifies Atlantic hurricane exposure, low-lying coastal plains, heavy rainfall, periodic drought, and repeated flood and storm events as major hazards affecting Haiti.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Cyclone, flood, drought, and coastal exposure is nationally material but spatially uneven.
evidence_records.ecological_level: coastal plains, watersheds, and urban valleys
institutions: Ministry of Public Health and Population
evidence_records.uncertainty: National event counts combine hazards and periods and do not establish local exposure or climate attribution for each event.

evidence_records.statement: Haiti's National Adaptation Plan sets a 2022-2030 framework covering agriculture, health, infrastructure, and water, with municipal capacity, governance, costing, resource mobilization, and monitoring as stated priorities.
evidence_records.compact_statement: The national plan defines sector and municipal adaptation responsibilities but not delivered outcomes.

source_refs.locator: p. 16, executive summary description of the 2022-2030 plan, priority actions, governance, cost, and monitoring

evidence_records.uncertainty: Plan adoption demonstrates institutional intent, not financing, implementation quality, municipal reach, or effectiveness.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI and NUPI assess that climate change is rarely a main conflict driver in Haiti but can interact with livelihoods, mobility, armed actors, and political-economic grievances, while violence and instability weaken community resilience.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate-security risks are mediated and bidirectional, not deterministic.

source_refs.locator: pp. 2-4, sections 'Climate-related peace and security risks', 'Livelihood impacts', 'Migration and mobility', and 'Political and economic grievances'

evidence_records.uncertainty: The specialist synthesis organizes plausible and documented mechanisms but does not estimate causal effects or show uniform operation across Haiti.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI reports that most Haitian agriculture is rainfed and that drought, irregular rainfall, soil and water stress interact with insecurity and economic crisis to threaten production and food security.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Rainfed dependence creates food and livelihood sensitivity to interacting climate and security shocks.

source_refs.locator: pp. 2-3, sections 'Livelihood impacts' and discussion of rainfed agriculture, drought, food insecurity, and insecurity
country context and outcomes 1-3 on acute food insecurity and climate-related shocks

evidence_records.uncertainty: The sources do not allocate observed food insecurity among climate, violence, prices, poverty, and other drivers.

evidence_records.statement: The climate-health assessment and SIPRI synthesis link heavy rainfall and flooding with water- and vector-borne disease risks where waste management, safe water, sanitation, and health systems are inadequate.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Flood and rainfall health risks rise where WASH and health systems are weak.
institutions: Ministry of Public Health and Population

source_refs.locator: p. 2, lines discussing precipitation, flooding, water-borne and vector-borne disease and inadequate waste management
sections II-IV on climate-sensitive disease burdens and health-system adaptive capacity

evidence_records.uncertainty: Disease transmission is multi-causal and the sources do not estimate the attributable climate share for particular outbreaks.

evidence_records.statement: UN reporting documents gang violence as a primary driver of mass displacement, restricted movement, complicated humanitarian access, school closure, and loss of basic services, with women and children disproportionately affected.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Armed violence drives displacement and sharply restricts services and humanitarian access.

source_refs.locator: paragraphs under 'Mass displacement' and 'Impact on children and women'

evidence_records.uncertainty: Reported totals are time-specific and the page does not quantify how displacement changes exposure to each climate hazard.

evidence_records.statement: UNICEF and ICRC report that armed violence interrupts clinics, supply chains, water, health, and transport services and forces humanitarian operations to adapt or suspend delivery in affected areas.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Violence erodes the service and access systems needed to absorb climate and health shocks.
institutions: International Committee of the Red Cross

source_refs.locator: pp. 1-2, highlights and situation overview on suspended clinics, non-functional health centres, displacement, and access
sections 'Access to health and emergency services' and 'Improving living conditions for residents and displaced persons'

evidence_records.uncertainty: Operational reporting documents disruption and response but not the additional losses during a specific climate shock.

evidence_records.statement: UN reporting finds that displaced households often live with overstretched host families or in crowded, high-risk sites lacking adequate food, water, sanitation, shelter, and medical care.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Conflict displacement concentrates people in sites and communities with high hazard sensitivity.

source_refs.locator: section 'Mass displacement', paragraphs on host families, high-risk sites, and service shortages
p. 2, situation overview on displacement sites, host families, food insecurity, cholera, and health services

evidence_records.uncertainty: Site and host-family conditions vary, and the reports do not map exposure to specific flood, heat, or cyclone return periods.

evidence_records.statement: WFP's independent country-plan evaluation found that the portfolio adapted to a difficult context and reached many people, but contextual and funding constraints kept it focused on emergency assistance and impeded intended integration and resilience shifts.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Independent evaluation found adaptive delivery alongside constrained resilience transition.

source_refs.locator: evaluation webpage conclusions on adaptation, reach, contextual and funding constraints, and the impeded shift from emergency response

evidence_records.uncertainty: The evaluation covers WFP activities only through July 2022 and does not isolate climate-specific or peace outcomes.

evidence_records.statement: A World Bank results brief reports expansion of certified Municipal Civil Protection Committees to all 140 municipalities, training of volunteers, national DRM reforms, and use of strengthened systems during the 2021 earthquake response.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Municipal civil-protection structures provide a nationwide disaster-response platform.
institutions: Ministry of Public Works, Transport and Communication

source_refs.locator: sections 'Improving disaster response capacity' and 'Enhancing the resiliency of critical transport infrastructure'

evidence_records.uncertainty: The implementing institution reports outputs and performance classifications; it does not independently measure current readiness or climate-shock outcomes.

evidence_records.statement: Haiti's adaptation plan prioritizes climate-smart agriculture, irrigation, integrated water management, reforestation, watershed management, capacity building, and disease prevention among its highest-priority actions.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Planned cross-sector actions target watershed, food, water, health, and municipal resilience.

source_refs.locator: p. 16, executive summary list of 21 highest-priority adaptation actions and estimated implementation budget

evidence_records.uncertainty: Prioritization and costing do not demonstrate financing, equitable implementation, maintenance, or outcomes.

evidence_records.statement: WFP's 2024-2028 plan intends to link emergency assistance with safety nets, livelihood opportunities, home-grown school feeding, climate resilience, national systems, and humanitarian logistics.
evidence_records.compact_statement: The current WFP plan provides intended adaptive and delivery capacity across food systems and safety nets.
evidence_records.uncertainty: The record describes intended outcomes; implementation, coverage, distributional effects, and resilience results are not yet independently evaluated.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI documents a Haiti Climate Security Group and recommends climate-resilient livelihood options, integrated dialogue, and a national climate-security policy, while not demonstrating that these mechanisms have produced peace outcomes.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Emerging climate-security coordination offers a potential resilience and peace platform.

source_refs.locator: pp. 1 and 4, recommendations on reintegration, dialogue, the Haiti Climate Security Group, and national climate-security policy

evidence_records.uncertainty: The source documents coordination and recommendations rather than adoption, reach, or measured climate-resilience and peace outcomes.

evidence_records.statement: The World Bank's 2022 diagnostic identifies chronic fragility, weak and uneven state capacity, recurrent crises, and limited shock-responsive social protection and service systems as structural constraints on inclusive recovery.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Chronic institutional weakness limits equitable shock response and recovery.

source_refs.locator: executive summary and sections on recurrent crises, chronic fragility, service delivery, disaster risk management, and shock-responsive social protection

evidence_records.uncertainty: The structural diagnostic predates the latest violence and does not quantify conflict's additional effect on climate losses or adaptation outcomes.

evidence_records.statement: WWA estimated the 2021-2025 five-year Iranian SPEI-60 drought at about a 1-in-5-year event in the present climate versus roughly 1-in-250 in a 1.3°C cooler climate.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Warming strongly increased multi-year drought likelihood.

source_refs.locator: “Results,” Table 1 discussion, paras. beginning “However, the Probability Ratios…” (World Weather Attribution)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Rapid attribution study rather than long-form peer-reviewed event paper; uncertainty ranges remain material.

evidence_records.statement: WWA estimated five-year rainfall totals in Iran during 2021-2025 as approximately a 1-in-25-year low-rainfall event, but attribution uncertainty encompassed no change.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Rainfall attribution is weaker than drought/evaporative attribution.

source_refs.locator: “Results: Trends in rainfall totals,” paras. 2-5 (World Weather Attribution)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Does not support a confident quantitative claim that climate change caused the rainfall deficit.

evidence_records.statement: Iran's 2015 INDC projected mean temperature to rise by more than 1.5°C and surface runoff to fall 25% by 2030.
evidence_records.compact_statement: National policy projected hotter conditions and lower runoff.

source_refs.locator: §3 “Adaptation and Vulnerability,” Vulnerability, para. beginning “It is predicted…” (Asia Pacific Energy Policy)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Government policy projection; model/scenario not identified in accessible text.

evidence_records.statement: World Bank WDI reports annual freshwater withdrawals equal to 72% of internal renewable water resources in 2022.
evidence_records.compact_statement: National freshwater withdrawals are high relative to internal resources.

source_refs.locator: Environment indicator “Annual freshwater withdrawals, total (% of internal resources)” (World Bank Open Data)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Indicator is not equivalent to agriculture's share of withdrawals or consumption.

evidence_records.statement: A nationwide study estimated approximately 74 km³ of groundwater depletion during 2002-2015.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Groundwater depletion is large and long-running.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Historical period; spatial rates vary substantially.

evidence_records.statement: The same study found extreme groundwater overdraft over roughly 77% of national land area and concluded human withdrawals were the principal basin-scale cause, although meteorological/hydrological drought intensified depletion.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Human withdrawals dominate groundwater depletion.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Strong evidence against a climate-only explanation; does not itself attribute governance decisions.

evidence_records.statement: In six rural Isfahan districts, researchers using 266 household surveys and key-informant interviews identified poor water governance as the leading cause of local water scarcity.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Local scarcity was primarily governance-related.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Local study; “leading cause” reflects this study's design and setting.

evidence_records.statement: The Isfahan study found three formerly river-connected districts more vulnerable than three without direct river access, with vulnerability scores 0.35-0.44 versus 0.19-0.23.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Rural vulnerability differs markedly within one basin.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Index depends on study methodology; not nationally representative.

evidence_records.statement: A ZayandehRud Basin study used meteorological data and a random survey of 301 farmers and found differing upstream/downstream perceptions of climate, water crisis and conflict.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate-water-conflict perceptions vary across basin users.

source_refs.locator: Abstract, “Study focus” and “New hydrological insights” (Directory of Open Access Journals)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Survey/perception evidence; does not independently establish causal violence effects.

evidence_records.statement: ZayandehRud farmers reported that worsening water insecurity intersected with perceived injustice and disputes between sub-basins and agricultural, industrial, municipal and environmental users.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Allocation and injustice mediate local climate-water tensions.

source_refs.locator: Abstract, final two findings paragraphs (Directory of Open Access Journals)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Causality is partly perception-based; governance and allocation are independent drivers.

evidence_records.statement: WWA describes Iran's current water crisis as jointly arising from repeated drought, increasing evaporative demand, water-intensive agriculture and unsustainable groundwater extraction.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate and demand pressures compound one another.

source_refs.locator: “Key Messages,” first two bullets (World Weather Attribution)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Rapid synthesis; component mechanisms stronger than exact national attribution shares.

evidence_records.statement: WWA reports farmers as particularly exposed because irrigation-dependent income, higher input costs and limited livelihood alternatives reduce adaptive capacity and may contribute to urban migration.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Irrigation-dependent livelihoods have limited coping options.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Migration mechanism is synthesized, not established through a dedicated Iran causal migration study here.

evidence_records.statement: Iran's INDC states that sanctions and financial/technological restrictions constrain capacity development and institutional structures for climate action.
evidence_records.compact_statement: External restrictions can constrain adaptation capacity.

source_refs.locator: §1, paras. on restrictions and institutional capacity (Asia Pacific Energy Policy)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Government position; no independent quantitative estimate of the effect.

evidence_records.statement: Iran's current FAO portfolio includes a US$3 million National Adaptation Plan project for priority sectors for 2025-2028.
evidence_records.compact_statement: A national adaptation planning process is funded and under implementation.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Presence of a project does not demonstrate successful adaptation.

evidence_records.statement: FAO launched a 2025 climate-resilient agriculture initiative using drought-tolerant crops, good agricultural practices, participatory varietal selection and farmer field schools.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate-smart agricultural capacity is being developed.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Outcomes remain prospective.

evidence_records.statement: UNDP's May 2025 wetland programme factsheet reports an average 27.7% reduction in irrigation water use and approximately 22.5% increase in crop yields among participating pilot-site farmers.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Pilot sites report water savings with higher yields.

source_refs.locator: PDF p.3, “Results to Date - Impact on local farming and agriculture” (UNDP)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Implementer-reported, no verified counterfactual or independent impact evaluation.

evidence_records.statement: UNDP reports formal collaboration among environmental, agricultural, community and private-sector actors through integrated wetland-management structures.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Cross-sector wetland institutions exist in project areas.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Institutionalization is programme-reported; durability not independently evaluated.

evidence_records.statement: UNDP reports participatory wetland approaches rolled out across 25 provinces and 38 wetlands, with local committees and national wetland-management arrangements.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Participatory environmental governance has been scaled geographically.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Scale does not prove effectiveness or equitable participation.

evidence_records.statement: UNDP reports more than 700 rural women involved in green jobs in its Lake Urmia-related programme.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Some adaptation programming explicitly includes women's livelihoods.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Beneficiary/output measure; no evidence here of sustained income or reduced vulnerability.

evidence_records.statement: A UNDP terminal evaluation consultancy for the 2021-2024 Lake Urmia and other wetlands component was publicly procured in 2023.
evidence_records.compact_statement: An independent-style terminal evaluation was commissioned.
evidence_records.uncertainty: The final report and findings were not located/verified; procurement is not evidence of effectiveness.

evidence_records.statement: The World Bank reports that conflict, sanctions and social unrest have disrupted Iranian economic activity and that damaged infrastructure and water/energy shortages constrain non-oil growth.
evidence_records.compact_statement: FCV/economic conditions coincide with infrastructure and utility constraints.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Does not decompose how much disruption is attributable to each factor.

evidence_records.statement: The World Bank expects high food inflation, import shortages and conflict-related shocks to increase poverty.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Current FCV/economic shocks heighten household sensitivity.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Forward-looking World Bank assessment, not observed poverty outcome.

evidence_records.statement: As of end-2025, UNHCR's situation portal recorded about 1.638 million Afghan refugees/other Afghans in need of international protection in Iran.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Iran hosts a large protection-sensitive Afghan population.

source_refs.locator: “Afghan refugees and other Afghans in need of international protection” table (UNHCR Data Portal)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Not climate-attributed; administrative categories and estimates may change.

evidence_records.statement: UNHCR/IOM data recorded 426,700 returns from Iran to Afghanistan during 2026 through 1 August, including 351,700 deportations.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Cross-border mobility changed rapidly in 2026.

source_refs.locator: “Total Returns … by country” and “Deportations … by country” (UNHCR Data Portal)

evidence_records.uncertainty: This is an FCV/mobility condition, not evidence that climate caused return or deportation.

evidence_records.statement: ECMWF/ERA data for 1980-2020 show rising annual mean temperatures in Iraq, particularly in the north.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Iraq has an observed warming trend, strongest in the north.
evidence_records.uncertainty: National communication using established reanalysis; does not attribute the entire trend to anthropogenic climate change.

evidence_records.statement: Using 21 NEX-GDDP GCMs, Iraq's national assessment projects roughly 2.5°C end-century warming in Anbar, Salah al-Din and Baghdad under RCP4.5 and up to 6.5°C in Duhok under RCP8.5.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Substantial end-century warming is projected under both scenarios.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Scenario and model uncertainty remain; RCP8.5 is a high-emissions pathway.

evidence_records.statement: The same national assessment projects an approximately 150 mm decline in precipitation in Duhok by century-end under RCP8.5.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Northern precipitation decline is projected under high emissions.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Precipitation is less robust than temperature; other scenarios/locations differ.

evidence_records.statement: For the Southern Mesopotamian Plain, models project 3-5°C warming by century-end but no statistically significant trend in annual precipitation under RCP4.5 or RCP8.5.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Southern Iraq warms strongly without a clear annual-rainfall trend.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Annual precipitation may obscure seasonal/extreme changes.

evidence_records.statement: APSIM modeling for the Southern Mesopotamian Plain indicates wheat yield could fall from about 4.5 to 3 t/ha by century-end under RCP8.5 because of worsening heat and water stress.
evidence_records.compact_statement: High-emissions heat/water stress threatens southern wheat yields.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Model resolution is explicitly insufficient for plot-scale dynamics; not a national yield forecast.

evidence_records.statement: Iraq's projected water deficit is driven jointly by demand growth, upstream withdrawals/dams, domestic management and climate pressures; the national communication states demand would exceed available freshwater by 2035 even without climate change.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Iraq's water deficit is explicitly multi-causal.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Individual contributions of climate versus policy/infrastructure are not separated quantitatively.

evidence_records.statement: As of September 2025, a UN synthesis reported 31,001 families (186,006 people) displaced due to climatic factors in central and southern Iraq; 63% had moved from rural to urban areas.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate-associated displacement is increasingly rural-to-urban.

source_refs.locator: publication text, para. beginning “Water scarcity has had…”. (The United Nations in Iraq)

evidence_records.uncertainty: UN advocacy synthesis; underlying DTM instrument was not independently reproduced here; “climatic factors” is broader than anthropogenic climate attribution.

evidence_records.statement: A 2026 World Bank diagnostic reports 83% access to improved drinking-water sources in 2023 but only 60% of households reporting safe and consistently available water; non-revenue water exceeds 60%, sewerage coverage is below 30%, and over 70% of urban sewage is discharged untreated.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Water-service weakness compounds climate exposure.

source_refs.locator: §Sectoral and Institutional Context, para.6, PDF p.4.

evidence_records.uncertainty: Sector diagnostic aggregates heterogeneous regional conditions.

evidence_records.statement: World Bank modeling estimates 35% of agriculture and construction workers are exposed to extreme heat, with productivity and earnings implications.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Outdoor and manual workers face substantial heat exposure.

source_refs.locator: Special Focus, Fig.19 discussion, PDF p.31. (World Bank)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Model/synthesis estimate; not an occupational cohort evaluation.

evidence_records.statement: World Bank modeling finds a 20% decline in water availability plus higher-temperature crop impacts could reduce medium-term GDP by 3.9%; modeled 10-20% food-price rises would increase poverty by 1.6-4.4 percentage points.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate-water-agriculture shocks can transmit through prices and poverty.

source_refs.locator: Special Focus, Fig.19 discussion, PDF p.31. (World Bank)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Scenario modeling, not observed outcome or causal estimate of conflict.

evidence_records.statement: Iraq's 2025 NDC explicitly calls for meaningful participation by vulnerable communities, youth, women and persons with disabilities and notes disproportionate climate impacts on women and vulnerable rural/ecosystem-dependent populations.
evidence_records.compact_statement: National policy recognizes differentiated vulnerability.

source_refs.locator: PDF p.8 and §Women, Girls and Vulnerable Groups, pp.35-36.

evidence_records.uncertainty: Mostly policy diagnosis; quantitative comparative impact evidence is limited and some statistics require independent validation.

evidence_records.statement: The 2025 NDC calls for Ministry of Environment-Ministry of Planning co-leadership, stronger National Climate Committee capacity and establishment of an NDC implementation unit with workplans, indicators and data systems.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Iraq has a defined national climate-governance architecture.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Existence/planned strengthening of architecture does not demonstrate implementation quality or outcomes.

evidence_records.statement: The Kurdistan Region's 2024 LAP was developed through a participatory technical-working-group process and specifies a future monitoring, review and learning structure with indicators, data collection and periodic evaluation.
evidence_records.compact_statement: KRI has localized adaptation planning and proposed MRL capacity.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Plan-level capacity only; not evidence of achieved resilience; KRI findings cannot be generalized nationally.

evidence_records.statement: World Bank modeling indicates that improving water-use efficiency by 10% or 20% would reduce the modeled GDP loss from the water/temperature shock scenario from 3.9% to 3.1% or 2.4%, respectively.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Water efficiency has modeled adaptation benefits.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Modeled benefit, not evaluated implementation performance.

evidence_records.statement: The approved USD 39 million SRVALI programme is designed for six years in Karbala, Muthanna and Najaf to improve climate-resilient agriculture and water-use efficiency, with close to two million intended rural beneficiaries.
evidence_records.compact_statement: A major targeted adaptation investment is planned in three governorates.

source_refs.locator: paras.7-14 and 22-32. (The United Nations in Iraq)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Financing/design verified; beneficiary and resilience statements are targets, not measured outcomes.

evidence_records.statement: WFP's independent evaluation found unconditional food assistance buffered shocks for vulnerable IDPs/refugees, while ongoing shocks and soaring prices partly offset food-security gains; difficulties demonstrating results and lack of a collective social-protection vision weakened sustainability of newer initiatives.
evidence_records.compact_statement: WFP assistance buffered shocks but sustainability/results evidence was limited.

source_refs.locator: official evaluation page, conclusions bullets. (World Food Programme)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Only official evaluation-page summary was accessible; not specifically a climate-program evaluation.

evidence_records.statement: UNDP's independent evaluation found climate/clean-energy elements within stabilization activities were mostly ad hoc and piecemeal, while critical-infrastructure rehabilitation was delivered at substantial scale and was perceived as facilitating return and strengthening the social contract.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Stabilization delivered infrastructure, but climate integration was weakly systematic.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Independent evaluation, but climate-specific activities were a small part of the evaluated portfolio.

evidence_records.statement: UNAMI states that climate change does not directly cause conflict; hazards can exacerbate tensions where social, economic and political conditions, grievances and poor resource management create pathways to insecurity.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate is a risk multiplier, not a deterministic conflict cause.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Strong causal calibration but primarily qualitative synthesis, not causal identification.

evidence_records.statement: UNAMI reports that environmentally/climate-displaced people commonly move to urban centres with limited services and employment, and documents exclusion and harassment that can increase inter-community tensions.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Displacement can transmit climate stress into urban service and cohesion pressures.

source_refs.locator: Existing analysis, PDF pp.6-7; displacement section pp.12-13.

evidence_records.uncertainty: Relies partly on IOM/Berghof evidence and qualitative cases; conflict consequence is conditional.

evidence_records.statement: In March 2024, a water-access dispute in southeastern Dhi Qar escalated violently, causing fatalities and injuries and requiring national security intervention; UNAMI emphasizes that weapons and political/armed-group affiliations complicate such conflicts.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Water competition has produced localized violence, but climate is only one contributor.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Direct violence observed; complete climate -> violence causal chain is not isolated. Must not be generalized nationally.

evidence_records.statement: UNAMI documents instances where armed groups or affiliates bypass or impede land, water and service regulation, potentially undermining water security, public services and climate adaptation.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Armed-actor political economy can obstruct adaptation.
evidence_records.ecological_level: Muthanna; Missan; Basra and other cited locations

source_refs.locator: §Exploitation of natural resources by armed actors, PDF pp.11-12.

evidence_records.uncertainty: Qualitative/report-based cases; degree of representativeness is unknown.

evidence_records.statement: UNAMI finds that inconsistent assistance and unclear registration/responsibility for climate-displaced people can generate perceived neglect and distrust, with politically contingent assistance leaving people vulnerable to manipulation.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Assistance gaps can turn displacement into a governance/social-cohesion risk.

source_refs.locator: §Limited and politically-motivated assistance for climate displacement, PDF pp.12-14.

evidence_records.uncertainty: Qualitative and partly case-specific; “climate displaced” classification can include environmental factors beyond attribution to climate change.

evidence_records.statement: In Al-Rifai, Berghof respondents reported that water-access conflicts had subsided in a wetter year and that, when disputes occurred, tribal, security and administrative authorities generally resolved them quickly.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Local institutions can contain water-related disputes.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Self-reported local perceptions; cannot establish a general national coping capacity.

evidence_records.statement: UNAMI identifies participatory climate and natural-resource governance as a potential peace-supporting capacity and cites the May 2024 Kirkuk Climate Forum as an example of climate issues creating space for dialogue and collective action.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Inclusive climate governance can create peace-supporting dialogue opportunities.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Evidence supports an entry point/opportunity, not a quantified reduction in violence.

evidence_records.statement: The World Bank projects climate change could reduce Lebanon's water availability by up to 9% by 2040 and up to 50% during the dry season.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Material dry-season water decline projected.
evidence_records.scenario: 2040; emissions scenario not specified in accessible release

source_refs.locator: webpage paragraph beginning “Climate change is projected to decrease water availability…” (World Bank)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Projection is verified in the release, but model/emissions scenario is not specified there.

evidence_records.statement: Climate impacts covered by the CCDR are projected to reduce Lebanon's growth potential by up to 2% annually by 2040.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate may materially constrain growth.

source_refs.locator: paragraph beginning “Climate change in Lebanon…” (World Bank)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Summary figure; accessible release does not expose full modelling assumptions.

evidence_records.statement: The CCDR identifies Lebanon's limited adaptive capacity as having been further weakened by the economic and financial crisis, including through compromised public finances and deteriorating services.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Economic crisis weakens adaptation capacity.

source_refs.locator: paragraphs on readiness/adaptive capacity and public finances (World Bank)

evidence_records.uncertainty: “Adaptive capacity” is a diagnostic assessment, not a single directly measured indicator.

evidence_records.statement: Lebanon's 2025 NAP establishes a 2025-2035 adaptation roadmap covering eight climate-sensitive sectors and cross-cutting governance, finance, data/monitoring and stakeholder engagement.
evidence_records.compact_statement: National adaptation framework now exists.

source_refs.locator: webpage paragraphs under “Lebanon National Adaptation Plan (NAP)” (UNDP)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Existence/design does not demonstrate implementation effectiveness.

evidence_records.statement: Lebanon's NDC 3.0 explicitly identifies continuing gaps in data availability, institutional coordination and financial resources for climate implementation.
evidence_records.compact_statement: NDC records implementation constraints.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Verified on publication page; detailed sector gaps in the underlying PDF were not separately checked.

evidence_records.statement: In Greater Beirut and Mount Lebanon, the World Bank states that private water tankers can cost up to ten times more than public supply alternatives addressed by the SGBWSP.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Informal water provision can impose high household costs.

source_refs.locator: paragraph beginning “The project aims to increase water supply…” (World Bank)

evidence_records.uncertainty: “Up to” figure is a project diagnostic and may vary by place/time.

evidence_records.statement: The World Bank reports that Lebanon's multiple crises have severely obstructed planning, implementation and maintenance of water infrastructure and hindered service sustainability.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Crisis conditions obstruct water-system adaptation.

source_refs.locator: paragraph beginning “Moreover, as a result of the multiple crises…” (World Bank)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Source does not quantify each crisis's separate contribution.

evidence_records.statement: The 2025 RDNA assessed US$6.8 billion in physical damage and US$7.2 billion in economic losses from the conflict over 8 Oct 2023-20 Dec 2024.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Conflict caused major damage/loss independently of climate.

source_refs.locator: RDNA release paragraphs on assessment period and damage/loss totals (World Bank)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Must not be relabelled climate damage; relevance is through reduced resilience/recovery capacity.

evidence_records.statement: LEAP is structured as a US$1 billion scalable recovery framework, with an initial US$250 million World Bank contribution to restore lifeline services and critical infrastructure.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Recovery financing capacity exists but is incomplete.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Financing/design is not evidence that infrastructure has already been restored or made climate-resilient.

evidence_records.statement: UNHCR's portal recorded 889,625 Syrians with active UNHCR records as of 30 Jun 2026, while IOM DTM snapshots recorded 360,132 IDPs and 821,077 returning IDPs in July 2026.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Large, dynamic displacement exposure persists.

source_refs.locator: portal “Total Registered Refugees,” “IDPs in Lebanon,” “Returning IDPs” (UNHCR Data Portal)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Categories and dates differ; figures must not be summed. Syrian registration suspension affects interpretation.

evidence_records.statement: In the April-June 2025 IPC period cited by the FSAS guidance, about 1.17 million Lebanese residents, displaced Syrians and Palestine refugees were in IPC Phase 3+, with conflict, continued displacement and reduced humanitarian food assistance identified as main drivers.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Recent food insecurity was primarily conflict/assistance driven.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Statistic is reproduced in guidance from IPC rather than independently re-analysed here; no climate attribution is claimed.

evidence_records.statement: In Wave 22, 76.0% of respondents reported at least one listed climate-associated exposure; 66.3% reported water shortage and 59.2% excessive heat.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Water shortage and heat dominate perceived exposure.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Self-reported exposure; not observational climate attribution.

evidence_records.statement: Wave 22 respondents reporting climate-related household financial loss were more common in rural than urban areas (45.9% vs 37.3%) and among Syrian than Lebanese respondents (53.5% vs 37.6%).
evidence_records.compact_statement: Reported climate-linked losses are differentiated.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Respondent attribution may conflate climate with wider economic/conflict shocks; report offers plausible mechanisms, not causal estimates.

evidence_records.statement: Wave 22 found 78.8% perceived climate-related issues as increasing strain on basic services and 55.0% perceived them as contributing to tension/conflict.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate-service/tension linkage is widely perceived.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Perception, not causality or measured violence.

evidence_records.statement: The same survey found that attribution of climate pressures to tension was strongly shaped by pre-existing group relations and perceived competition over jobs/resources, with the climate-tension/negative Lebanese-Syrian relation association concentrated in Beirut and the Beqaa.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Existing tensions mediate climate-risk perceptions.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Association and perception; does not show climate independently caused tension or conflict.

evidence_records.statement: 65.9% of Wave 22 respondents reported at least one household coping action; among copers, 60.1% cited using water wisely and 11.0% switching to renewable energy.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Coping is widespread but mostly incremental.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Self-reported coping; does not establish effectiveness or sustainability.

evidence_records.statement: Although 32.6% reported using solar or other renewable power as supplemental electricity, the Wave 22 report interprets much of this uptake as necessity arising from Lebanon's electricity crisis rather than deliberate climate adaptation.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Solar uptake should not automatically be coded as adaptation.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Important attribution caution; some households may still receive adaptation benefits.

evidence_records.statement: UNICEF reports that rehabilitation of a well in one divided North Lebanon community was accompanied by increased dialogue and reduced tension, informing later WASH/social-cohesion pilots.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Water projects may support local cohesion.
evidence_records.ecological_level: North Lebanon, specific community unnamed in executive summary
geographies: specific community unnamed in executive summary
evidence_records.uncertainty: Programme narrative, not counterfactual evaluation; do not generalize beyond the case.

evidence_records.statement: ALEF describes the Bcharreh-Denniyeh dispute as involving contested land/water rights, groundwater recharge and pastoral livelihoods, episodic violence and weak governance; its evidence does not isolate climatic change as the cause.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Local water conflict is governance-mediated, not climate-determined.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Policy note relies materially on secondary sources and advances a strong interpretive argument; national extrapolation is rejected.

evidence_records.statement: FSAS guidance identifies political/sectarian tensions and threat of war as primary drivers of tensions among Lebanese, while competition over low-skilled jobs and service access is identified as a driver of Lebanese-Syrian tensions.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Non-climate political and economic drivers remain central.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Guidance synthesizes prior perception evidence; it is not a causal econometric study.

evidence_records.statement: The independent LHSP evaluation found that concentrating support in selected municipalities could leave neighbouring municipalities feeling excluded and create tensions; it documents one Akkar example and a Bekaa dispute over unequal solar-panel support.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Uneven aid/infrastructure allocation can generate grievances.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Not climate-specific; relevant as an empirically evaluated warning for area-based climate/resilience programming.

evidence_records.statement: The LHSP evaluation found no comprehensive programme-wide reporting and no analysis showing how outputs contributed to outcomes, limiting its ability to determine whether the programme reduced social tensions.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Response effectiveness could not be robustly measured.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Strong evidence of an evaluation gap, not evidence that the intervention failed.

evidence_records.statement: WWA estimated Storm Daniel's extreme rainfall over its Libya analysis region as approximately a 1-in-300 to 1-in-600-year event in the present climate.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Storm Daniel rainfall was exceptionally rare.

source_refs.locator: webpage Key findings, bullets on return period and observed rainfall. (World Weather Attribution)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Return-period estimate depends on datasets and statistical fit; regional event estimate, not every municipality.

evidence_records.statement: WWA estimated human-induced warming may have made the Libya extreme-rainfall event up to about 50 times more likely and up to about 50% more intense, while emphasizing that the uncertainty range includes the possibility of no detectable change.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate attribution exists but is highly uncertain.

source_refs.locator: Key findings, attribution and uncertainty bullets. (World Weather Attribution)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Upper-bound estimate should not be reported without the uncertainty statement; does not attribute total damages to climate change.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI reports a mean annual temperature of about 22.92°C and cites projected warming of approximately 1.42°C by 2060.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Substantial warming is projected.
evidence_records.scenario: 2060; underlying scenario not specified in accessible fact sheet
evidence_records.uncertainty: Secondary synthesis; model ensemble and emissions scenario are not reproduced.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI reports projected mean annual precipitation decline of about 7% by 2050 while heavy-rainfall intensity is expected to increase.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Drier averages can coexist with stronger extremes.
evidence_records.scenario: 2050; scenario not specified in accessible fact sheet
evidence_records.uncertainty: Secondary projection; scenario/model details absent.

evidence_records.statement: UNDP reports that roughly 70% of Libya's population lives along the coast, placing substantial population and assets in areas potentially exposed to sea-level and coastal hazards.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Coastal concentration increases exposure.

source_refs.locator: webpage paragraphs on coastal concentration and climate pressures. (UNDP)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Approximate UNDP figure; exposure is not equivalent to demonstrated damage.

evidence_records.statement: The Derna RDNA summary estimated about 1.5 million people - 22% of Libya's population - were affected in the assessed flood area and nearly 44,800 people were displaced.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Derna flooding generated large-scale exposure and displacement.

source_refs.locator: RDNA findings paragraphs reporting population affected and displacement. (World Bank)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Event-specific; does not establish how much damage is attributable to climate change versus dam/infrastructure/governance factors.

evidence_records.statement: UNICEF documented severe post-Storm-Daniel disruption to WASH and health facilities, including damaged water infrastructure, water shortages and non-functional or partially functional health facilities in affected eastern areas.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Flood damage disrupted basic services.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Immediate post-disaster snapshot; service status changed over time.

evidence_records.statement: UNHCR estimated that about 467,000 Sudanese refugees had arrived in Libya since April 2023 by the time of its October 2025 update.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Sudan's war created major additional displacement exposure in Libya.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Estimate derived from multiple operational sources; not climate displacement.

evidence_records.statement: WFP's 2021-2022 resilience exercise found 7 of 19 assessed livelihood zones were not resilient to climate change, while agricultural access was also constrained by conflict, COVID-19, water and irrigation limitations.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Rural livelihood sensitivity is multi-causal.

source_refs.locator: printed pp. 5-6, agricultural livelihoods and climate-resilience discussion. (The United Nations in Libya)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Older evidence and mixed causal drivers; cannot be generalized to every rural area.

evidence_records.statement: The World Bank reports persistent weakness and regional disparities in health, education, water and electricity service delivery amid institutional fragmentation.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Weak basic services increase shock sensitivity.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Macro synthesis; does not quantify climate-specific service impacts.

evidence_records.statement: The independent UNDP evaluation found a fragmented institutional landscape, weak coordination and limited technical capacity, and reported that by mid-2025 no finalized/endorsed NDC or comprehensive national adaptation/mitigation framework had resulted from the evaluated work.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Core climate-governance frameworks remained incomplete in 2025.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Predates 2026 drought/water strategies and later NDC-development progress.

evidence_records.statement: Although the evaluated programme trained local actors in local climate action planning, the independent evaluation found no local climate action plans had subsequently been developed and implemented through that activity.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Training did not yet translate into implemented local plans.

source_refs.locator: printed p. 65, local climate action plan finding.

evidence_records.uncertainty: Applies to the evaluated intervention, not every local climate initiative in Libya.

evidence_records.statement: Libya's National Drought Management Strategy and Action Plan, published in January 2026, sets out a ten-year, multi-sector framework for integrated drought management.
evidence_records.compact_statement: A national drought-planning framework now exists.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Existence of strategy does not demonstrate implementation or outcome effectiveness.

evidence_records.statement: The 2050 National Water Security Strategy was officially endorsed in April 2026; the launch source reports that over 90% of current water supply relies on non-renewable groundwater and sets goals including lower consumption, reduced groundwater dependence and network losses below 25%.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Water strategy targets structural scarcity and system losses.

source_refs.locator: launch page, endorsement and five core pillars/targets paragraphs. (UNDP)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Targets are prospective and not evidence that outcomes have been achieved.

evidence_records.statement: UN reporting in June 2026 stated that approximately 642,600 people had been reached with more reliable climate-resilient water systems, including 40 solar-powered pumping or treatment installations, and that local technicians had been trained.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Recent programmes expanded reported local water-service capacity.
evidence_records.ecological_level: Named Libyan municipalities, especially southern/western sites

source_refs.locator: webpage water security section. (The United Nations in Libya)

evidence_records.uncertainty: UN programme-reported outputs/reach; no independent outcome or durability assessment.

evidence_records.statement: The independent UNDP evaluation reported approximately 71% delivery by June 2025, about US$1.3 million in unspent EU funds, weaknesses in outcome-focused monitoring and an implementation window judged overly ambitious.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Independent evaluation found significant delivery and M&E limitations.
evidence_records.uncertainty: One programme only; not an evaluation of all Libyan climate policy.

evidence_records.statement: WWA found that conflict and state fragility contributed to deteriorating infrastructure and inadequate dam maintenance and constrained adaptation planning and disaster coordination before the Derna catastrophe.
evidence_records.compact_statement: FCV conditions magnified disaster vulnerability.

source_refs.locator: Key findings, bullets on dam failure, maintenance, fragility and warnings. (World Weather Attribution)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Qualitative causal mechanism for vulnerability; does not quantify how much loss each governance factor caused.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI assesses that climate- and water-related livelihood pressures may increase risks of grievances or intercommunal tensions, while stressing that climate is rarely the principal driver of conflict in Libya.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate-livelihood stress is a conditional conflict-risk factor.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 2, “Climate and peace and security.” (SIPRI)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Expert synthesis; does not demonstrate a national causal effect of climate on violence.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI documents Fezzan examples in which perceived inequity in Great Man-Made River water management contributed to contestation and interference with pumps.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Water governance can mediate local grievance and disruption.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Local example; water shortage also reflects non-climatic governance and hydrological factors.

evidence_records.statement: The same SIPRI assessment records that shared reliance on water infrastructure has also generated cooperation among communities and armed actors in maintaining access.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Shared water dependence can create cooperation incentives.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Local qualitative evidence; persistence and scalability of cooperation are not evaluated.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI reports that about 25% of migrants in an IOM sample had experienced a climate shock or stressor in the year before migrating, while the fact sheet treats migration as multi-causal.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate exposure appears in some migrants' histories but does not establish climate-caused migration.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Sample-based association; no causal identification and not representative of every migrant.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI reports that fragmentation, checkpoints and security competition impeded aspects of the Derna response and that migrants/refugees experienced exclusion or discrimination in parts of the recovery environment.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Fragmented security governance can obstruct inclusive disaster recovery.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Qualitative synthesis; extent and duration of exclusion vary.

evidence_records.statement: The World Bank identifies institutional fragmentation and hydrocarbon dependence as central structural constraints and reports continuing regional disparities in public services.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Political-economic structure constrains resilience capacity independently of climate.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Structural context; not itself proof of a climate-FCV causal pathway.

evidence_records.statement: UNICEF's early post-Derna assessment identified women, girls and children among groups facing heightened protection and service risks after the flood and documented substantial education-facility damage.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Disaster impacts were differentiated by age and gender-related vulnerability.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 3-4, gender/protection and education sections.

evidence_records.uncertainty: Humanitarian assessment; differentiated outcomes were not measured comprehensively or longitudinally.

evidence_records.statement: The UNFCCC National Communication registry listed no Libyan National Communication submission in the Libya row when accessed in August 2026.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Formal UNFCCC reporting remains incomplete.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Narrowly indicates absence in this specific registry; does not demonstrate absence of domestic climate studies or strategies.

evidence_records.statement: Mali’s reported average temperature increased from about 28°C in 1950-1980 to about 29.5°C in 2000-2020.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Long-term warming is observed.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Derived by WB from secondary climate sources rather than a new station-data analysis.
