evidence_records.statement: Average annual mean temperature increased by about 1°C between 1960-1991 and 1991-2020.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Historical warming of ~1°C.

source_refs.locator: PDF p.26/84, §1.2.1 “Historical Trends and Future Projections.” (World Bank1)

evidence_records.uncertainty: High: explicit CCDR statistic; aggregation masks local variation.

evidence_records.statement: Average rainfall declined slightly over roughly 50 years and became more volatile; the CCDR estimates about 65% of the West Bank at medium or high flood risk, especially in the northwest.
evidence_records.compact_statement: More variable rain and substantial WB flood exposure.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Flood share is model/assessment based; does not establish annual realized losses.

evidence_records.statement: CCDR SSP projections indicate approximately +2°C by 2055 and +3°C by 2090, with more frequent/intense extremes and worsening drought, especially late-century and in southern areas.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Strong additional warming and drought risk.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Scenario/model uncertainty grows toward 2090; magnitudes are approximate.

evidence_records.statement: Under the CCDR projections, selected Gaza cities receive about +10 mm annual precipitation under SSP1 but roughly −10 mm under higher scenarios; West Bank cities may lose >20 mm under higher scenarios. The report estimates that 10% lower rainfall could reduce aquifer recharge by 14-24%, and 15% lower rainfall by 28-50%.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Rainfall/recharge changes are scenario-sensitive.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Recharge relationship is modelled; city projections should not be generalized to every locality.

evidence_records.statement: The CCDR projects greater water-scarcity risk in Gaza and greater flood risk in eastern parts of the West Bank, demonstrating spatially different climate exposure.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Gaza water risk and eastern WB flood risk differ.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp.27-28/84, §1.2.2 “Climate Change Risks and Vulnerabilities.” (World Bank1)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Relative risks are modelled; present infrastructure conditions in Gaza have since changed substantially.

evidence_records.statement: Mid-century projections indicate very high warm-season maximum temperatures and growing hot-day exposure; the CCDR identifies outdoor workers, older people, young children and people with cardiovascular disease as especially vulnerable.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Heat exposure is differentiated by occupation and health.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Population vulnerability can change; current Gaza living conditions are not represented in the modelling baseline.

evidence_records.statement: The 2021 Updated NDC identifies 12 highly climate-vulnerable sectors and reports implementation action plans for six sectors, with further planning conditional on finance.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate planning covers 12 sectors, unevenly operationalized.
evidence_records.uncertainty: High for documented policy architecture; no inference that plans were implemented effectively.

evidence_records.statement: The NDC sets conditional water adaptation targets including wastewater reuse, rainwater capture, lower non-revenue water, rehabilitation of wells/springs and Gaza desalination capacity.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Water adaptation measures were formally planned.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp.15-16/55, “Water” and “Coastal and marine (Gaza Strip).” (UNFCCC10)

evidence_records.uncertainty: These are targets, not achieved outcomes; the stated Gaza desalination timetable requires current verification.

evidence_records.statement: The Updated NDC estimated total indicative implementation cost for 2021-2040 at about US$5.93bn and an identified funding gap of at least about US$2.74bn, while noting incomplete costing.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Pre-conflict climate-finance gap was already large.
evidence_records.uncertainty: High for 2021 policy estimate; not a current 2026 financing-gap estimate.

evidence_records.statement: The Updated NDC states that restrictions on land/resources, movement, trade, borders and infrastructure reduce Palestinian adaptive capacity, especially in Area C and Gaza.
evidence_records.compact_statement: National policy identifies FCV/access constraints on adaptation.
evidence_records.uncertainty: This is an attributed government policy assessment, not independent causal identification; partially triangulated by CCDR.

evidence_records.statement: Before October 2023, the CCDR documented severe fiscal pressure, EQA staffing shortages, weak coordination and absence of systematic climate-fiscal risk identification/screening.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate institutions had material implementation constraints pre-2023.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Predates current conflict; present capacity cannot be assumed unchanged.

evidence_records.statement: The May 2026 World Bank economic update reports that suspension of clearance revenues since May 2025, financing constraints, arrears and borrowing had left PA fiscal management focused on short-term crisis containment.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Fiscal crisis narrows capacity for longer-term investment.

source_refs.locator: PDF p.8/32 (printed Executive Summary p.2). (The World Bank14)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Directly documents fiscal conditions, but reduced climate expenditure specifically is an inference unless separately budget-traced.

evidence_records.statement: The May 2026 World Bank report estimates that more than 90% of Gaza electricity assets had been damaged and only one 4 MW feeder was operating, serving a desalination plant.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Gaza energy-system destruction constrains WASH and recovery.

source_refs.locator: PDF p.8/32 (printed p.2), Executive Summary “Reliable electricity…”. (The World Bank14)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Conflict impact, not climate impact; system condition may change rapidly.

evidence_records.statement: West Bank electricity imports from Israel declined from 97% to 88% between 2019 and 2025 as solar capacity expanded, although the World Bank estimates substantial further generation/network investment is needed for scale-up.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Solar expansion provides a limited resilience capacity.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Resilience evidence, not evidence of a peace outcome; investment requirement is prospective.

evidence_records.statement: Gaza stakeholders consulted in 2008-2009 identified rainfall variability, heat and sea-level-related water/food pathways, but regarded conflict-related restrictions and recurrent violence as overwhelming or compounding forecast climate risks.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Foundational Gaza study finds conflict mediates climate vulnerability.

source_refs.locator: article pp.287-290, methodology and vulnerability-pathway results. (ResearchGate15)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Qualitative, small stakeholder set, old; key political actors absent; does not demonstrate climate causing violence.

evidence_records.statement: The same Gaza study characterized many coping practices as short-term and reactive and argued that resource, livelihood and institutional constraints impeded transition to longer-term adaptation.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Short-term coping may not build adaptive capacity.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Study interpretation of qualitative evidence; not current and not a quantified outcome evaluation.

evidence_records.statement: Mason et al. (2012) argued from consultations and case evidence that movement/access restrictions and damage or threats to agricultural and water assets constrained some West Bank coping and adaptation options.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Access conditions constrained some WB adaptation options.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Old qualitative/interpretive evidence; local cases must not be nationalized.

evidence_records.statement: The 2025 PLOS scoping review identified interacting Gaza WASH political-economy constraints including restrictions/blockade, institutional fragmentation, internal political divisions, financing, planning, transparency and sustainability problems.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Gaza WASH vulnerability has multiple institutional mediators.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Scoping review synthesizes heterogeneous literature and does not estimate causal effect sizes.

evidence_records.statement: IEG rated the Gaza Water Supply & Sewage System Improvement project outcome Satisfactory; approximately 150,000 beneficiaries obtained more reliable water, but overall water quality improved only marginally, and the wastewater BOD-reduction target was not fully reached.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Historical WASH project achieved mixed but positive results.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Independent evaluation, but dated; endpoint data were imperfect and quality outcome was limited.

evidence_records.statement: IEG found that monitoring systems and rapid damage assessment after the 2014 conflict supported project redesign, additional financing and rehabilitation, but rated risk to development outcome Very High.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Institutional monitoring enabled historical recovery but sustainability was fragile.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Relevant resilience capacity, not evidence it survived 2023-26 destruction; no peace outcome evaluated.

evidence_records.statement: The IEG review recorded access-related supervision constraints and a misprocurement episode; it reported no significant unintended project impacts and rated ICR quality modest.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Evaluation found fiduciary and evidence-quality limitations.
evidence_records.uncertainty: “No significant unintended impacts identified” is not proof of absence; evaluation information was incomplete in places.

evidence_records.statement: The April 2026 RDNA estimates US$35.2bn direct damage, US$22.7bn economic losses and US$71.4bn recovery/reconstruction needs in Gaza; WASH damage is ~US$1.70bn and WASH needs ~US$4.24bn.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Conflict has radically altered Gaza’s asset/service baseline.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp.9-11, “Key Findings,” Table 1. (The United Nations in Palestine2)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Large-scale standardized estimate, but substantial remote assessment and access limitations; figures are not climate-loss estimates.

evidence_records.statement: UNICEF estimated in July 2026 that 82% of Gaza families were water insecure, up to 70% could not access six litres/person/day, and nearly 90% of WASH infrastructure had been damaged or destroyed.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Severe current Gaza water vulnerability is conflict/access driven.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Operational estimate; rapidly changing; not evidence of climate attribution.

evidence_records.statement: IPC classified over 1.2m people, 59% of Gaza’s population, in Crisis or worse during mid-April-June 2026 and projected over 1.4m, 67%, for July-December; IPC states that large-scale assistance after the Oct 2025 ceasefire improved food-security conditions.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Assistance is an important current coping buffer, but food insecurity remains severe.
evidence_records.uncertainty: IPC classification is robust convergence analysis; attribution of improvement to assistance is synthesis rather than experimental causality.

evidence_records.statement: OCHA reported that West Bank WASH damage from demolitions and settler attacks was increasing reliance on emergency water trucking, especially among Bedouin and herding communities; about 160 WASH structures had been affected by settler attacks in 2026 by late July.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Conflict/access pressures reduce water-service resilience in parts of the West Bank.
evidence_records.ecological_level: Area C; Ramallah, Tubas, Jerusalem, Hebron, Bethlehem, Nablus, Jericho and other locations
evidence_records.uncertainty: Humanitarian incident/cluster reporting; no demonstrated climate shock in the cited incidents.

evidence_records.statement: UNICEF estimated that more than 800,000 people in the West Bank required health and WASH assistance, with Area C/Jordan Valley particularly constrained by displacement, movement restrictions and settler violence; >150,000 children faced education barriers.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Vulnerability is geographically and demographically differentiated in the West Bank.
evidence_records.ecological_level: West Bank, especially Area C/Jordan Valley
evidence_records.uncertainty: Operational estimate; does not isolate climate sensitivity from conflict/service constraints.

evidence_records.statement: Taken together, current infrastructure destruction, energy failure, water-service disruption, access constraints and fiscal pressure plausibly reduce practical capacity to implement pre-2023 climate plans and respond to future hazards.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Current FCV conditions likely depress adaptive capacity.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Triangulated inference; no study located quantifies the post-2023 reduction in NAP/NDC implementation capacity.

evidence_records.statement: Projected heat, drought, groundwater-recharge and flood pressures could compound livelihood, health, food and water insecurity where damaged infrastructure, market/access restrictions and weak fiscal/institutional capacity limit coping; the evidence reviewed does not demonstrate that these climate pressures cause violence.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate may compound existing fragility through mediated service/livelihood pathways.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Complete contemporary causal chain has not been demonstrated; current direct Climate-FCV evidence is weak and mostly older qualitative work.

evidence_records.statement: Six Sudan stations over 1961-2010 showed a fairly strong warming trend except Kadugli, which showed slight cooling.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Historical warming at 5/6 NAP stations.

source_refs.locator: PDF p.49, §5.2.3, lines describing six-station record. (UNFCCC1)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Six stations do not capture all local microclimates; record ends 2010.

evidence_records.statement: The same six-station assessment found strong precipitation seasonality, a north-south gradient and interannual variability but no long-term precipitation trend.
evidence_records.compact_statement: No common long-term rainfall trend in NAP station sample.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Does not exclude subnational wetting/drying or changes after 2010.

evidence_records.statement: The NAP used 22 CMIP5 GCMs and RCP2.6/4.5/6.0/8.5, with BCSD downscaling for future scenarios.
evidence_records.compact_statement: NAP projection basis: CMIP5, 22 GCMs, four RCPs.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Method now dated relative to CMIP6.

evidence_records.statement: For Port Sudan, the NAP's ensemble mean indicated warming up to roughly 3°C by 2100, while projected precipitation ranged across both wetter and drier outcomes; the other five stations showed a similar uncertainty pattern.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Warming robust; rainfall direction uncertain.
evidence_records.uncertainty: “Up to 3°C” is a Port Sudan illustration, not a single national warming estimate.

evidence_records.statement: The updated NDC reports increased rainfall variability, lower rainfall, rising temperatures and flood/drought extremes across all 18 states.
evidence_records.compact_statement: NDC reports broad climate pressures nationwide.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Government synthesis; its “lower rainfall” formulation contrasts with NAP's six-station finding of no historical long-term trend.

evidence_records.statement: The NDC reports crop-suitability and yield problems and cites modelling of continuing impacts on major crops and the Kordofan gum-Arabic belt during 2030-2060.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Rainfed crop sensitivity is a national adaptation concern.
evidence_records.uncertainty: NDC does not provide sufficient detail here to independently reproduce every modelling result.

evidence_records.statement: Farmers in Kordofan, Darfur and Gedarif were reported to use dry-season night grazing to reduce livestock heat exposure.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Night grazing is a documented livestock coping practice.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Policy-report evidence; prevalence and effectiveness not independently evaluated.

evidence_records.statement: The NDC states that HCENR was consolidated as the national environmental council under 2020 legal amendments and identifies 12 adaptation priorities costing roughly US$3.85 billion.
evidence_records.compact_statement: National adaptation architecture and priorities exist.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Formal architecture does not establish current operating capacity after war.

evidence_records.statement: The NDC identifies inadequate project preparation, weak state-level adaptation planning, unfinished enabling-environment work and absence of a dedicated NAP M&E system as implementation gaps.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Major adaptation implementation and M&E gaps existed before the war.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp.27-28, planning/financing, enabling environment and M&E subsections. (UNFCCC2)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Predates the additional institutional disruption of the 2023 war.

evidence_records.statement: The 2025 HCENR NAP presentation says national adaptation resources remain insufficient and external finance, technology and capacity-building remain critical.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Adaptation finance/capacity gap persisted into 2025.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Government presentation, not an independent finance-gap assessment.

evidence_records.statement: Adelphi concludes that climate-related changes in natural-resource availability do not directly or automatically produce conflict and identifies marginalization, conflict history and governance failures as independent drivers.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Direct “climate war” causality is unsupported.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Not a causal statistical study itself.

evidence_records.statement: Adelphi identifies resource competition, displacement/livelihood loss and inadequate institutional responses as three mediated routes through which climate/environmental stress can interact with fragility.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Three mediated Climate-FCV mechanisms.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Mechanisms are synthesis, not proof that every link operates in every locality.

evidence_records.statement: NUPI/SIPRI assesses that displacement can sharpen climate vulnerability and that migration changes associated with resource availability may increase local-conflict risks in some locations.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Displacement and mobility can mediate climate-security risk.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Conditional expert synthesis; current mass displacement is overwhelmingly war-related.

evidence_records.statement: CGIAR's pathway analysis identifies livelihood/food-security and resource-access/availability as its two main climate-security pathways.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate-security pathways center on livelihoods and resources.
evidence_records.uncertainty: “Logical mechanisms”; not proof of a complete causal chain.

evidence_records.statement: CGIAR describes earlier or altered pastoral movement and livestock-route pressures as mechanisms that can increase contact and disputes with settled farmers where land/water governance is weak.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Mobility timing can mediate farmer-herder risk.
evidence_records.ecological_level: Darfur; Kordofan; Blue Nile; Kassala examples
evidence_records.uncertainty: Mixes older literature and workshop interpretation; weapons, politics, tenure and conflict history remain independent drivers.

evidence_records.statement: At Al Fashir station, 2000-2024 maximum and minimum temperatures increased, while rainfall showed an increasing trend and a 45.45% coefficient of variation.
evidence_records.compact_statement: North Darfur local record shows warming plus wetter/highly variable rainfall.

source_refs.locator: §3 results, Figures 7-8; paragraph reporting trends. (CMI - Chr. Michelsen Institute10)

evidence_records.uncertainty: One station; reported rainfall trend should not be nationalized.

evidence_records.statement: The North Darfur study concluded that conflict impeded crop yield more than rainfall variability in its 2000-2024 analysis.
evidence_records.compact_statement: In North Darfur, conflict effects on crop yield exceeded rainfall effects in study results.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Observational/local analysis, not an experimental causal estimate.

evidence_records.statement: Surveyed North Darfur households reported migration, asset sales, borrowing, reduced food intake and social support as coping strategies, alongside improved/early-maturing seeds among adaptation practices.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Households combine erosive coping and agronomic adaptation.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Internet-based conflict-period survey; attribution to climate versus conflict is difficult.

evidence_records.statement: UNHCR reported about 9 million people displaced within Sudan and 4.4 million across borders by April 2026.
evidence_records.compact_statement: War has produced massive displacement and exposure.

source_refs.locator: webpage paragraph beginning “Since the war started in April 2023…”. (UNHCR3)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Operational totals are dynamic and rounded.

evidence_records.statement: In May 2026, FAO/WFP/UNICEF estimated around 40% of health facilities were non-functional, 17 million people lacked safe drinking water and 24 million lacked adequate sanitation.
evidence_records.compact_statement: War-era service collapse raises climate sensitivity.

source_refs.locator: webpage paragraph beginning “The destruction of civilian infrastructure…”. (World Food Programme15)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Operational estimates may change; source attributes destruction primarily to conflict.

evidence_records.statement: FAO/WFP reported 14 areas in North Darfur, South Darfur and South Kordofan at risk of Famine through September 2026; about 19.5 million people had faced IPC Phase 3+ through May 2026.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Acute hunger remained extreme in mid-2026.

source_refs.locator: webpage heading “Hotspots of highest concern”, Sudan paragraphs. (World Food Programme14)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Hunger Hotspots identifies armed conflict/violence as primary driver across most hotspots; not a climate-attribution result.

evidence_records.statement: In El Fasher, the IPC FRC identified siege and near-total blockade, with restrictions on goods and destruction of water infrastructure, as the key driver of the 2025 famine finding.
evidence_records.compact_statement: El Fasher famine pathway was conflict/access-driven.

source_refs.locator: PDF p.3, Executive Summary, El Fasher subsection. (IPCinfo5)

evidence_records.uncertainty: FRC used extrapolation and informants because direct access/data were limited.

evidence_records.statement: In Kadugli, the FRC reported that 2025 seasonal rainfall was generally adequate, although delayed, while hostilities disrupted planting and access to supply roads.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Adequate rain did not prevent conflict-driven agricultural failure.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Direct local data were sparse; FRC relied partly on expert judgement.

evidence_records.statement: The 2026 World Bank Thabat project paper says federal institutions cannot be relied upon for implementation because of conflict, while state/local institutions remain more operational.
evidence_records.compact_statement: War shifts delivery toward local/third-party structures.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Project-specific institutional assessment, not comprehensive census of government functionality.

evidence_records.statement: Thabat's World Bank ISR recorded “Satisfactory” progress toward its PDO as of 20 January 2026, while overall project risk remained High and M&E was Moderately Satisfactory.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Current project administration reports continued implementation under high risk.

source_refs.locator: PDF p.6, “Key Information from Last ISR”. (World Bank13)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Administrative implementation rating, not independent impact effectiveness.

evidence_records.statement: A 2021 UNDP/GEF terminal evaluation rated overall project outcomes and effectiveness Satisfactory, implementation/execution Moderately Satisfactory and sustainability Moderately Likely, but financial-resource sustainability Moderately Unlikely.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Pre-war evaluated adaptation showed results but financing vulnerability.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp.3-4, Table 1 Evaluation Rating. (UNDP IEO Evaluation Resource Center11)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Field sample constrained; not representative nationally; no evidence that results survived the current war.

evidence_records.statement: The same evaluation recorded risks including unclear institutional responsibilities, weather-station security and incomplete inclusion of pastoralists in an insurance programme.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Adaptation delivery had institutional and inclusion weaknesses.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp.34-35. (UNDP IEO Evaluation Resource Center11)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Pre-war programme-specific evidence.

evidence_records.statement: Adelphi identifies locally appropriate water infrastructure, water governance and monitoring as potential entry points, noting that water access can become a focal point for community stabilization.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Cooperative water governance is a potential peace-supporting capacity.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Recommended mechanism, not evaluated peace outcome.

evidence_records.statement: NUPI/SIPRI recommends locally owned adaptation, natural-resource conflict management, gender-differentiated responses and participation of women/youth in environmental peacebuilding and early warning.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Local ownership and inclusive governance are identified peace-support capacities.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Recommendations, not demonstrated outcomes; some institutional context is outdated.

evidence_records.statement: Earlier Darfur analysis found that armed conflict itself accelerated environmental degradation and weakened traditional environmental management while political/economic marginalization remained an independent conflict driver.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Conflict can erode ecological/resource-management resilience.

source_refs.locator: article paragraphs beginning “The conflict in Darfur…” and “The debate…”. (Humanitarian Practice Network12)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Old and Darfur-specific; environmental degradation must not itself be assumed to be climate-caused.

evidence_records.statement: Multi-model projections place Somalia’s warming at 1.4-1.9°C by 2030, 1.5-2.3°C by 2050 and 1.4-3.4°C by 2080 relative to pre-industrial conditions, depending on RCP2.6/RCP6.0.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Substantial warming is projected.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Stronger confidence for warming direction than local impacts; older RCP framework.

evidence_records.statement: Long-run precipitation is projected to increase on average, but models show substantial disagreement on magnitude and heavy precipitation while agreeing on high interannual variability.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Rainfall variability is more certain than rainfall magnitude.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Heavy-rainfall/flood projections are highly uncertain.

evidence_records.statement: Median sea level is projected to rise by 36 cm under RCP2.6 and 42 cm under RCP6.0 by 2080 relative to 2000.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Coastal sea level rises under both scenarios.

source_refs.locator: PDF file p.1/19, “Summary - Sea level rise.”

evidence_records.uncertainty: Local coastal inundation and cyclone consequences are not established by this figure.

evidence_records.statement: Severe-to-extreme drought expanded across much of southern Somalia and parts of central Somalia in Jan-Feb 2026, with persistent severe drought in parts of Lower Shabelle, Lower/Middle Juba, Bay and Middle Shabelle in March.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Q1 2026 drought was severe but spatially uneven.

source_refs.locator: PDF file p.1/8, “SWALIM Strengthens Early Warning…,” drought paragraph.

evidence_records.uncertainty: Operational monitoring, not anthropogenic attribution.

evidence_records.statement: Low Shabelle River levels, reduced flows and increased groundwater dependence raised water-access and irrigation concerns in Q1 2026, while mapped river breakages indicated concurrent flood vulnerability along the Juba and Shabelle.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Drought stress and flood exposure can coexist in river systems.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Breakage mapping indicates vulnerability, not realised flood losses.

evidence_records.statement: The 2025 Deyr maize-and-sorghum harvest was about 15,600 tonnes, approximately 75% below the previous five-year average; the earlier 2025 Gu harvest was above average.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Deyr crop failure did not mean every 2025 season failed.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Five-year comparator itself includes weak seasons.

evidence_records.statement: Deyr failure in central and northern pastoral areas caused serious water/pasture shortages and prompted pastoralists to move livestock earlier and farther than usual.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Drought altered pastoral mobility.

source_refs.locator: webpage heading “Livestock sector severely affected…,” para. 1. (FAOHome)

evidence_records.uncertainty: The evidence establishes mobility response, not resulting conflict.

evidence_records.statement: Sorghum prices in Dinsoor and maize prices in Qorioley more than doubled between Sep 2025 and Jan 2026; Mogadishu sorghum and maize rose 25% and 45% respectively from Nov 2025 to Jan 2026.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Drought-linked production losses coincided with steep food-price rises.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Market prices have multiple determinants; source links seasonal effects to Deyr concerns, not climate alone.

evidence_records.statement: IPC estimated 6.0 million people, 31% of the analysed population, in Phase 3+ during Apr-Jun 2026; deterioration reflected poor rainfall together with food prices, currency disruption, conflict/insecurity, flood risk and inadequate assistance.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Acute food insecurity is explicitly multi-causal.

source_refs.locator: PDF file p.1/27 “Overview/Key Drivers” and p.2/27 driver synthesis.

evidence_records.uncertainty: Projection can change as rainfall, prices, conflict and assistance evolve.

evidence_records.statement: Nearly 1.88 million children aged 6-59 months were expected to require treatment for acute malnutrition in 2026, with worsening food insecurity interacting with disease, feeding practices, inadequate services and funding constraints.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Child malnutrition reflects multiple interacting pressures.

source_refs.locator: PDF file p.1/27 headline and p.2/27 nutrition paragraph.

evidence_records.uncertainty: Not a climate-attributable malnutrition estimate.

evidence_records.statement: Burhakaba agropastoral areas were at risk of Famine, not classified in Famine under the most-likely scenario; the risk depended on a plausible combination of failed Gu rains, sharply rising prices and inadequate humanitarian food-security assistance.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Burhakaba famine risk is explicitly conditional.

source_refs.locator: PDF file p.13/27, Annex 1 “Burhakaba District…Risk of Famine.”

evidence_records.uncertainty: Must not be restated as an observed famine.

evidence_records.statement: UNHCR’s Q2 2026 monitoring says conflict and drought together accounted for nearly 90% of recorded displacement during the quarter.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Current displacement is jointly associated with conflict and drought.

source_refs.locator: webpage summary paragraph under report title. (UNHCR Data Portal)

evidence_records.uncertainty: “Recorded” displacement only; methodology detail was not available on publication page; the figure does not separate causal shares.

evidence_records.statement: In the Newly Liberated Areas of Hirshabelle and Galmudug, EIP identifies drought/flood effects on livelihoods and resource availability as exacerbators of existing land/water competition, grievances and political/communal tensions, while explicitly rejecting climate as a direct root cause.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate stress can amplify local conflict drivers rather than directly cause conflict.

source_refs.locator: PDF file pp.4-6/70 Executive Summary; p.42/70 §3.3/Fig. 6.

evidence_records.uncertainty: Mixed-method plausibility/context analysis; locality-specific; not causal identification.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI’s Somalia case study identifies livelihoods, migration/displacement, poverty and grievances as channels through which climate-related change can affect UNSOM peacebuilding, while also retaining civil war, violence, poverty, population pressure, land management and weak governance as conflict drivers.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate-security effects are mediated and embedded in pre-existing fragility.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Older, mission-centred plausibility probe; should not be translated into a deterministic recruitment/violence claim.

evidence_records.statement: UNDP identified weak federal coordination, state-level technical/managerial capacity and adaptation financing conditions as barriers to adaptation planning.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Institutional capacity constrains adaptation.

source_refs.locator: webpage “Project summary,” first two paragraphs. (UNDP Climate Change Adaptation)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Programme diagnostic rather than independent institutional survey.

evidence_records.statement: UNDP planned adaptation-project activities in states where it already had operations in order to avoid potential security-related risks.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Insecurity directly influenced adaptation-programme geography.

source_refs.locator: webpage paragraph immediately after “Location: Somalia.” (UNDP Climate Change Adaptation)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Demonstrates programme-design constraint, not the national magnitude of foregone adaptation.

evidence_records.statement: NDC 3.0 places adaptation at the centre of climate policy and identifies planned investments in climate-resilient agriculture, water, health and infrastructure alongside gender-responsive and conflict-sensitive measures.
evidence_records.compact_statement: National policy explicitly frames adaptation as conflict-sensitive.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Evidence of policy intent only; implementation/effectiveness not demonstrated.

evidence_records.statement: By Feb 2023, Biyoole had established 51 community management systems and improved water sources for 362,731 people; IEG also found the flood/drought livelihood-support indicator only partly achieved.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Rural resilience projects produced substantial outputs but missed some targets.

source_refs.locator: PDF file p.88/146 (printed p.56), rural resilience; p.89/146 Table 4.2.

evidence_records.uncertainty: Several figures originate from project implementation reports; broader outcome attribution should remain cautious.

evidence_records.statement: IEG concluded that limited fiscal space and government capacity undermine the sustainability of service delivery and that overly rapid portfolio expansion risks overstretching systems and coordination platforms.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Fragility and fiscal limits threaten service sustainability.
evidence_records.uncertainty: World Bank portfolio lens, not a complete assessment of all Somali institutions.

evidence_records.statement: WFP’s independent evaluation identified rapid food/cash scaling during the 2021-23 drought as its main CSP achievement, while finding that funding gaps and logistics constrained nutrition, school feeding, resilience and market-access work and that broad capacity strengthening spread resources thinly.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Emergency response performed strongly in some areas but resilience work faced constraints.

source_refs.locator: webpage evaluation summary, paras. 1-4. (World Food Programme)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Evaluation supports programme performance, not a claim that WFP alone caused national food-security change.

evidence_records.statement: SWALIM’s Q1 2026 drought indices, climate updates and river monitoring were disseminated to SoDMA and humanitarian coordination bodies and used for response prioritisation; earlier drought forecasts had triggered anticipatory-action initiatives.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Early-warning infrastructure supports anticipatory coping.

source_refs.locator: PDF file p.1/8, monitoring/dissemination and anticipatory-action paragraphs.

evidence_records.uncertainty: Source documents use of information and prior triggers, not counterfactual losses avoided.

evidence_records.statement: The Federal Government activated the National Preparedness Plan for Food and Nutrition Security Crises on 5 Feb 2026 for the first time, following risk monitoring, technical consultations and prime-ministerial approval.
evidence_records.compact_statement: A national crisis-governance mechanism was activated in 2026.

source_refs.locator: webpage opening paragraphs and paras. 101-105. (World Bank)

evidence_records.uncertainty: Activation and intended response are verified; effectiveness after activation is not.

evidence_records.statement: UNDP reports that its 2025 programmes provided clean water to 23,000 people and reports peacebuilding/service outputs, including community dispute mechanisms; these are programme-reported rather than independently evaluated outcomes.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate resilience and peace-supporting capacity exist, but evidence is mainly output-level.
evidence_records.uncertainty: Self-reported annual results; causal effect and durability not established.

evidence_records.statement: ERA5 reanalysis presents South Sudan's 1991-2020 climatology and 1950-2023 historical record at daily scale and 0.25-degree resolution; the portal describes a broad historical warming signal while cautioning that reanalysis is model-based and that precipitation trends are harder to distinguish from natural variability.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Use ERA5 as light climate context, retaining its model and precipitation-trend caveats.
institutions: World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal
European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts

source_refs.locator: named webpage heading 'Climatology (ERA5)', methodology, trends, and 'Data Caveats' sections

evidence_records.uncertainty: ERA5 is model-based; national aggregation masks local variation and supports no social attribution.

evidence_records.statement: The 2025 SIPRI-NUPI fact sheet describes a tropical savannah climate with seasonal White Nile tributary flooding, severe drought and flood exposure, increasing rainy-season precipitation, declining dry-season rainfall, and consecutive floods that no longer reliably recede during the dry season.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Screen for changing flood persistence and dry-season water stress, not a single uniform hazard trend.

source_refs.locator: page 2, section 'Climate exposure: Trends and projections' and section 'Socioecological vulnerabilities'

evidence_records.uncertainty: Sparse gauges and synthesized datasets limit subnational trend and site-level inference.

evidence_records.statement: The World Bank CCDR key messages project that hotter conditions could reduce sorghum yields by 2050.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Screen agrifood investments for projected heat-related sorghum yield risk through 2050.

source_refs.locator: official landing-page key-message bullet on hotter conditions and sorghum-yield impacts by 2050

evidence_records.uncertainty: Only official CCDR key messages were accessible; project exposure still needs local assessment.

evidence_records.statement: In flood-affected Rubkona, the SIPRI-NUPI synthesis reports declining livestock holdings and crop farming alongside greater reliance on aid, firewood, and wild foods; it also notes erosion of reciprocal household support and livelihood-related shifts in gender roles, indicating that repeated shocks and conflict can narrow customary coping options.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Assess whether assistance strengthens viable livelihoods and reciprocal coping rather than replacing them.

source_refs.locator: page 2, section 'Livelihood impacts', paragraphs on Rubkona livelihood change and coping mechanisms

evidence_records.uncertainty: Selected qualitative communities are not nationally representative; conflict, markets, and aid also shape coping.

evidence_records.statement: IOM's field validation in three flood-affected payams found damaged or dysfunctional public facilities and reduced road access to health care, markets, and schools; respondents also reported that access constraints prevented aid from reaching some populations and that much facility damage persisted for months.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Map all-season access to facilities and aid routes, including the duration of flood disruption.

source_refs.locator: official webpage numbered results bullet 3, infrastructure and facility-access sub-bullet

evidence_records.uncertainty: Three purposively assessed payams are not nationally representative despite substantial participation.

evidence_records.statement: The same IOM assessment found that floods made farming impossible in many assessed bomas, contributed to livestock loss, changed displacement duration, shifted some communities rapidly between hosting and displacement, and placed additional strain on resources available to communities receiving displaced people.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Screen livelihood recovery and host-community capacity together because flood displacement can reverse hosting roles.

source_refs.locator: official webpage numbered results bullet 3, livelihood and displacement sub-bullets

evidence_records.uncertainty: Purposive local coverage documents co-occurrence, not a single mechanism producing tension.

evidence_records.statement: The UN Common Country Analysis reports that violence and very poor road infrastructure restrict humanitarian reach, rainy-season conditions make many roads impassable, and conflict and flooding together reduce access to drinking water, health, and nutrition services; it also identifies repeated new and secondary displacement.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Treat violence, seasonal roads, service functionality, and secondary displacement as one access-risk screen.

source_refs.locator: document pages 14-15, paragraphs under humanitarian access, nutrition, and 'Displacement and Population movements'

evidence_records.uncertainty: Mixed reference periods support compound-risk screening, not separate conflict and flood effects.

evidence_records.statement: The 2021 INFORM profile scores South Sudan high across hazard and exposure, vulnerability, and lack of coping capacity, with especially elevated components for uprooted people, governance, physical infrastructure, access to health care, food security, and violent conflict.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Use INFORM to flag compound vulnerability and coping constraints, not to rank individual project sites.

source_refs.locator: page 1, risk-components panel and detailed indicators for vulnerability and lack of coping capacity

evidence_records.uncertainty: The national composite masks subnational variation and supports screening, not causal inference.

evidence_records.statement: A UNFPA-led study summary from Malakal, Kapoeta South, and Rubkona reports that flood, drought, displacement, and economic stress coincide with restricted reproductive-health access, increased gender-based violence, child marriage, and survival-driven exploitation, while flooded facilities and heat events further strain health and education access.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Integrate GBV, child-marriage, reproductive-health, and girls' education safeguards into climate response.
institutions: South Sudan National Bureau of Statistics

source_refs.locator: named webpage headings 'Women and girls at risk: A Climate-Induced Crisis' and 'Call to Action: Gender-Responsive Climate Adaptation'

evidence_records.uncertainty: A summary of three high-exposure locations cannot establish national prevalence.

evidence_records.statement: IOM event tracking recorded 20,109 flood-related displacements during December 2024, concentrated in Twic, Rubkona, and Mayiendit counties, and displaced respondents identified health, shelter, and food as their most pressing needs.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Use current event tracking to size immediate health, shelter, and food needs without treating it as a displacement stock.

source_refs.locator: official webpage summary paragraphs for the 1-31 December 2024 reporting period

evidence_records.uncertainty: One month of reported movements is neither a displacement stock nor long-term assessment.

evidence_records.statement: South Sudan's first National Adaptation Plan states that priority sectors lacked concrete NDC implementation plans and identifies sector vulnerability assessment, capacity building, stronger policy and budget mainstreaming, early warning, and institutional coordination as measures needed to move national commitments toward implementation.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Check whether projects close documented planning, coordination, capacity, budget, and early-warning gaps.

source_refs.locator: document page 72, sections on NDC implementation gaps, five adaptation priorities, and 14 Second NDC sectors

evidence_records.uncertainty: The 2021-2025 NAP diagnoses gaps and plans reforms; subsequent implementation requires verification.

evidence_records.statement: South Sudan's Second NDC sets adaptation priorities for climate-smart agriculture and livestock, water management, health-system resilience, flood and drought early warning, land-use planning, and inclusive participation by local communities, women, youth, civil society, and the private sector.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Align activities with NDC sector priorities while testing participation and implementation capacity locally.
evidence_records.scenario: National adaptation commitments principally oriented to 2030

source_refs.locator: official PDF adaptation section, sector priorities and numbered vulnerable-community actions

evidence_records.uncertainty: NDC commitments and intended measures do not demonstrate consistent implementation or achieved resilience.

evidence_records.statement: The SIPRI-NUPI fact sheet reports that 2024 flooding displaced people across 22 counties and that arrivals in high-ground areas of Unity State added population pressure where food insecurity, displacement, and limited coping capacity were already present; reports linked these pressures with local tensions.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Plan high-ground relocation with host-resource, land-use, food-security, and coexistence safeguards.

source_refs.locator: page 3, section 'Migration and mobility', paragraphs on 2024 flood displacement and Unity State high-ground pressures

evidence_records.uncertainty: Local associations do not establish a deterministic pathway; governance, assistance, and prior disputes matter.

evidence_records.statement: Across the SIPRI-NUPI and UN climate-security syntheses, drought, flooding, and altered seasons are assessed as changing pasture, water, cropland, and pastoral movement conditions; where customary agreements and dispute-resolution mechanisms are weak, these shifts may heighten farmer-herder or cattle-group competition, while local dialogues have produced shared livelihood-protection rules.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Support negotiated mobility and resource-sharing rules before changing water, pasture, or cropland access.

source_refs.locator: pages 2-3, sections 'Livelihood impacts' and 'Migration and mobility', including UNMISS dialogue outcomes
official information brief, context section and strategic-interventions bullet on livelihoods, mobility, early warning, and peacebuilding

evidence_records.uncertainty: Climate and mobility are rarely sole drivers; weapons, elite incentives, disease, and disputes matter.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI-NUPI documents cases where floodwater compounded landmine risk and prevented people from following evacuation advice, while prolonged inundation and violent land-grabbing constrained safe return; it also notes that some flood conditions produced temporary cooperation rather than violence.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Assess mines, contested tenure, land-grabbing, and negotiated access before evacuation, return, or relocation.

source_refs.locator: page 4, section 'Armed actors and security', paragraphs on Pigi evacuation, land-grabbing, and temporary cooperation

evidence_records.uncertainty: Documented examples are not nationally prevalent; mines, armed actors, land claims, and cooperation alter outcomes.

evidence_records.compact_statement: Screen whether conflict and institutional weakness are constraining climate adaptation capacity.
evidence_records.statement: The SIPRI-NUPI fact sheet and UN Common Country Analysis assess that conflict, political instability, weak rule of law and public institutions, limited infrastructure, and low trust reduce the capacity of households and institutions to prepare for, adapt to, and recover from climate-related shocks.

source_refs.locator: page 2, section 'Climate change and peace and security', paragraphs on governance, trust, infrastructure, and adaptive capacity
pages 14-15, section on humanitarian access, public services, infrastructure, and conflict- and flood-related disruption

evidence_records.uncertainty: The synthesis cannot isolate institutional or conflict effects from poverty, displacement, and infrastructure deficits.

evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate-security pathways can pass through livelihoods, mobility, recruitment, and elite exploitation
evidence_records.statement: The Climate Security Mechanism brief identifies livelihood disruption, displacement and mobility, recruitment incentives, and elite exploitation of climate-related pressures as possible pathways linking climate stress and insecurity, and recommends conflict-sensitive peacebuilding, early warning, policy integration, and coordination as responses.

source_refs.locator: sections on climate-security pathways and strategic interventions, including livelihood disruption, mobility, recruitment, elite exploitation, early warning, and coordination

evidence_records.uncertainty: Possible pathways are not quantitative attribution and remain conditional on local conflict and political economy.

evidence_records.compact_statement: Conflict-sensitive flood response combined high-ground preparation with community dialogue
evidence_records.statement: The Climate Security Mechanism reports that the 2024 conflict-sensitive flood response plan identified 243 high-ground locations and supported more than 30 awareness campaigns and dialogues, including a Yirol dialogue involving host communities, displaced people, and cattle keepers.

source_refs.locator: heading 'United for Resilience', paragraphs on the 2024 conflict-sensitive response plan, 243 high grounds, more than 30 campaigns and dialogues, and Yirol

evidence_records.uncertainty: Reported activities lack independent outcome evaluation and evidence of consistent implementation.

evidence_records.compact_statement: Localized forecasting and dialogue face language, finance, supply, and trust constraints
evidence_records.statement: The Climate Security Mechanism describes localized forecasting, community knowledge, youth engagement, and dialogue as resilience capacities, while identifying warning communication, language, financing, and supply gaps that can limit timely preparedness in fragile settings.

evidence_records.uncertainty: Potential and local delivery are documented, but durable climate-resilience and peace outcomes were not causally evaluated.

evidence_records.statement: The climate-health assessment models hundreds of operating health facilities as exposed to a mid-century 1-in-100-year flood, while conflict-damaged lifelines and access could convert physical exposure into service disruption.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Health-facility flood exposure intersects with fragile lifelines and access.
institutions: Ministry of Public Health and Population
evidence_records.uncertainty: Exposure modelling does not measure structural vulnerability or continuity, and an annex scenario label appears erroneous.

pathways.climate_pressure: Recurrent drought, above-normal heat and possible spring rainfall decline.
pathways.documented_impact: Crop/rangeland and water stress; reduced agricultural livelihood security.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Income loss, food prices, debt, thin labour markets and reduced humanitarian assistance.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where household reserves, markets and assistance are weak, climate-related livelihood losses may increase negative coping, distress mobility and localized grievances; violence is not an automatic result.
geographies: National mechanism with high exposure documented in Central Highlands and multiple drought-affected districts
pathways.uncertainty: No national causal study demonstrates a drought -> conflict effect while controlling for these factors.
pathways.compact_statement: Drought can deepen livelihood stress through agriculture, water, markets and aid constraints, potentially increasing harmful coping or grievances, but available evidence does not demonstrate that it causes violence.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, slower recharge and higher evaporative demand.
pathways.documented_impact: Difficult household water access and declining groundwater availability.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Large return flows, population concentration, over-extraction, weak infrastructure, water costs and queues at shared sources.
pathways.possible_consequence: Local water disputes or host-returnee tension may increase where scarce supplies and costs cannot be managed equitably.
geographies: broader mechanism plausible but not nationally demonstrated
pathways.uncertainty: The relative contribution of drought versus return flows and long-term over-extraction is not quantified.
resilience_factors: humanitarian WASH investment and demand management
pathways.compact_statement: In surveyed Herat and Kandahar communities, drought and recharge constraints interact with returns, extraction and weak infrastructure; this compound water stress has been associated with localized tensions but not demonstrated organized conflict.

pathways.climate_pressure: Prolonged drought and episodic floods.
pathways.documented_impact: Loss of livelihoods/assets and deteriorating access to food, water and shelter.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Household savings/assets, debt, rental costs, service access and social networks.
pathways.possible_consequence: When coping options are exhausted, households may relocate; displacement can then reproduce exposure and increase protection and livelihood risks.
geographies: Nahr Shahi and Sholgareh in Balkh
pathways.uncertainty: Purposive qualitative data cannot estimate how frequently drought produces displacement nationally.
pathways.compact_statement: Balkh evidence documents a gradual drought-livelihood-displacement process, but household resources and social/service conditions substantially mediate whether movement occurs.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, flood and associated livelihood/service shocks.
pathways.documented_impact: Greater need for income diversification, disaster assistance and health/WASH services.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Restrictions on women’s work, mobility and public participation, plus sociocultural norms and shortages of women service providers.
pathways.possible_consequence: Women and female-headed households may have fewer adaptation and recovery options and may depend more heavily on home-based or informal coping.
geographies: with detailed livelihood evidence from Herat
pathways.uncertainty: Restrictions and enforcement vary spatially; available studies do not estimate an independent climate-adaptation effect.
resilience_factors: targeted financial/assets support and availability of women service staff
pathways.compact_statement: Political and social restrictions can narrow women’s options for responding to climate shocks, although household resources and provincial context produce substantial variation.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought/flood demand on food, health, water and livelihood systems.
pathways.documented_impact: High food/water needs and increased demand for recovery support.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Declining international assistance, political constraints on engagement and non-standard delivery channels.
pathways.possible_consequence: Lower service and adaptation coverage may prolong vulnerability after climate shocks and weaken household buffers.
alternative_explanations: workforce shortages and general fiscal constraints
pathways.uncertainty: No study located quantitatively estimates how much aid contraction changed climate-specific recovery outcomes.
pathways.compact_statement: Aid and institutional constraints plausibly reduce climate-recovery capacity by weakening already strained services, but climate-specific outcome effects remain poorly evaluated.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and climatic stress on transboundary river systems.
pathways.documented_impact: Greater pressure on available water.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Dam/irrigation decisions, allocation rules, weak transboundary mechanisms and bilateral politics.
pathways.possible_consequence: Water disputes may contribute to interstate tension; conversely, cooperative water governance may create dialogue opportunities.
pathways.uncertainty: The climate contribution to the 2023 dispute cannot be isolated.
resilience_factors: water diplomacy and joint disaster preparedness
pathways.compact_statement: Climate stress can intensify the importance of shared water, but allocation and political decisions are indispensable mediators; water cooperation can also support dialogue.

pathways.climate_pressure: Continuing drought, flood and temperature risk.
pathways.documented_impact: Continuing need for climate information, DRR, resilient livelihoods and water management.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Political transition in 2021, altered institutional structures, donor engagement constraints and project suspension.
pathways.possible_consequence: Institutional learning, national/provincial capacity building and continuity of adaptation programmes may weaken even when some community assets remain.
geographies: National institutions plus former CDRRP project areas
alternative_explanations: funding cycles and weak M&E independent of political transition
pathways.uncertainty: Current provincial and sectoral institutional capacity has not been systematically mapped.
resilience_factors: international technical support and alternative monitored financing
pathways.compact_statement: Political and institutional disruption can interrupt higher-level adaptation capacity even where some community-level resilience investments persist.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, flood and compound displacement/return pressures.
pathways.documented_impact: High unmet needs among displaced and returning households.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Strength of family, neighbourhood, charity and community-support networks.
pathways.possible_consequence: Strong informal support may reduce immediate exclusion, destitution and host-returnee tension, although its durability under prolonged poverty is uncertain.
pathways.uncertainty: No evaluation measures whether solidarity mechanisms actually prevent conflict or improve long-run resilience.
pathways.compact_statement: Informal solidarity is a documented coping asset in some communities, but its peace and long-term resilience effects have not been independently evaluated.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, heat, and rainfall variability affecting rainfed production
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced crop and livestock productivity, water stress, food insecurity, and livelihood loss
pathways.fcv_mediator: High rainfed-agriculture dependence, poverty, weak market and input access, displacement, and insecurity
pathways.possible_consequence: Household distress, mobility, protection risks, and localized grievances may intensify where alternative livelihoods and assistance are inaccessible
alternative_explanations: Armed violence, inflation, market disruption, poverty, and policy choices can produce food insecurity and distress without a climate shock.
pathways.uncertainty: The interaction is well supported at national scale, but the relative contribution of climate pressures is not estimated.
pathways.compact_statement: Drought, heat, and erratic rainfall can deepen livelihood and food-security stress where rainfed dependence, poverty, insecurity, and weak access limit alternatives.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, rainfall variability, and land degradation affecting pasture, water, and cropland
pathways.documented_impact: Changed resource availability and livelihood mobility among farmers and pastoralists
pathways.fcv_mediator: Overlapping land claims, weak resource governance, armed-group exploitation, and disrupted customary dispute resolution
pathways.possible_consequence: Farmer-herder disputes or political exploitation of local grievances may become more likely, but are not an automatic result of climate pressure
alternative_explanations: Agricultural expansion, herd growth, political exclusion, weapons, insurgency, and unresolved tenure disputes independently shape violence.
pathways.uncertainty: Available evidence supports conditional mechanisms rather than a Burkina Faso-wide causal effect.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related resource stress may aggravate farmer-herder disputes when land governance and dispute resolution are weak or grievances are exploited.

pathways.climate_pressure: Heavy rainfall and flooding in towns receiving conflict-displaced households
pathways.documented_impact: Damage to temporary shelters, asset loss, and repeated housing insecurity
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict displacement, scarce safer urban land, poverty, and limited municipal shelter capacity
pathways.possible_consequence: Repeated displacement, exclusion, and competition for safer land and services may deepen household insecurity and local tension
alternative_explanations: Housing exclusion, poverty, conflict displacement, and poor drainage can create the same shelter risks without climate change.
pathways.uncertainty: Direct flood exposure is documented at selected sites; tension and repeated displacement are conditional consequences.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict displacement can place households on flood-prone land, where heavy rain then compounds shelter loss and insecurity.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, flood, and food-system shocks requiring timely assistance and adaptation
pathways.documented_impact: Higher need for food, water, livelihood, and climate-risk services
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed insecurity, blocked transport, disrupted markets, weak services, and constrained humanitarian access
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate shocks may produce larger and more unequal losses because conflict limits early warning, farming, markets, assistance, and recovery
alternative_explanations: Chronic poverty, remoteness, underinvestment, and macroeconomic shocks can independently reduce response reach and worsen losses.
pathways.uncertainty: The sources establish access and performance constraints but do not quantify the additional climate loss attributable to conflict.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict and access constraints can magnify climate losses by restricting farming, markets, early warning, assistance, and recovery.

pathways.climate_pressure: Overlapping climate, displacement, health, and economic shocks
pathways.documented_impact: Pressure on municipal finance, services, shelter, and social assistance
pathways.fcv_mediator: Uneven fiscal transfers, local capacity limits, weak accountability, and rapid displacement into receiving municipalities
pathways.possible_consequence: Unequal or delayed services may deepen exclusion and mistrust, while capable and accountable municipalities can reduce these risks
alternative_explanations: Public-finance policy, COVID-19 restrictions, administrative reform, and conflict displacement can drive municipal service stress without climate shocks.
pathways.uncertainty: Program outputs show capacity and constraints but not causal effects on trust, cohesion, or climate resilience.
pathways.compact_statement: Municipal capacity and accountability mediate whether overlapping shocks produce exclusion or more inclusive local delivery.

pathways.climate_pressure: Rainfall uncertainty affecting crop-calendar decisions and local preparedness
pathways.documented_impact: Risk of mistimed sowing, seed loss, and weak local climate information
pathways.fcv_mediator: Uneven last-mile services, institutional coordination, community liaison coverage, and insecurity-related access gaps
pathways.possible_consequence: Accessible climate information may protect livelihoods and reduce distress, while unequal coverage could leave high-risk communities behind
alternative_explanations: Input quality, soil conditions, market access, extension services, and insecurity also determine crop and livelihood outcomes.
pathways.uncertainty: Outputs and testimonials do not establish forecast accuracy, equitable uptake, yields, or conflict-sensitive coverage.
pathways.compact_statement: Last-mile hydrometeorological services may reduce livelihood losses when information is trusted, timely, and accessible in insecure areas.

pathways.climate_pressure: Rising heat, rainfall variability and episodic drought/heavy rainfall.
pathways.documented_impact: Agricultural production and food availability are sensitive to rainfall and climate shocks.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict, displacement, degraded roads, prices and weak purchasing power shape whether production changes translate into household food access.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate-related production losses could worsen acute food insecurity where conflict and market-access constraints limit coping.
geographies: drought concern greater in northern CAR
pathways.uncertainty: IPC does not quantify a separate climate causal effect; future drought direction is uncertain.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate shocks can affect food production, but whether this produces severe food insecurity in CAR is strongly mediated by conflict, markets, roads, poverty and assistance. (IPCinfo)

pathways.climate_pressure: Rainfall variability, drought and pasture/water pressures in CAR and surrounding regions.
pathways.documented_impact: Changes in timing or geography of pastoral movements.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Weak cross-border regulation, land/water access rules, armed-group involvement and local dispute-management capacity.
pathways.possible_consequence: Altered livestock movement may increase the likelihood of localized farmer-herder tensions where regulation and negotiated access are weak.
affected_groups: sedentary farmers and communities along corridors
pathways.uncertainty: NUPI explicitly identifies a lack of robust CAR-specific climate-security monitoring.
resilience_factors: compensation arrangements and functioning local mediation
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related mobility pressure can matter, but governance of routes and resources - and armed insecurity - determines whether mobility becomes cooperative, disruptive or violent. (NUPI)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, rainfall variability and seasonal pasture/water stress.
pathways.documented_impact: Pastoralists require mobility and negotiated resource access.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed violence and state withdrawal can remove route controls, compensation procedures and dispute-resolution mechanisms.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate and seasonal resource stress may become harder to manage peacefully when conflict erodes institutions that previously organized mobility.
pathways.uncertainty: Practitioner evidence is not a nationally representative causal study.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict can reduce the institutional capacity needed to manage ordinary and climate-amplified pastoral resource pressures. (NUPI)

pathways.climate_pressure: Seasonal flooding and other climate shocks can affect already fragile infrastructure and services.
pathways.documented_impact: CAR has large displaced populations; Birao experienced a particularly sharp refugee influx from the Sudan conflict.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict-driven displacement increases demand for water, health, shelter, education and livelihoods in low-capacity locations.
pathways.possible_consequence: Host areas with large service deficits may have less capacity to absorb an additional flood, drought or food-production shock.
geographies: the mechanism should not be generalized automatically
pathways.uncertainty: No reviewed study estimates the marginal effect of displacement on climate-disaster losses in Birao.
resilience_factors: Integration of refugee and host-community services
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict-driven population shocks can consume scarce service capacity and plausibly reduce resilience to subsequent climate shocks, but the combined effect has not been directly evaluated.

pathways.climate_pressure: Rainfall variability and production shocks.
pathways.documented_impact: Agricultural output and food availability vary with rainfall and other shocks.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Persistent conflict, displacement and degraded roads restrict market and humanitarian access; high prices and low purchasing power further constrain households.
pathways.possible_consequence: A localized climate-related production shock could have larger food-security effects where conflict has already impaired transport and markets.
alternative_explanations: assistance coverage and local harvest conditions
pathways.uncertainty: Relative contributions of climate, conflict and market variables are not causally decomposed.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict-damaged access and weak purchasing power can magnify the household consequences of climate-sensitive food-production changes. (IPCinfo)

pathways.climate_pressure: Heat, rainfall variability, floods and drought.
pathways.documented_impact: Effective adaptation requires observations, risk analysis and water/hydrometeorological information.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Weak institutions, limited staff/equipment, fragmented planning and broader fragility constrain data generation and use.
pathways.possible_consequence: Poor climate information can reduce the timeliness and targeting of adaptation and disaster-management decisions.
alternative_explanations: Fiscal scarcity and technical constraints may exist independently of armed conflict
pathways.uncertainty: Reviewed documents do not estimate the share of climate-information deficits caused specifically by FCV.
pathways.compact_statement: Fragile institutional capacity constrains the information systems required to anticipate and manage climate risks, although the specific contribution of conflict is not quantified. (UNFCCC)

pathways.climate_pressure: Food-production and livelihood shocks.
pathways.documented_impact: Emergency agricultural assistance is intended to protect or restore livelihoods.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Weak administrative systems and targeting through formal organizations can shape who receives assistance.
pathways.possible_consequence: Programme design can unintentionally leave highly vulnerable households with less support and therefore lower recovery capacity.
pathways.uncertainty: Evaluation concerns a 2014-2016 operation, so current programme design may differ.
resilience_factors: Vulnerability-based targeting independent of formal membership
local technical capacity and procurement systems
pathways.compact_statement: Independent evaluation demonstrates that delivery rules in a fragile environment can themselves create resilience gaps by excluding vulnerable non-members.

pathways.climate_pressure: Seasonal variability in pasture, water and agricultural resources.
pathways.documented_impact: Pastoral mobility creates recurring needs for negotiated access to land and water.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Local agreements, compensation, regulated routes and farmer-pastoralist exchange can reduce disputes.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where legitimate local governance functions, resource variability may be managed through negotiation rather than escalation.
alternative_explanations: Economic complementarity between livestock and crop systems
pathways.uncertainty: No experimental or quasi-experimental evaluation was identified.
resilience_factors: reciprocal agricultural-pastoral exchange and local dispute resolution
pathways.compact_statement: CAR evidence contains not only risk pathways but also peace-supporting institutions that can mediate resource variability without violence. (ICRC)

pathways.climate_pressure: Erratic rainfall, drought periods and flooding.
pathways.documented_impact: Reported reductions/disruptions in pasture, livestock water, crops and fishing/farming livelihoods.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competition over water, channels, grazing areas and crops, interacting with local resource-sharing rules.
pathways.possible_consequence: Under adverse governance and security conditions, these pressures may contribute to intercommunal clashes and displacement.
pathways.uncertainty: Interview-based evidence cannot estimate the climate contribution to violence.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related livelihood stress may aggravate already-governed resource disputes; it is not demonstrated as a sufficient cause of violence. (Refugees International)

pathways.climate_pressure: Climate shocks affect already vulnerable livelihood systems.
pathways.documented_impact: Acute food insecurity and constrained household coping.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict displacement, loss/restriction of land and livelihood access, concentration of needs.
pathways.possible_consequence: Displaced and host households may become less able to absorb subsequent climate or price shocks.
geographies: Far North and other crisis regions
pathways.uncertainty: No reviewed study decomposes the relative climate/conflict contributions.
resilience_factors: accessible markets and conflict-sensitive resource access
pathways.compact_statement: Climate shocks occur inside a conflict-displacement system that can weaken coping, rather than independently producing acute hunger. (UNHCR Data Portal)

pathways.climate_pressure: Unreliable rainfall and dry spells.
pathways.documented_impact: Poorer pasture and longer livestock movements.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Crop/grazing encroachment, livestock density, crop damage and land-tenure pressures.
pathways.possible_consequence: These interacting pressures may aggravate farmer-pastoralist conflict.
pathways.uncertainty: No national extrapolation is justified.
pathways.compact_statement: In Kilum-Ijim, climate variability interacts with herd pressure and land governance rather than operating as a stand-alone conflict driver. (Frontiers)

pathways.climate_pressure: Urban flood and other hazard exposure.
pathways.documented_impact: Need for resilient urban infrastructure and services.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Security problems restricted implementation and caused reductions in project scope.
pathways.possible_consequence: Conflict may leave some exposed urban communities with delayed or incomplete resilience investments.
geographies: Particularly Far North and NW/SW project locations
alternative_explanations: counterpart funding and staffing also constrained implementation
pathways.uncertainty: Project experience cannot be generalized to every municipality.
resilience_factors: municipal capacity support and conflict-sensitive delivery
pathways.compact_statement: Recent project evidence directly shows insecurity delaying or narrowing resilience investment. (World Bank)

pathways.climate_pressure: Multi-hazard exposure requiring coordinated adaptation.
pathways.documented_impact: Climate policies require sectoral/local implementation.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Institutional fragmentation, limited decentralization capacity, fiscal constraints and weak data systems.
pathways.possible_consequence: Adaptation may be slower, less spatially targeted or less sustainable.
affected_groups: Especially populations dependent on weak local service systems
sectors: Cross-sectoral climate policy and public services
systems_assets_resources: Cross-sectoral climate policy and public services
alternative_explanations: normal administrative complexity and project design
pathways.uncertainty: No reviewed nationwide study estimates adaptation losses attributable to governance fragmentation.
pathways.compact_statement: Cameroon has an increasingly articulated climate architecture, but implementation bottlenecks may weaken conversion of policy into local resilience. (UNFCCC)

pathways.climate_pressure: Climate shocks are one contributor to humanitarian needs.
pathways.documented_impact: Severe food insecurity in conflict-affected regions.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Displacement and insecurity elevate needs while donor shortages reduce delivery.
pathways.possible_consequence: Reduced aid coverage could increase harmful coping or deepen vulnerability to subsequent shocks.
pathways.uncertainty: Downstream conflict/stability effects have not been evaluated.
resilience_factors: Reliable multi-year humanitarian finance and livelihood-support transitions
pathways.compact_statement: Assistance capacity is itself a mediator of whether multi-causal shocks become deeper household crises. (World Food Programme)

pathways.climate_pressure: Natural-resource stress may intensify livelihood-management challenges.
pathways.documented_impact: Water/pasture access can be a focus of community disputes.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Quality of dialogue, dispute management and inclusive resource rules.
pathways.possible_consequence: Stronger local institutions may reduce escalation even under resource stress.
