alternative_explanations: Wider security trends and other interventions may explain perceived conflict reductions
pathways.uncertainty: No independent counterfactual evaluation of peace outcomes.
pathways.compact_statement: Evidence suggests local resource institutions can be peace-supporting, but the measured magnitude of their effect remains uncertain. (MPTF Gateway)

pathways.climate_pressure: Participant households face climate and non-climate shocks.
pathways.documented_impact: AEP-Youth improved measured food security but did not improve measured shock-recovery ability.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict/insecurity was explicitly included among non-climate shocks in the evaluation framework.
pathways.possible_consequence: Economic or food-security improvements should not automatically be interpreted as climate/FCV resilience.
alternative_explanations: Differential shock exposure among participants and comparison households
pathways.uncertainty: Programme geography excludes major Far North and East crisis contexts.
resilience_factors: Targeted programming that explicitly measures recovery
pathways.compact_statement: Measurable livelihood gains did not automatically produce measurable shock resilience. (IFAD) ---

pathways.climate_pressure: Rising heat, changing rainfall, drought/flood episodes.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced or disrupted agricultural production and climate-sensitive livelihood stress.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Existing land disputes, unequal access, weak resource governance and lack of alternative livelihoods.
pathways.possible_consequence: Livelihood pressure may intensify existing disputes or grievances over land and water in parts of eastern DRC.
alternative_explanations: demographic pressure and market conditions independently generate conflict
pathways.uncertainty: SIPRI explicitly states that specific livelihood-to-conflict mechanisms remain less clear than the climate-to-livelihood link. (SIPRI2)
resilience_factors: extension services and inclusive resource planning
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related livelihood stress may increase pressure on already contested land and water, but political and governance conditions determine whether tension escalates.

pathways.climate_pressure: Recurring drought, rainfall variability and declining pasture/water availability.
pathways.documented_impact: Altered livestock mobility and competition for water/pasture.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Pre-existing farmer-pastoralist disputes, identity conflict and land-access arrangements.
pathways.possible_consequence: Greater tension, livestock theft or violence has been reported locally where altered movement intersects with existing disputes.
pathways.uncertainty: Local, largely qualitative evidence; it must not be generalized across South Kivu or nationally.
resilience_factors: participatory land/water governance and agro-pastoral cooperation
pathways.compact_statement: In the Ruzizi Plain, climate-sensitive changes in pasture and livestock movement appear to interact with - not originate independently from - existing farmer-pastoralist conflict.

pathways.climate_pressure: Extreme rainfall, floods and rainfall-triggered landslides.
pathways.documented_impact: Housing/livelihood loss and displacement.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Overcrowded sites, inadequate basic services, resource scarcity and weak post-disaster recovery.
pathways.possible_consequence: Displacement may create or intensify localized tensions between displaced and host communities where services/resources are already scarce.
alternative_explanations: Conflict displacement is far larger in many eastern areas and may independently overwhelm services
poor planning and infrastructure condition flood losses
pathways.uncertainty: Disaster-displacement figures should not automatically be interpreted as anthropogenic-climate displacement.
pathways.compact_statement: Flood displacement can add pressure to fragile local service/resource systems, potentially worsening grievances where recovery is weak.

pathways.climate_pressure: Future drought, flood, heat or rainfall shocks.
pathways.documented_impact: Households require access to farmland, markets, services and humanitarian support to cope.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed-group control, insecurity, road blockage, displacement and restricted territorial access.
pathways.possible_consequence: Communities exposed to conflict may experience greater livelihood loss, food insecurity and slower recovery when climate shocks occur.
geographies: North/South Kivu and other conflict-affected eastern provinces
institutions: local authorities and armed actors controlling access
alternative_explanations: infrastructure deficits and commodity-price shocks can also reduce coping capacity outside active conflict
pathways.uncertainty: Effects on quantified adaptation outcomes have rarely been evaluated.
resilience_factors: conflict-sensitive adaptation and locally trusted delivery channels
pathways.compact_statement: Insecurity can convert otherwise manageable climate shocks into deeper crises by removing access to land, markets, services and recovery assistance. (SIPRI2)

pathways.climate_pressure: Climate mitigation/adaptation requires functioning forest, land and ecosystem governance.
pathways.documented_impact: Armed actors and political-economic networks exploit forests/minerals and damage environmental governance.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict financing, corruption, weak state authority and elite competition.
pathways.possible_consequence: Forest-management and resilience objectives may be harder to implement, increasing environmental vulnerability and weakening mitigation capacity.
alternative_explanations: regulatory design and global commodity demand also drive environmental loss
pathways.uncertainty: Environmental degradation should not be relabelled as climate damage; specific climate consequences require separate evidence.
resilience_factors: forest monitoring and conflict-sensitive natural-resource governance
pathways.compact_statement: FCV-linked extraction can undermine institutions needed for climate mitigation and adaptation, while remaining an independent environmental and political-economy driver. (NUPI3)

pathways.climate_pressure: Extreme rainfall and flood hazard.
pathways.documented_impact: Damage to roads, water, electricity, housing and agricultural assets.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Poverty, informal settlement, weak drainage/DRM capacity, fiscal limitations and weak coordination.
pathways.possible_consequence: Repeated losses could deepen service deficits, recovery burdens and public grievances; violence is not demonstrated by the evidence reviewed.
pathways.uncertainty: No source reviewed demonstrates that urban floods cause violence or conflict.
pathways.compact_statement: Flood losses place additional pressure on weak urban service systems, but any transition from service stress to FCV outcomes remains unproven. (World Bank5)

pathways.climate_pressure: Multi-hazard climate exposure requiring sustained adaptation investment.
pathways.documented_impact: Large planned adaptation requirements and implementation needs.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Fiscal pressure, weak coordination, governance limitations and - where relevant - conflict-related access constraints.
pathways.possible_consequence: Delayed, incomplete or unsustained adaptation may leave households and infrastructure exposed to future shocks.
alternative_explanations: COVID-19 and maintenance failures independently affect performance
pathways.uncertainty: National adaptation effectiveness has not been comprehensively evaluated.
resilience_factors: predictable financing and locally owned implementation
pathways.compact_statement: Policy ambition exceeds demonstrated delivery capacity, leaving a gap between adaptation plans and sustained resilience outcomes. (IMF7)

pathways.climate_pressure: Livelihood and environmental stresses.
pathways.documented_impact: Communities face livelihood, displacement and resource-management challenges.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Social cohesion, inclusion, local legitimacy and collective action.
pathways.possible_consequence: Well-supported women-, youth- and community-led initiatives could reduce vulnerability and strengthen peaceful problem-solving, although programme-level effects on violence are not established.
alternative_explanations: Community organizations may have limited resources
pathways.uncertainty: No reviewed evaluation measures whether these initiatives reduce conflict incidence.
resilience_factors: agro-pastoral cooperatives and inclusive customary/local governance
pathways.compact_statement: Local social institutions provide credible resilience and peace-supporting capacity, but their impact has not been rigorously quantified. (SIPRI2)

pathways.climate_pressure: Extreme heat.
pathways.documented_impact: Higher heat exposure is associated with more food-insecure households.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Household food insecurity and livelihood stress.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where other political, economic and security conditions are adverse, food insecurity may contribute to greater conflict risk.
pathways.uncertainty: Causal direction and omitted-variable effects remain material.
pathways.compact_statement: Extreme heat may raise conflict risk through food insecurity, but available Ethiopia evidence is correlational rather than proof that heat causes conflict. (World Food Programme1)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and poor pasture/water availability.
pathways.documented_impact: Pastoralists adjust mobility and other coping strategies.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competition over common water and pasture.
pathways.possible_consequence: Increased probability of local intercommunal tension or conflict in some Somali Region settings.
pathways.uncertainty: Strongly location-dependent.
pathways.compact_statement: Drought can affect local conflict risk through mobility and governed access to pasture/water; it is not an automatic conflict trigger. (SIPRI7)

pathways.climate_pressure: Heavy rainfall and flooding.
pathways.documented_impact: Infrastructure, crops, livelihoods and settlements are exposed to flood damage.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Displacement, service congestion, lost assets and unequal recovery.
pathways.possible_consequence: In fragile or poorly governed settings, these stresses could exacerbate grievances or reduce social cohesion.
pathways.uncertainty: No verified source here demonstrates a national flood -> violence causal effect.
pathways.compact_statement: Flood impacts may interact with displacement and service deficits, but a conflict consequence remains inferential. (World Bank2)

pathways.climate_pressure: Any concurrent drought/heat/flood shock.
pathways.documented_impact: Conflict exposure is associated with materially higher food poverty in surveyed pastoral/agropastoral communities.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Violence, market disruption and household asset/income loss.
pathways.possible_consequence: Households affected by conflict may have fewer resources with which to cope with subsequent climate shocks.
pathways.uncertainty: Direct effect on specific adaptation outcomes was not measured.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict-associated food poverty plausibly reduces household climate-coping capacity, but the complete adaptation chain has not been directly evaluated. (World Bank2)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought or other climate-related humanitarian stress.
pathways.documented_impact: Insecurity creates risks and raises WFP operating costs.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Access restrictions, insecurity and increased delivery costs.
pathways.possible_consequence: Assistance, recovery and resilience services may reach fewer people, arrive later or cost more.
geographies: Particularly Amhara in current WFP reporting
pathways.uncertainty: No quantified causal estimate of lost resilience outcome.
pathways.compact_statement: Insecurity demonstrably constrains humanitarian operations; its precise reduction in climate-resilience outcomes is not quantified. (World Food Programme8)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and seasonal water/pasture scarcity.
pathways.documented_impact: Pastoral dry-season grazing and water access are important to livelihood continuity.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unrecognized communal tenure, expropriation/displacement risk and contested access.
pathways.possible_consequence: Poorly governed land change may heighten livelihood vulnerability and potentially aggravate local fragility.
institutions: Formal land administration and customary institutions
pathways.uncertainty: National incidence is not quantified.
resilience_factors: Recognition of communal rights and locally grounded customary governance
pathways.compact_statement: Institutions governing land and seasonal access can mediate whether climate stress becomes a livelihood or fragility problem. (World Bank2)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought.
pathways.documented_impact: Drought insurance/cash can help households maintain livestock or meet needs.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Reduced need for drought-driven mobility and competition.
pathways.possible_consequence: Intercommunal conflict risk may fall where mobility-related resource competition is a relevant conflict mechanism.
pathways.uncertainty: Severe drought still generated migration; peace effect not rigorously estimated.
pathways.compact_statement: Insurance has a plausible peace-supporting pathway, but evidence is mixed and programme targeting can generate its own tensions. (SIPRI7)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, erosion and land degradation interacting with climate variability.
pathways.documented_impact: Evaluated SLM interventions improved land-restoration indicators.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Distribution of access, grazing restrictions and livelihood compensation.
pathways.possible_consequence: Well-designed restoration can increase resilience; poorly designed closures can increase livestock-keeper vulnerability and potentially create grievances.
pathways.uncertainty: Evidence concerns evaluated watersheds, not all restoration programmes.
pathways.compact_statement: Adaptation can restore ecosystems while producing distributional harm if livelihood access is ignored. (Independent Evaluation Group13) ---

pathways.climate_pressure: Tropical cyclones, heavy rainfall, flooding, and coastal pressures affecting dense settlements and infrastructure
pathways.documented_impact: Damage to homes, roads, health facilities, crops, water systems, and local livelihoods
pathways.fcv_mediator: Poverty, deforestation, unsafe urbanization, weak services, limited municipal resources, and low institutional legitimacy
pathways.possible_consequence: Displacement, unequal recovery, livelihood loss, and perceived exclusion may deepen social tension, but violence is not an automatic climate outcome
alternative_explanations: Political instability, armed violence, poor land-use planning, chronic poverty, and infrastructure underinvestment can independently produce displacement and grievance.
pathways.uncertainty: Hazard and vulnerability are documented, but no admitted source estimates a climate effect on social tension or conflict.
pathways.compact_statement: Cyclone and flood losses may deepen displacement and exclusion where poverty, unsafe settlement, and weak local delivery constrain recovery.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, heat, rainfall variability, flooding, and soil and water stress affecting rainfed agriculture
pathways.documented_impact: Lower or less reliable production, livestock and water stress, food insecurity, and livelihood loss
pathways.fcv_mediator: Rainfed dependence, market disruption, poverty, insecurity, weak safety nets, and armed-group control of transport and commerce
pathways.possible_consequence: Distress, indebtedness, migration, recruitment vulnerability, or political grievance may increase when households lack viable alternatives
alternative_explanations: Inflation, trade and market disruption, violence, policy choices, land degradation, and chronic poverty independently affect food security and mobility.
pathways.uncertainty: The sources establish interacting pressures but do not estimate the relative climate contribution or a causal recruitment effect.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate stress can worsen food and livelihood insecurity where rainfed dependence, market disruption, poverty, and violence restrict alternatives.

pathways.climate_pressure: Flood, cyclone, heat, and disease risks requiring functioning water, health, transport, and humanitarian systems
pathways.documented_impact: Higher demand for safe water, medical care, emergency transport, supplies, and public information
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed-group control, violence, blocked supply chains, facility damage, fuel shortages, staff insecurity, and constrained humanitarian access
pathways.possible_consequence: Weather and health shocks may cause larger and more unequal losses because conflict disables preparedness, access, response, and recovery
institutions: International Committee of the Red Cross
alternative_explanations: Chronic underinvestment, workforce shortages, poverty, and weak maintenance can disrupt health and water systems without armed violence.
pathways.uncertainty: Service disruption is directly documented, but its additional effect during a defined climate event is not quantified.
pathways.compact_statement: Armed violence can magnify climate and health losses by disabling water, health, transport, and humanitarian delivery systems.

pathways.climate_pressure: Heavy rainfall, flooding, heat, and disease exposure in displacement sites and overstretched host communities
pathways.documented_impact: Overcrowding, inadequate shelter, unsafe water and sanitation, and pressure on health and other basic services
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict displacement, site location, armed-group control, poverty, gendered protection risks, and weak local services
pathways.possible_consequence: Displaced and host households may face repeated displacement, disease, deeper deprivation, or local tension when hazards strike already overloaded settings
alternative_explanations: Housing shortages, land-use failure, poverty, and weak WASH services can create similar site risks independently of climate change.
pathways.uncertainty: Compounded exposure is directly documented, while repeated displacement and local tension remain conditional consequences.
pathways.compact_statement: Violence-driven displacement can place households in overcrowded, poorly serviced settings where flood, heat, and disease risks compound insecurity.

pathways.climate_pressure: Cyclones, floods, and other hydroclimatic emergencies requiring coordinated local preparedness and response
pathways.documented_impact: Demand for warnings, evacuation, shelters, damage assessment, road access, and rapid assistance
pathways.fcv_mediator: Uneven municipal capability, limited finance, weak coordination and legitimacy, insecurity, and damaged transport links
pathways.possible_consequence: Capable and accountable local systems can reduce unequal losses, while weak or inaccessible systems can deepen exclusion and delayed recovery
institutions: Ministry of Public Works, Transport and Communication
alternative_explanations: Hazard magnitude, remoteness, transport quality, national political decisions, and external financing also determine response performance.
pathways.uncertainty: Reported capacity gains are not independently evaluated and earthquake response cannot be interpreted as climate-response effectiveness.
pathways.compact_statement: Municipal civil-protection and transport capacity mediate whether emergencies lead to timely, inclusive response or delayed and unequal recovery.

pathways.climate_pressure: Overlapping climate, food, displacement, and violence pressures affecting young people and livelihood systems
pathways.documented_impact: Eroded livelihoods, reduced coping options, displacement, and greater need for social and economic reintegration
pathways.fcv_mediator: Poverty, coercive recruitment, exclusion, weak legitimacy, limited livelihood alternatives, and fragmented climate-security coordination
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate-resilient livelihood and dialogue initiatives may support reintegration and reduce vulnerability, but peace effects remain unmeasured
alternative_explanations: Recruitment and violence are principally shaped by armed-group coercion, political economy, security conditions, exclusion, and criminal incentives.
pathways.uncertainty: The admitted evidence supports a policy rationale and coordination platform, not causal effects on recruitment, reintegration, or peace.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-resilient livelihoods and dialogue may support reintegration where poverty and exclusion narrow alternatives, but peace outcomes are unproven.

pathways.climate_pressure: Higher temperatures and warming-enhanced evaporative demand during multi-year drought.
pathways.documented_impact: More severe agricultural drought and water stress.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Irrigation dependence, livelihood losses, high input costs and limited alternatives.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where household buffers are weak, these pressures could increase distress mobility or socioeconomic grievances; violence is not demonstrated.
geographies: strongest livelihood relevance in irrigated agricultural areas
pathways.uncertainty: No national causal estimate links drought exposure to migration or grievances.
pathways.compact_statement: Warming-enhanced drought can worsen irrigation stress, but household and FCV consequences depend heavily on water governance and economic alternatives. (World Weather Attribution)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought/climate variability.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced water availability and perceived worsening of water insecurity.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Allocation disputes, upstream/downstream differences, perceived injustice and competing sectoral claims.
pathways.possible_consequence: Local and regional water disputes may intensify when water insecurity and perception gaps are not managed.
alternative_explanations: agricultural policy and historical claims to water
pathways.uncertainty: Survey-based perception evidence cannot establish a unique climate causal effect.
resilience_factors: Social-learning platforms and conflict-sensitive stakeholder dialogue recommended by the study
pathways.compact_statement: In ZayandehRud, climate-related water stress is documented as one factor interacting with allocation and perceived injustice in local disputes - not as a stand-alone conflict cause. (Directory of Open Access Journals)

pathways.climate_pressure: Meteorological/hydrological drought.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced recharge and increased groundwater depletion during dry conditions.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unsustainable withdrawals and governance of access to groundwater.
pathways.possible_consequence: Persistently depleted aquifers could deepen livelihood insecurity and competition among water users.
pathways.uncertainty: National groundwater evidence does not itself measure conflict outcomes.
pathways.compact_statement: Drought can accelerate groundwater depletion, but extensive human withdrawal is the dominant documented depletion driver; FCV risk would therefore be mediated by access and governance rather than climate alone. (Nature)

pathways.climate_pressure: Multiple climate hazards requiring adaptation.
pathways.documented_impact: Need for finance, technology and institutional capacity.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Sanctions and restrictions on finance, technology and international cooperation.
pathways.possible_consequence: Adaptation planning or implementation may be slower, more expensive or narrower than otherwise possible.
pathways.uncertainty: The INDC is a government position and does not quantify sanctions' marginal adaptation effect.
pathways.compact_statement: Iran's own climate policy identifies sanctions and external restrictions as adaptation-capacity constraints, but the scale of their effect remains unevaluated. (Asia Pacific Energy Policy)

pathways.climate_pressure: Concurrent water and energy shortages.
pathways.documented_impact: Stress on economic activity and infrastructure.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict-related damage, sanctions, trade disruption, weak investment and import constraints.
pathways.possible_consequence: These conditions may reduce capacity to maintain, finance or upgrade water, energy and other climate-sensitive infrastructure.
pathways.uncertainty: No source in the verified set directly estimates lost adaptation investment.
resilience_factors: Institutional delivery arrangements insulated from direct financing channels
such as the World Bank/WHO COVID project model
pathways.compact_statement: Current FCV and economic disruption can plausibly narrow infrastructure-resilience capacity, although quantitative adaptation losses are unmeasured. (World Bank)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and water scarcity.
pathways.documented_impact: Pressure on wetlands and dependent livelihoods.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competing water use, weak inter-organizational collaboration and livelihood dependence.
pathways.possible_consequence: Degradation could increase livelihood stress; participatory and integrated basin management may reduce such risk.
pathways.uncertainty: Programme reporting cannot establish counterfactual effectiveness.
pathways.compact_statement: Participatory wetland management provides a plausible resilience mechanism, but independent evidence of durable conflict- or vulnerability-reduction effects is missing. (UNDP)

pathways.climate_pressure: Water scarcity/drought.
pathways.documented_impact: Agricultural and economic stress.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Inflation, income pressure, food-market conditions and unequal household buffers.
pathways.possible_consequence: Combined pressures could raise grievances or lower coping capacity, especially among poorer households.
pathways.uncertainty: No verified study demonstrates a complete climate -> poverty -> grievance causal chain nationally.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate stress can add to household economic pressure, but sanctions, prices and conflict remain independent and potentially dominant explanations. (World Bank)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, scarcity, ecosystem stress.
pathways.documented_impact: Need for more efficient production and basin coordination.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Institutional fragmentation and competing user interests.
pathways.possible_consequence: Multi-stakeholder institutions and livelihood alternatives may reduce vulnerability and provide channels for managing distributional tensions.
alternative_explanations: Programme participation may be uneven and gains may not persist after funding
pathways.uncertainty: No verified independent evaluation demonstrates peace outcomes.
pathways.compact_statement: Iran has observable institutional and community adaptation assets, but their contribution to durable peace or FCV reduction has not been independently demonstrated. (FAOHome)

pathways.climate_pressure: Rising temperatures, heat stress and potentially declining water availability.
pathways.documented_impact: Modelled reductions in wheat/crop productivity, labour productivity and household purchasing power.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Livelihood insecurity, food prices, poverty and unequal exposure.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where social protection, jobs and services are inadequate, these pressures could increase grievances or susceptibility to instability; violence is not an automatic consequence.
pathways.uncertainty: Economic and crop estimates are model scenarios, not observed conflict effects.
resilience_factors: climate-smart agriculture and shock-responsive social protection
pathways.compact_statement: Heat and water stress can erode agricultural and labour income and raise food costs; instability effects depend on markets, protection systems and governance.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, declining water availability and salinity interacting with other water-management pressures.
pathways.documented_impact: Rural livelihood loss and climate-associated displacement.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Rapid rural-urban mobility, inadequate urban services, limited employment, exclusion and harassment.
pathways.possible_consequence: Host-community/displaced-community tensions may increase where service capacity and economic opportunities are already weak.
affected_groups: Rural displaced households and urban host communities
alternative_explanations: urban labour-market weakness and pre-existing service deficits
pathways.uncertainty: Current displacement figures classify “climatic factors”; they do not isolate anthropogenic climate attribution.
resilience_factors: durable-solutions policy and recognition/support of climate-related mobility
pathways.compact_statement: Water-linked rural displacement can transfer stress to urban services and jobs, potentially increasing tensions where local capacity is inadequate. (The United Nations in Iraq)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and lower/less reliable water availability.
pathways.documented_impact: Tighter irrigation and groundwater access.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competition among user groups interacting with customary rights, centralized allocation, political affiliation and widespread weapons.
pathways.possible_consequence: Water disputes may escalate to violence in particular settings.
geographies: Strongest documented examples in southern governorates
affected_groups: Farmers and other local water users
pathways.uncertainty: No basis for a national claim that drought causes communal violence.
resilience_factors: customary dispute-resolution mechanisms and transparent water-sharing institutions
pathways.compact_statement: Scarcer water can increase opportunities for violent competition, but escalation depends strongly on governance, allocation systems, weapons and local political relations.

pathways.climate_pressure: Water scarcity and heat create greater value and competition around climate-sensitive resources.
pathways.documented_impact: Armed actors or affiliates have reportedly bypassed regulations, controlled water-intensive activities or obstructed improvements to public systems in selected localities.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Coercion, political influence, regulatory capture and illicit/semi-licit resource markets.
pathways.possible_consequence: Adaptation and equitable resource management can become less effective, increasing vulnerability to future climate stress.
affected_groups: pastoral/nomadic communities and users lacking political protection
alternative_explanations: market incentives and broader corruption independent of organized armed actors
pathways.uncertainty: Representativeness and prevalence are not established nationally.
resilience_factors: transparent allocation and conflict-sensitive resource governance
pathways.compact_statement: In some localities, armed-actor political economy can undermine resource regulation and public services, reducing climate-adaptation capacity.

pathways.climate_pressure: More constrained and variable water availability increases the salience of allocation decisions.
pathways.documented_impact: Local and inter-governorate disputes over centrally allocated water.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Perceived inequity, limited participation, unclear responsibility and political mobilization.
pathways.possible_consequence: Allocation grievances may fuel protests, inter-community disputes or political confrontation.
geographies: Local disputes nationwide in UNAMI synthesis
alternative_explanations: historical allocation rules and political competition
pathways.uncertainty: Climate change is not separable from the broader water-governance system.
pathways.compact_statement: Water-governance choices mediate whether physical scarcity translates into cooperation or grievance.

pathways.climate_pressure: Water and livelihood stress contributing to displacement.
pathways.documented_impact: Climate-displaced populations may fall outside consistent registration and assistance systems.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Perceived neglect, unequal assistance, political patronage and exploitation.
pathways.possible_consequence: Distrust, protest risk and erosion of social cohesion may increase.
alternative_explanations: poverty and broader politicization of social assistance
pathways.uncertainty: Institutional treatment varies geographically; local examples cannot establish a uniform national pattern.
pathways.compact_statement: Displacement becomes a larger FCV risk when support systems are unclear, unequal or politically manipulated.

pathways.climate_pressure: Heat, drought, floods and water stress increase demands on infrastructure and institutions.
pathways.documented_impact: Conflict-damaged or weak infrastructure, limited O&M and fragmented institutional capacity constrain reliable services.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Reconstruction burden, weak governance, corruption and prioritization of security.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate shocks may generate larger welfare and livelihood losses because preventive and adaptive systems are weaker.
geographies: conflict-affected and service-deficient areas particularly relevant
alternative_explanations: demographic growth and technical inefficiency independent of armed conflict
pathways.uncertainty: Relative contribution of past conflict versus other institutional drivers is rarely quantified.
resilience_factors: institutional coordination and systematic climate integration in reconstruction
pathways.compact_statement: FCV legacies can magnify climate vulnerability by weakening infrastructure, regulation and implementation capacity.

pathways.climate_pressure: Shared exposure to water scarcity and other climate risks.
pathways.documented_impact: Climate and natural-resource issues create common policy problems across communities and institutions.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Participation, dialogue, trust and locally accepted conflict-resolution mechanisms.
pathways.possible_consequence: Inclusive climate action may reduce escalation risks and strengthen social cohesion, although an effect on violence has not been quantitatively demonstrated.
geographies: Kirkuk example plus proposed national/subnational application
alternative_explanations: Existing social relations and political incentives may be more important than the climate forum/action itself
pathways.uncertainty: Evidence demonstrates a plausible entry point, not a measured peace impact.
resilience_factors: transparent allocation and locally legitimate dispute-resolution mechanisms
pathways.compact_statement: Climate action can support peace when it expands inclusive participation and legitimate resource-sharing mechanisms.

pathways.climate_pressure: Higher temperatures, declining precipitation and drought; projected dry-season water decline.
pathways.documented_impact: Water shortage, unreliable public supply and costly private alternatives.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unequal access, affordability, service failure, perceived unfairness and pre-existing group/resource competition.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where governance and distribution are already contested, additional water stress could worsen grievances or intergroup tensions.
geographies: strongest directly observed perception evidence in Beirut/Mount Lebanon and Beirut/Beqaa tension analysis
pathways.uncertainty: No source reviewed estimates an independent causal effect of climate change on violent conflict.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related water stress may aggravate tension through service failure and perceived inequity, but scarcity alone is not demonstrated to cause conflict. (World Bank)

pathways.climate_pressure: Heat, drought, rainfall variability.
pathways.documented_impact: Self-reported livelihood/financial losses, especially among rural and economically precarious respondents.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Informal employment dependence, reduced household income, competition over jobs/resources and existing economic crisis.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate-sensitive livelihood shocks could intensify competition and social tension where labour markets and household finances are already stressed.
affected_groups: displaced Syrians working in climate-sensitive sectors
pathways.uncertainty: Survey respondents attribute losses to climate; causal attribution was not independently tested.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-sensitive livelihood losses may compound job/resource competition, but political economy and labour-market conditions remain independent drivers.

pathways.climate_pressure: Heat, drought, floods and other climate hazards remain external pressures.
pathways.documented_impact: Crisis-constrained public finances and conflict-damaged lifeline infrastructure.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Reduced fiscal space, maintenance failures, implementation constraints and reconstruction burdens.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate hazards may produce larger service and welfare impacts because institutions and infrastructure have less capacity to absorb shocks.
geographies: especially conflict-damaged South/Nabatiyeh and service-stressed urban areas
alternative_explanations: Long-standing infrastructure underinvestment and governance weaknesses predate recent hostilities
pathways.uncertainty: Sources demonstrate damage and capacity constraints more directly than they measure resulting changes in climate vulnerability.
resilience_factors: protected maintenance finance and NAP integration
pathways.compact_statement: The strongest reverse pathway is that conflict and economic collapse weaken infrastructure and institutions needed to manage climate risk. (World Bank)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought/heat and water stress may affect agriculture and livelihoods.
pathways.documented_impact: High acute food insecurity in 2025.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict, displacement, loss of purchasing power and reduced humanitarian assistance.
pathways.possible_consequence: Additional climate-related production or income shocks could compound food insecurity and competition for scarce assistance or employment.
geographies: with rural and displacement-affected areas potentially more exposed
alternative_explanations: The cited 2025 evidence explicitly identifies conflict
displacement and reduced assistance - not climate - as the main immediate food-insecurity drivers
pathways.uncertainty: No reviewed source apportions the 2025 IPC burden quantitatively to climate.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate shocks could compound food insecurity, but the recent acute burden cannot be credibly described as climate-driven.

pathways.climate_pressure: Water scarcity/stress.
pathways.documented_impact: Water access can become a focus of local stress and mistrust.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Service-provider accountability, communication and intercommunity dialogue.
pathways.possible_consequence: Well-designed WASH investment may reduce tension while strengthening capacity to manage climate-related water stress.
geographies: candidate nationally only as a programme theory
alternative_explanations: Dialogue or wider political changes may have contributed independently
pathways.uncertainty: No counterfactual evaluation; the observed local experience does not establish general effectiveness.
pathways.compact_statement: WASH projects can potentially serve as peace-supporting adaptation when infrastructure and dialogue are deliberately combined.

pathways.climate_pressure: Increasing water scarcity/drought can add stress to already contested resources.
pathways.documented_impact: Local competition over springs/groundwater and high reliance on informal/private provision.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Ambiguous land/water rights, weak enforcement, fragmented governance and perceived unequal allocation.
pathways.possible_consequence: Under worsening scarcity, unresolved institutional disputes could become harder to mediate and reduce cooperation needed for adaptation.
alternative_explanations: sectarian politics and governance failures can generate conflict independent of climatic change
pathways.uncertainty: Climate's contribution to the specific Bcharreh-Denniyeh conflict is not isolated.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate stress may amplify contested water governance, but the causal core of documented local disputes is institutional and political as well as environmental.

pathways.climate_pressure: Water, heat or energy-related resilience needs can motivate geographically targeted investment.
pathways.documented_impact: Independent LHSP evaluation found that uneven infrastructure/solar support sometimes created intermunicipal grievances.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Beneficiary selection, geographic targeting, transparency and perceived distributive fairness.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate/adaptation investments could unintentionally intensify local grievances if benefits are visibly unequal and conflict sensitivity is weak.
geographies: Evaluation examples from Akkar and Bekaa
pathways.uncertainty: LHSP was not a climate-adaptation programme, so transfer to climate programming is an explicitly cautious inference.
pathways.compact_statement: Adaptation finance itself can become conflict-sensitive when allocation is unequal; evaluated Lebanese development experience provides a concrete warning.

pathways.climate_pressure: Exceptional extreme rainfall during Storm Daniel; anthropogenic influence is plausible but highly uncertain.
pathways.documented_impact: Flooding, dam failures, widespread physical damage, service disruption and displacement.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Infrastructure maintenance, institutional fragmentation, disaster planning, warning interpretation and coordination.
pathways.possible_consequence: Extreme rainfall can produce much larger human and economic losses where dam safety, maintenance, emergency governance and exposure are inadequate.
alternative_explanations: infrastructure quality and emergency decisions independently affected losses
pathways.uncertainty: The magnitude of anthropogenic influence on the rainfall is highly uncertain; no evidence apportions total losses quantitatively among rainfall, dams and governance.
pathways.compact_statement: Derna demonstrates compound disaster risk, not simple climate causation. (World Weather Attribution)

pathways.climate_pressure: Multiple climate hazards requiring coordinated preparation.
pathways.documented_impact: Weak/incomplete climate planning, degraded infrastructure and uneven emergency/recovery capacity.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Divided governance, institutional rivalry, weak coordination and conflict legacy.
pathways.possible_consequence: Fragmentation may reduce the maintenance, planning and coordination needed to prevent climate shocks from becoming disasters.
geographies: with strongest direct disaster evidence in eastern Libya
affected_groups: especially communities relying on fragile public infrastructure
alternative_explanations: procurement and sanctions/external constraints may also affect implementation
pathways.uncertainty: Direct evidence varies by institution; national institutional weakness does not imply identical municipal performance.
pathways.compact_statement: FCV-related institutional fragmentation is a documented constraint on climate resilience.

pathways.climate_pressure: Warming, drought, declining mean rainfall and rainfall variability.
pathways.documented_impact: Water stress, irrigation pressure and reduced rural livelihood resilience.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Water allocation, livelihood dependence, inequality, institutional legitimacy and market conditions.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where access is perceived as inequitable and livelihood alternatives are weak, worsening water stress could increase grievances or local tension, but violence is not an automatic result.
pathways.uncertainty: No strong national causal estimate links temperature or rainfall change to violent events.
pathways.compact_statement: Water scarcity becomes an FCV risk through governance and livelihoods, not through climate alone. (SIPRI)

pathways.climate_pressure: Chronic water stress potentially intensified by warming and reduced rainfall.
pathways.documented_impact: Dependence on shared, vulnerable water infrastructure.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Allocation rules, control of pumps/infrastructure, perceptions of fairness and mutual dependence.
pathways.possible_consequence: Scarcity and shared infrastructure may produce either contestation or cooperation depending on governance arrangements and incentives.
affected_groups: Communities and users dependent on shared water systems
alternative_explanations: infrastructure condition and local power relationships can drive both service interruptions and cooperation independently of climate
pathways.uncertainty: Duration and transferability of cooperative arrangements are not evaluated.
resilience_factors: credible allocation procedures and shared maintenance agreements
pathways.compact_statement: Water dependence is not intrinsically conflictual; institutions determine whether it divides or connects communities. (SIPRI)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, heat and other climate stressors.
pathways.documented_impact: Livelihood disruption among some migrants and climate-sensitive communities.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict, income loss, migration policy, protection conditions, routes, markets and household resources.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate shocks may contribute to decisions to move, but available Libyan evidence does not establish them as a dominant or sufficient cause of migration.
pathways.uncertainty: The 25% climate-shock figure is sample-based association, not causal attribution.
resilience_factors: service inclusion and safe mobility options
pathways.compact_statement: Climate may be one migration stressor, but Libya's mobility dynamics remain strongly multi-causal. (SIPRI)

pathways.climate_pressure: Major flood/disaster event.
pathways.documented_impact: Humanitarian, service and reconstruction needs after Derna.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competing authorities, checkpoints, securitized access, institutional rivalry and social/legal status.
pathways.possible_consequence: Fragmented security governance can delay aid and make recovery less inclusive, particularly for groups with weak protection or documentation.
alternative_explanations: scale of destruction and administrative capacity also constrained response
pathways.uncertainty: Available evidence is predominantly qualitative regarding the magnitude of delay/exclusion.
resilience_factors: transparent reconstruction processes and status-neutral service provision
pathways.compact_statement: Political-security fragmentation affected who could deliver and receive recovery assistance. (SIPRI)

pathways.climate_pressure: Flooding, heat, drought and water stress.
pathways.documented_impact: WASH, health and education disruption; unreliable services.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Pre-existing public-service weakness, displacement status, poverty, documentation and gender/age-related vulnerability.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate shocks may create larger welfare losses for people already facing weak services or barriers to assistance.
geographies: Strongest direct evidence in eastern flood zones
structural service weakness is national with regional differences
alternative_explanations: discrimination and chronic service underinvestment create vulnerability independently of climate
pathways.uncertainty: Differentiated quantitative outcome data are limited.
resilience_factors: resilient WASH/health systems and protection-sensitive disaster planning
pathways.compact_statement: Climate exposure intersects with pre-existing service and protection inequalities.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, heat, water scarcity and disaster risk.
pathways.documented_impact: Recognition of planning, infrastructure and technical-capacity deficits.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Institutional coordination, financing, local implementation capacity and shared-resource governance.
pathways.possible_consequence: The new drought and water strategies and local water/DRR investments could strengthen resilience and create practical cooperation incentives if implementation becomes sustained and inclusive.
alternative_explanations: Strategies may remain underfunded or fragmented
infrastructure investments may fail without maintenance and governance reform
pathways.uncertainty: Independent outcome evidence for 2025-2026 initiatives is not yet available.
pathways.compact_statement: Libya has emerging resilience assets, but implementation rather than policy adoption is the critical test. (UNDP)

pathways.climate_pressure: Positive temperature anomalies and/or negative precipitation anomalies.
pathways.documented_impact: Changes in maize production and household food-security status.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Household food insecurity and livelihood stress.
pathways.possible_consequence: Higher subsequent incidence of several ACLED conflict-event categories, conditional on the study model.
pathways.uncertainty: Structural-equation mediation is compatible with the pathway but does not establish event-level climate causality. (Frontiers)
pathways.compact_statement: Climate anomalies may contribute to conflict risk through crop and food-security effects, but the observed relationship is mediated and non-deterministic.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, inadequate rain, late or variable rainy seasons.
pathways.documented_impact: Changes in pasture/water availability and livestock movement.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Rules governing access to land, water and seasonal routes; interaction among farmers and pastoral groups.
pathways.possible_consequence: Local disputes or violence may become more likely where mobility intersects poorly governed or contested access.
geographies: Inner Niger Delta and pastoral corridors
pathways.uncertainty: Mobility is itself an adaptation strategy and must not be characterized as inherently destabilizing. (SIPRI)
pathways.compact_statement: Rainfall stress can alter pastoral mobility, but whether this becomes conflict depends heavily on institutions and access governance.

pathways.climate_pressure: Heavy precipitation and floods.
pathways.documented_impact: Crop losses, erosion and potential infrastructure damage; FAO specifically reported 2024 flood-related crop losses.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Food prices, market access, household asset depletion and uneven assistance.
pathways.possible_consequence: Higher vulnerability, displacement or local grievances may result where recovery and markets are weak.
pathways.uncertainty: No retained source directly demonstrates that specific Mali floods caused subsequent violence.
pathways.compact_statement: Flood losses can deepen food and livelihood stress, but an FCV consequence requires additional social and institutional mediators. (World Bank)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, heat and rainfall-related livelihood stress.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced or more uncertain natural-resource-based livelihood options.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Poverty, unemployment, absence of alternatives, grievances and armed-group economic incentives.
pathways.possible_consequence: Recruitment vulnerability may increase for some individuals.
geographies: Principally northern and central Mali in the retained qualitative evidence
pathways.uncertainty: SIPRI explicitly describes recruitment as complex and the study as a plausibility probe. (SIPRI)
pathways.compact_statement: Climate stress may narrow livelihoods and thereby enlarge recruitment opportunities, but it is one contributor among many.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought/rainfall variability remains the environmental stressor to which livelihood systems need to adapt.
pathways.documented_impact: Conflict disrupted irrigation and livestock markets and pushed some herds southward.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Insecurity, market closure and constrained movement.
pathways.possible_consequence: Households may lose access to otherwise effective drought-coping options and face greater resource pressure elsewhere.
pathways.uncertainty: Much of the documented mechanism comes from earlier conflict periods.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict can disable livelihood strategies that would otherwise help households adapt to climatic variability. (SIPRI)

pathways.climate_pressure: Concurrent heat, drought, flood or food-system stress.
pathways.documented_impact: Insecurity, blockades, movement restrictions and fuel constraints interrupt health, nutrition, education and humanitarian delivery.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Physical access and operational continuity.
pathways.possible_consequence: Climate- and food-shock recovery may be slower and mortality/welfare risks higher where assistance cannot reach populations.
pathways.uncertainty: Current humanitarian reports rarely isolate the incremental effect on *climate adaptation* as such.
pathways.compact_statement: Insecurity can turn an environmental shock into a more severe humanitarian event by constraining the services needed for coping and recovery. (UNICEF)

pathways.climate_pressure: Increasing heat, variable rainfall, drought/flood exposure.
pathways.documented_impact: Growing pressure on natural-resource management and demand for coordinated adaptation.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Weak institutional coordination, limited budgets, unequal access and weak local governance.
pathways.possible_consequence: Adaptation gaps and perceived unfairness may aggravate grievances or disputes.
geographies: with greater constraints in conflict-prone localities
pathways.uncertainty: Institutional weakness is independently consequential and should not be relabelled as a climate effect.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate pressures place additional demands on already constrained institutions; weak or unequal responses can in turn worsen both vulnerability and grievance risk. (World Bank)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought and rainfall variability.
pathways.documented_impact: Need for mobility, livelihood adjustment and collective natural-resource management.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Local legitimacy, dispute resolution, collective decision-making and grievance handling.
pathways.possible_consequence: Stronger locally legitimate institutions may reduce the chance that resource pressure escalates into conflict while enabling adaptation.
geographies: specific evidence should not be generalized to all Mali
alternative_explanations: Some local institutions can also reproduce exclusion or unequal access
pathways.uncertainty: Strong independent evidence on peace outcomes from climate/resource institutions remains limited.
pathways.compact_statement: Locally legitimate coping and resource-governance institutions are plausible peace-supporting capacities, but their distributional and conflict effects require evaluation.

pathways.climate_pressure: Rising temperature, longer dry spells and inadequate water.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced rain-fed agricultural performance and livelihood security.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Debt, landlessness risk, rising input costs, declining credit, poverty and an existing armed-conflict environment.
pathways.possible_consequence: These combined pressures may influence grievances and household/community relationships with armed resistance actors; the evidence does not show climate as an independent cause of recruitment or violence.
geographies: Magway and lower Sagaing Dry Zone
pathways.uncertainty: SIPRI/NUPI directly presents the chain but does not estimate the independent effect of climate stress. (SIPRI6)
resilience_factors: climate information and local conflict-sensitive agricultural support
pathways.compact_statement: Dry Zone climate stress can worsen farm hardship, but any effect on conflict dynamics is mediated through finance, livelihoods and pre-existing political violence.

pathways.climate_pressure: Cyclone, extreme rain and flooding.
pathways.documented_impact: Damage to shelter, WASH, infrastructure, livelihoods and services.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Humanitarian-access restrictions, insecurity, territorial contestation and blocked transport.
pathways.possible_consequence: Slower relief and recovery can prolong unmet needs and deepen vulnerability.
affected_groups: Rohingya and ethnic Rakhine populations among others
alternative_explanations: terrain and the scale of the disaster
pathways.uncertainty: Evidence is strong for specific events but cannot be assumed uniform across Myanmar. (Doctors Without Borders4)
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict and access restrictions have demonstrably reduced the reach of climate-disaster response in specific Myanmar settings.

pathways.climate_pressure: Floods, cyclones and heavy rain.
pathways.documented_impact: Temporary relocation, camp damage, WASH shortages and mine/ERW uncertainty.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Prior conflict displacement and settlement in vulnerable locations.
pathways.possible_consequence: People displaced by conflict may face repeated displacement and accumulating asset/service losses during climatic disasters.
alternative_explanations: poor settlement siting and inadequate infrastructure can generate vulnerability independently of conflict
pathways.uncertainty: National IDP figures do not indicate how many IDPs are directly climate-exposed. (World Bank5)
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict displacement can turn a climatic shock into repeated displacement and additional protection risk.

pathways.climate_pressure: Floods, cyclones, heat and other weather extremes.
pathways.documented_impact: Need to evacuate, migrate or relocate.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict, mobility restrictions, insecurity and contested territory.
pathways.possible_consequence: Households unable to move safely may remain in highly exposed areas or lose access to livelihoods and assistance.
geographies: source emphasizes displaced and minority populations
pathways.uncertainty: Limited quantitative evidence identifies the relative contribution of each mobility constraint. (SIPRI6)
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict-related mobility constraints can reduce people's ability to use migration or evacuation as climate coping strategies.

pathways.climate_pressure: Cyclones and other disasters.
pathways.documented_impact: Large relief and governance needs.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Competing authorities' attempts to demonstrate governing capacity and legitimacy.
pathways.possible_consequence: Disaster response may reshape grievances and perceived authority without the hazard itself causing renewed conflict.
affected_groups: Disaster-affected communities including marginalized Rohingya populations
institutions: KNU and other local governance actors
pathways.uncertainty: Political effects vary strongly by actor and locality. (SIPRI6)
pathways.compact_statement: In post-coup Myanmar, disaster and climate action can become part of struggles over authority rather than merely technical adaptation.

pathways.climate_pressure: Climate hazards interacting with seasonal farming needs.
pathways.documented_impact: Threats to harvest and food security.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed confrontation preventing normal agricultural activity.
pathways.possible_consequence: Negotiated agricultural access may create a temporary peace-supporting window.
alternative_explanations: military or political rather than climate-specific
pathways.uncertainty: No evidence of durable peace effects. (SIPRI6)
pathways.compact_statement: Locally mediated harvest access can support food security and temporary de-escalation, but it is not evidence that adaptation causes peace.

pathways.climate_pressure: Multi-hazard climate risk requiring information, planning and coordinated adaptation.
pathways.documented_impact: High demand for climate information, agricultural adaptation and disaster preparedness.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Fragmented territorial control, contested institutions and politicization of environmental action.
pathways.possible_consequence: National adaptation plans and services may have uneven territorial reach and may be interpreted through political competition.
alternative_explanations: Long-standing administrative capacity and finance constraints predate the coup
pathways.uncertainty: No national post-2021 implementation audit was located.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict and divided authority appear to make adaptation capacity territorially uneven and politically contested.

pathways.climate_pressure: Flood, drought and livelihood shocks.
pathways.documented_impact: Local infrastructure, food and service needs.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Weak/contested state reach and security conditions.
pathways.possible_consequence: Community assets, grassroots institutions and third-party implementation may sustain limited resilience where conventional public delivery is constrained.
geographies: Karen areas and conflict-affected World Bank project locations
alternative_explanations: Selection toward more stable areas may itself explain better delivery
pathways.uncertainty: Programme outputs and institutional activity are not evidence of durable resilience or peace outcomes. (World Food Programme3)
pathways.compact_statement: Alternative delivery institutions can bridge some resilience gaps, but effectiveness and equity require independent evaluation.

pathways.climate_pressure: Tropical cyclones, intense rainfall and flooding.
pathways.documented_impact: Crop/livelihood losses and damage to schools, health facilities and water infrastructure.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Food access, market access, displacement, service scarcity and coping-capacity erosion.
pathways.possible_consequence: Where conflict, poverty or displacement already constrain households, repeated disaster losses could deepen humanitarian dependence and local competition, but violence is not an automatic outcome.
geographies: current 2026 flood areas include Gaza/Sofala and storm-affected Inhambane
alternative_explanations: market isolation and pre-existing service shortages
pathways.uncertainty: No identified national study estimates how much conflict or fragility risk changes because of cyclone exposure alone.
pathways.compact_statement: Cyclone/flood losses can worsen food and service stress through livelihoods, markets and displacement, especially where non-climate fragilities are already severe.

pathways.climate_pressure: Heat, drought and irregular rainfall.
pathways.documented_impact: Local pressure on arable land, fisheries and food availability.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Food insecurity, poverty, youth unemployment and competition over resources.
pathways.possible_consequence: These conditions may increase incentives for contentious or illicit livelihood strategies and disputes, but the Mecufi evidence does not demonstrate that climate stress causes violent recruitment or violence.
geographies: Mecufi District only for the complete pathway
pathways.uncertainty: No counterfactual and no national generalisability.
pathways.compact_statement: In Mecufi, climate-related livelihood stress is plausibly linked to competition through food insecurity and socioeconomic inequality rather than directly to violence.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, cyclone and flood damage affecting productive land.
pathways.documented_impact: Reduced or degraded cultivable land in the local assessment.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict displacement, rapid land occupation, unequal access and land governance.
pathways.possible_consequence: Disputes between hosts, displaced households or politically/economically stronger and weaker groups could intensify.
affected_groups: ethnic groups with unequal bargaining power
pathways.uncertainty: Future escalation is explicitly conditional.
pathways.compact_statement: In Mecufi, climate-related land pressure and conflict-driven displacement can interact through land access and governance.

pathways.climate_pressure: Background cyclone, flood and coastal-erosion risk.
pathways.documented_impact: Local mangroves serve as a protective ecological asset.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Insurgency-driven displacement, livelihood loss and pressure on services/natural resources.
pathways.possible_consequence: Unsustainable extraction, including mangrove cutting for salt production, may weaken natural buffering capacity and increase future hazard vulnerability.
pathways.uncertainty: Magnitude of mangrove loss attributable specifically to conflict displacement is not quantified.
resilience_factors: mangrove protection/restoration and conflict-sensitive resource governance
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict-related livelihood and displacement pressures can degrade natural assets that otherwise buffer climate hazards.

pathways.climate_pressure: Multiple recurring hazards require functioning health, education, WASH, transport and local governance.
pathways.documented_impact: Northern violence has caused displacement, infrastructure destruction and school closures.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Insecurity, restricted mobility, damaged infrastructure, weakened services and overstretched humanitarian capacity.
pathways.possible_consequence: Hazard preparedness, recovery and long-term adaptation may be slower or less equitable in conflict-affected districts.
pathways.uncertainty: Few evaluations directly measure adaptation outcomes in conflict versus non-conflict districts.
resilience_factors: protected service delivery and anticipatory financing
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict can make climate adaptation harder by disrupting the institutions, services and mobility on which preparedness and recovery depend.

pathways.climate_pressure: Cyclones and flooding.
pathways.documented_impact: Damage, poor sanitation and communicable-disease risks.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Weak public-health/adaptation intervention, rumours and distrust of authorities.
pathways.possible_consequence: The Mecufi assessment reports a pathway toward insecurity, protest or social unrest where disease outbreaks are interpreted through mistrust.
alternative_explanations: disease dynamics unrelated to climate and political grievances
pathways.uncertainty: No incidence/risk effect size is provided.
resilience_factors: responsive health services and community participation
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related disaster disruption may become politically salient through public-health failures and mistrust rather than through climate exposure alone.

pathways.climate_pressure: Multi-hazard climate exposure.
pathways.documented_impact: Large adaptation requirements and recurring livelihood/infrastructure losses.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Fiscal constraints, weak coordination, incomplete technical capacity and unequal service delivery.
pathways.possible_consequence: Uneven implementation could leave poorer or conflict-affected communities with lower resilience, potentially reinforcing existing inequalities and grievances.
affected_groups: Poor households and poorly served districts
pathways.uncertainty: No evidence found demonstrating that adaptation funding gaps themselves cause instability.
pathways.compact_statement: Implementation capacity is a mediator of climate vulnerability, but its relationship to fragility requires further empirical testing.

pathways.climate_pressure: Locally identified drought, flood, cyclone and coastal pressures.
pathways.documented_impact: Shared analysis of climate-security risks by authorities, communities and peacebuilders.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Trust, participation, conflict mediation, early warning and locally legitimate decision-making.
pathways.possible_consequence: These capacities could reduce escalation and improve conflict-sensitive adaptation, although effectiveness has not yet been demonstrated.
geographies: Mecufi and selected Cabo Delgado communities
alternative_explanations: Wider security conditions and state policy may overwhelm local peacebuilding capacities
pathways.uncertainty: GPPAC explicitly states that immediate impacts of its assessment were hard to assess.
pathways.compact_statement: Mozambique has locally documented peace-supporting capacities, but evidence of their effect on climate-FCV outcomes remains limited.

pathways.climate_pressure: Rainfall variability, dry spells and rising temperatures.
pathways.documented_impact: Pressure on rainfed and pastoral livelihood strategies and adaptation choices.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Cultivation encroachment, livestock mobility, access to wells/pasture, demographic pressure and weak/unequal land-governance implementation.
pathways.possible_consequence: Localized disputes or violence between resource users may become more likely where institutions fail to manage competing access.
geographies: particularly pastoral/agropastoral contexts in Tahoua and Tillabéri
pathways.uncertainty: No current national causal estimate.
resilience_factors: protected mobility corridors and equitable water/pasture rules
pathways.compact_statement: Climate stress can alter livelihood strategies, but whether this becomes conflict depends strongly on land institutions, access rules and political-economic conditions. (ResearchGate)

pathways.climate_pressure: Seasonal/intense flooding.
pathways.documented_impact: Livelihood losses; 2025 flooding affected livelihoods of about 474,000 people.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Existing conflict exposure, displacement and restricted humanitarian access.
pathways.possible_consequence: Flood-affected conflict zones may face deeper food-security or recovery problems than equally flooded but accessible areas.
geographies: with special relevance to conflict-affected areas
pathways.uncertainty: No counterfactual estimate of the added effect of conflict on flood recovery.
pathways.compact_statement: Flood risk and insecurity can compound because conflict changes access to assistance and recovery capacity rather than because flooding itself causes violence. (FAOHome)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, variable rainfall, heat.
pathways.documented_impact: Changing pastoral mobility and water/pasture strategies.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Agricultural encroachment, corridor obstruction, well access, unequal legal representation and weak Rural Code enforcement.
pathways.possible_consequence: Conflict risk may increase at specific encounter points between mobile herders and cultivators.
pathways.uncertainty: Present-day magnitude and geographic distribution are not established.
resilience_factors: Legally protected corridors and credible local mediation
pathways.compact_statement: Water or pasture scarcity is not sufficient to produce violence; conflict emerges through contested access and governance. (ResearchGate)

pathways.climate_pressure: Background rainfall variability and agricultural climate dependence.
pathways.documented_impact: Civil insecurity restricted access to fields and caused localized production shortfalls in Tillabéri and Diffa in 2025.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Armed insecurity and mobility restrictions.
pathways.possible_consequence: Households with reduced farm access may possess less income, stocks and flexibility to absorb subsequent drought/flood shocks.
pathways.uncertainty: Household-level resilience losses are not quantified.
pathways.compact_statement: Current evidence more clearly demonstrates insecurity constraining climate-sensitive livelihoods than climate shocks directly causing insecurity. (FAOHome)

pathways.climate_pressure: Floods, droughts and other covariate shocks remain background risks.
pathways.documented_impact: Displacement and insecurity increase needs while health, education and other services face access and funding constraints.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Forced displacement, insecure roads/territories, concentrated urban demand and resource constraints.
pathways.possible_consequence: Reduced baseline service capacity may make subsequent climate emergencies harder to absorb.
alternative_explanations: rapid population growth and fiscal constraints
pathways.uncertainty: Direct climate-adaptation outcome evaluation is absent.
pathways.compact_statement: FCV can erode the service base on which effective disaster response and adaptation depend.

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought/rainfall uncertainty.
pathways.documented_impact: Farmers and pastoralists diversify, change mobility, intensify agriculture, build wells or monetize previously shared resources.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unequal capital, tenure, access and institutional representation.
pathways.possible_consequence: Some adaptation choices may shift costs or exclude other groups, creating grievances or disputes.
geographies: Local rural Niger in older field evidence
alternative_explanations: Commercialization and demographic growth independent of climate
pathways.uncertainty: Contemporary prevalence is unknown.
resilience_factors: participatory governance and conflict-sensitive adaptation design
pathways.compact_statement: An adaptation intervention should not be assumed peace-positive merely because it reduces climate exposure. (ResearchGate)

pathways.climate_pressure: Drought, flood, rainfall variability.
pathways.documented_impact: Niger's policies call for improved forecasting, early warning and locally accessible climate services; UNICEF reports anticipatory flood preparation.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Timeliness and inclusiveness of information/assistance, local capacity and financing.
pathways.possible_consequence: Earlier action could reduce livelihood losses and pressure on crisis-response systems, provided services reach insecure and marginalized communities.
alternative_explanations: market access and infrastructure may dominate household outcomes
pathways.uncertainty: Current programme descriptions do not establish avoided losses or peace effects.
pathways.compact_statement: Early warning is a plausible resilience mechanism, but current evidence in this packet mostly demonstrates capacity and outputs rather than impacts.

pathways.climate_pressure: Climate variability raises the value of flexible access to land, pasture and water.
pathways.documented_impact: Resource-access disputes occur where mobility and cultivation overlap.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Quality and legitimacy of local dispute-resolution institutions.
pathways.possible_consequence: Inclusive land commissions and customary/formal mediation may reduce escalation.
geographies: broader mechanisms referenced in the 2026 World Bank diagnostic
alternative_explanations: local power relations and enforcement capacity
pathways.uncertainty: Louma finding is old and one-community evidence.
resilience_factors: Representation of both livelihood groups and women
pathways.compact_statement: Peace-supporting capacity appears to depend less on resource abundance alone than on legitimate institutions governing access and disputes. (ResearchGate) ---

pathways.climate_pressure: Higher temperatures, drought risk and rainfall variability in northern savanna areas.
pathways.documented_impact: Pressure on pastoral livelihoods/grazing resources and changing mobility patterns.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Movement into farming zones; land/resource access; weak land/livestock governance; small-arms and wider political/social conditions.
pathways.possible_consequence: Farmer-herder disputes may become more difficult to manage and, where governance and security conditions permit escalation, may become violent.
pathways.uncertainty: Climate is neither necessary nor sufficient for violence; spatial evidence directly cautions against a monotonic climate-conflict relationship.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate stress may shape pastoral mobility, but governance and other conflict drivers determine whether mobility becomes violent competition.

pathways.climate_pressure: Northern livelihood and grazing stress.
pathways.documented_impact: Seasonal or longer-distance pastoral movement toward less climate-exposed areas.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Destination-area competition and institutions governing access.
pathways.possible_consequence: Conflict risk may rise in places where climate impacts are less acute if those areas receive mobile livelihood groups and resource governance is weak.
pathways.uncertainty: One spatial study cannot establish a national law-like relationship.
pathways.compact_statement: The geographic location of climate stress and the location of violence can diverge because mobility transfers pressures across space. (SIPRI2)

pathways.climate_pressure: Severe rainfall/flood events; anthropogenic climate attribution not established for the specific 2024 event evidence.
pathways.documented_impact: Flood exposure affecting more than 480,000 people in the Northeast in 2024.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Existing violence, insecurity and large-scale displacement.
pathways.possible_consequence: Flood shocks can impose greater shelter, livelihood, health and service burdens on already displaced/conflict-affected communities.
pathways.uncertainty: Co-occurrence establishes compounding vulnerability, not a climate -> conflict causal pathway.
resilience_factors: inclusion of displaced groups in services and development systems
pathways.compact_statement: Floods can compound humanitarian needs where conflict has already displaced populations and weakened livelihoods. (UNHCR10)

pathways.climate_pressure: Background climate stress in the Lake Chad livelihood system.
pathways.documented_impact: Fishers and pastoralists require access to water, fisheries and pasture.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Military/security restrictions, forced evacuation, movement limitations and market closures.
pathways.possible_consequence: Conflict measures can reduce coping options and increase vulnerability to subsequent climate stress.
pathways.uncertainty: Evidence is narrow and older; national generalization is inappropriate.
resilience_factors: livelihood-sensitive security planning and maintaining safe access to productive resources where feasible
pathways.compact_statement: FCV can increase climate vulnerability by restricting access to the resources on which coping livelihoods depend.

pathways.climate_pressure: Not required as the proximate trigger; climate shocks can coexist in the wider food system.
pathways.documented_impact: Violence displaces people from farmland and obstructs humanitarian supply routes.
pathways.fcv_mediator: attacks, illegal checkpoints, partial inaccessibility and displacement.
pathways.possible_consequence: Reduced assistance and market/land access can deepen hunger and reduce households' capacity to withstand additional shocks, including climate shocks.
pathways.uncertainty: Current IPC evidence does not identify climate as a proximate malnutrition driver.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict demonstrably constrains food-assistance delivery; its effect on climate resilience is plausible but not separately quantified. (World Food Programme8)

pathways.climate_pressure: Multiple hazards across very different ecological regions.
pathways.documented_impact: Need for cross-sector, multi-level adaptation.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Weak coordination, limited local-government involvement, inadequate finance/skills and weak M&E.
pathways.possible_consequence: Adaptation may be delayed, fragmented or uneven, potentially leaving vulnerable/conflict-affected areas with lower resilience.
pathways.uncertainty: No evidence reviewed shows these adaptation gaps directly producing violence.
